sections.heading: The coast route in three days
body: A three-day split by OSRM routing is Brisbane to Coffs Harbour about 383 km, Coffs Harbour to Newcastle about 385 km, and Newcastle to Sydney about 161 km. Driving into each town centre adds distance, so these legs add up to more than the through route: Brisbane to Tweed Heads about 102 km (1 h 20 min), Tweed Heads to Ballina about 87 km (1 h 7 min), Ballina to Grafton about 136 km (1 h 44 min), Grafton to Coffs Harbour about 85 km (1 h 7 min), Coffs Harbour to Port Macquarie about 154 km (1 h 55 min), Port Macquarie to Taree about 80 km (1 h 4 min), Taree to Newcastle about 172 km (2 h 14 min) and Newcastle to Sydney about 161 km (2 h 12 min).

For night one, Banana Coast Caravan Park and Reflections Coffs Harbour Holiday Park are both on the Pacific Highway at Coffs Harbour. Check availability and prices with the park. Port Macquarie is the other natural break, about 537 km from Brisbane. The AussieCamps data lists Diamond Head, Indian Head and Kylies Beach campgrounds in Crowdy Bay National Park, near Port Macquarie, and Mungo Brush, Bombah Point and other Myall Lakes campgrounds near Bulahdelah, all national park campgrounds with a park entry fee listed.
tips: Coffs Harbour about 383 km from Brisbane
National park campgrounds list a park entry fee

sections.heading: The New England Highway in three days
body: Inland, a three-day split is Brisbane to Tenterfield about 266 km, Tenterfield to Tamworth about 300 km, and Tamworth to Sydney about 407 km. By OSRM the legs are Brisbane to Warwick about 156 km (2 h 11 min), Warwick to Tenterfield about 110 km (1 h 28 min), Tenterfield to Glen Innes about 92 km (1 h 12 min), Glen Innes to Armidale about 97 km (1 h 23 min), Armidale to Tamworth about 111 km (1 h 36 min), Tamworth to Scone about 132 km (1 h 50 min), Scone to Singleton about 74 km (1 h 8 min) and Singleton to Sydney about 201 km (2 h 34 min).

Tenterfield has Tenterfield Lodge Caravan Park and a second park on Rouse Street, and Bald Rock campground in Bald Rock National Park is a short drive away. Armidale has Armidale Tourist Park and BIG4 Armidale Highlander Van Village, and Tamworth has Austin Tourist Park and Paradise Tourist Park. Near Cunninghams Gap, the AussieCamps data lists Spicers Gap, Manna Gum and Poplar Flat camping areas in Main Range National Park. Wikipedia says the highway can see frost and snow in winter between the Moonbi Ranges and Stanthorpe, so check Live Traffic NSW in winter.
tips: Winter frost and snow possible on the highlands

sections.heading: Fuel and services
body: The sources checked list no fuel gap on either route, because both pass through a town roughly every hour. The longer gaps between towns are Taree to Newcastle at about 172 km and Coffs Harbour to Port Macquarie at about 154 km on the coast, and Tamworth to Scone at about 132 km on the New England. Fill up at the larger town before a long leg, since fuel and opening hours at each smaller town could not be confirmed.

Rest areas in the AussieCamps data on the coast include Macksville Lions Park near Nambucca Heads and Four Mile Hill Rest Area in the Mid-Coast, both listing toilets, picnic tables and a heavy vehicle area. Queensland says rest areas are not camping sites and allows up to 20 hours unless a sign says otherwise. In New South Wales the official advice conflicts, so read the sign. The rest area guide has the details.
tips: Longest gaps: 172 km coast, 132 km inland
Rest areas are for a break, not a bed

sections.heading: Road conditions, tolls and flood closures
body: Check Live Traffic NSW (livetraffic.com, 132 701) and QLDTraffic. The Pacific Highway closed between Ballina and Grafton in the March 2022 floods and heavy vehicles were detoured inland, so after heavy rain check before you leave and use the New England Highway as the fallback. No current closure was listed in the sources checked on 21 October 2026. Roadworks include an overtaking lane south of Tamworth due in late March 2027.

Both ends have tolls. NSW says that if you travel on a toll road without an account or pass you have 72 hours to pay or open an account, and Service NSW lists a casual pass for visitors that covers up to 30 days. Linkt says a Queensland road pass can cover trips made up to 5 days ago on all toll roads in Queensland. Which toll roads you meet depends on your route into each city, so check Linkt and Transport for NSW. The Pacific Highway north of Hexham has no tolls.
tips: Floods can close the Pacific Highway

sections.heading: Border rules between Queensland and New South Wales
body: The main rule at this border is about fire ants, not fruit fly. NSW DPIRD says anyone moving fire ant carriers out of the red, orange or yellow zones on its map must comply with the current Biosecurity (Fire Ant) Emergency Order, and carriers include soil, mulch, compost, manure, hay, green waste, pallets, packaging, containers and heavy vehicles. Queensland lists soil, manure, hay, straw, plants and their pots, mulch and sawdust. NSW runs roadside checks across the north of the state, and vehicles moving materials in breach are directed to return to Queensland. Caravans and camping gear are not on those lists, but the rules are written for carrier materials, so check NSW DPIRD on 1800 680 244 or Biosecurity Queensland on 13 25 23 about anything you carry. A fire ant nest was also found in Sydney's inner west in October 2026, so check NSW DPIRD for the control order.

Plant rules apply too. The Interstate Quarantine site says the whole of Queensland is a biosecurity zone for bananas, grape plants, mangoes and sugarcane, and to not take any plants, soil or items that have been in contact with these plants into Queensland. It also says the NSW Banana Bunchy Top Virus Control Zone covers the Tweed, Lismore, Ballina and Byron areas, which the Pacific route crosses, and to not move banana plants, bells, pseudo stems or leaves out of it. No Queensland and NSW fruit rule for travellers turned up in the sources checked. The interstate biosecurity guide covers the rest.
tips: Fire ants: soil, mulch, hay and plants
Banana plants must not leave the Tweed to Byron zone
Check NSW DPIRD and Biosecurity Queensland

sections.heading: Dump points and the clock change
body: The AussieCamps data lists dump points on the coast at Coffs Harbour Moonee Street Tourist Park (no washout tap listed), Diamond Waters Caravan Park at Dunbogan (washout tap listed) and Soldiers Point Big4 at Port Stephens (washout tap listed). On the inland route it lists Maitland Visitor Information Centre (washout tap listed), about 10 km off the line. That is what the data covers, not every dump point on the road, so check the dump points guide.

Queensland does not use daylight saving, and New South Wales does: NSW says it runs from Sunday 4 October 2026 to Sunday 4 April 2027, so between those dates New South Wales is one hour ahead of Queensland. Plan check-in times and campground gate hours on the New South Wales side with that hour in mind.
tips: Dunbogan and Port Stephens list a washout tap
NSW is one hour ahead until 4 April 2027

body: Build the drive as a trip in AussieCamps: add the overnight stops in order and it shows the distance and drive time between each, with a forecast for the day you plan to arrive at each stop. AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and a place page carries the facilities those sources publish.

Stored place details, saved places and guides work with no signal. Map tiles, routing, weather and photos need a connection, so open the trip while you are in coverage. AussieCamps runs on iPhone only, and it is free to download, with in-app purchases.
tips: Add each night as a stop
Mind the clock change at the border

faq: How long does it take to drive from Brisbane to Sydney?

About 10 h 52 min on the Pacific Motorway and Pacific Highway, about 907 km, or about 13 h 8 min on the New England Highway, about 970 km, by OSRM routing without stops. Most people split it over two or three days.
Is the Pacific Highway between Brisbane and Sydney all four lanes?

Yes. An Australian Government infrastructure listing says the full 657 km between Hexham and the Queensland border has been open as a four-lane divided road since 17 December 2020. The New England Highway is mostly single carriageway with overtaking lanes.
Are there tolls between Brisbane and Sydney?

Yes at both ends. Brisbane and Sydney have tolled motorways, and NSW says you have 72 hours to pay or open an account if you drive a Sydney toll road without a pass. Linkt says a Queensland road pass can cover trips made up to 5 days ago. Check which toll roads your route into each city uses.
Can I take soil, mulch or plants across the Queensland and New South Wales border?

Be careful. Fire ant rules in both states restrict carrier materials such as soil, mulch, hay, manure and plants, and NSW runs roadside checks across the north of the state. Check NSW DPIRD on 1800 680 244 or Biosecurity Queensland on 13 25 23 about anything you are carrying.

melbourne-to-brisbane-drive.title: Melbourne to Brisbane Drive 2026: Inland Newell Highway, Stops and Campsites
melbourne-to-brisbane-drive.description: Melbourne to Brisbane is about 1,675 km and 22 hours on the inland Newell Highway, or about 1,785 km via the Hume and Pacific Highway. Routes, overnight stops, fuel, floods, border rules and dump points.
melbourne-to-brisbane-drive.region: Victoria, New South Wales and Queensland
melbourne-to-brisbane-drive.imageAlt: A northbound view of the Newell Highway between Finley and Jerilderie, New South Wales, with eucalypts either side of the road
melbourne-to-brisbane-drive.intro: Melbourne to Brisbane is about 1,675 km and about 22 hours of driving on the inland route, the Newell Highway through Tocumwal, Dubbo, Moree and Goondiwindi, by OSRM routing. The coastal option through Sydney and the Pacific Highway is about 1,784 km, and it takes less time because more of it is dual carriageway.

sections.heading: Melbourne to Brisbane routes compared
body: The inland route leaves Melbourne through Shepparton, crosses the Murray at Tocumwal and follows the Newell Highway (A39) through Narrandera, West Wyalong, Parkes, Dubbo, Coonabarabran, Narrabri and Moree to Goondiwindi, then the Gore Highway through Millmerran and Toowoomba to Brisbane. Wikipedia says the Newell is 1,058 km from Tocumwal to Boggabilla and Goondiwindi, and that apart from short four-lane urban sections it is single carriageway with many overtaking lanes. Most rural sections are 110 km/h.

Two alternatives rejoin the Newell at Narrandera or skip it entirely. One uses the Hume Highway to Wagga Wagga, then the Sturt Highway to Narrandera. The other follows the Hume to Sydney and the Pacific Highway to Brisbane, which the Sydney to Melbourne and Brisbane to Sydney drive guides cover in detail. All figures are from OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data, computed on 21 October 2026, for a car from city centre to city centre with no stops. Towing and fuel stops add time.
tips: Newell: shortest, single carriageway, long legs
Via Sydney: longer but faster by the clock

sections.heading: The Newell in four days
body: By OSRM routing, a four-day split is Melbourne to Narrandera about 426 km, Narrandera to Dubbo about 394 km, Dubbo to Moree about 365 km and Moree to Brisbane about 490 km. The legs are Melbourne to Shepparton about 178 km (2 h 20 min), Shepparton to Tocumwal about 82 km (1 h 15 min), Tocumwal to Narrandera about 166 km (2 h 7 min), Narrandera to West Wyalong about 135 km (1 h 35 min), West Wyalong to Parkes about 140 km (1 h 50 min), Parkes to Dubbo about 119 km (1 h 29 min), Dubbo to Coonabarabran about 145 km (1 h 55 min), Coonabarabran to Narrabri about 120 km (1 h 28 min), Narrabri to Moree about 100 km (1 h 13 min), Moree to Goondiwindi about 124 km (1 h 29 min), Goondiwindi to Millmerran about 147 km (1 h 54 min), Millmerran to Toowoomba about 94 km (1 h 23 min) and Toowoomba to Brisbane about 125 km (1 h 46 min).
Three days is possible if you drive about 590 km on the last day, but towing makes four more realistic. These are driving distances without stops.

sections.heading: Where to stop on the Newell
body: Phone to confirm park details: the park names below come from listings and a 2015 Newell Highway visitor guide. Dubbo Midstate Caravan Park is at 21 Bourke Street in Dubbo. Narrabri Big Sky Caravan Park is at 11 to 35 Tibbereena Street. BIG4 Goondiwindi Holiday Park is at 36 Old Cunningham Highway, and Goondiwindi's showground is about 3 km north of town. River Meadows Caravan Park is in Forbes, at the corner of the Newell Highway and River Road, if you want a stop near Parkes.

The AussieCamps data lists Sandy Beach campground at Cudgel near Narrandera, and Murray River campgrounds near Tocumwal and Cobram, including Smithers Beach, Woperana and Quicks Beach. For a break, it lists Narrandera Visitors Centre, Dubbo Tourist Information Centre, McCann Park near West Wyalong and Millmerran rest areas with toilets, picnic tables and a heavy vehicle area. Spring Creek Rest Area, north of Narrabri, opened in September 2025 as the region's largest heavy vehicle rest area, with separate parking for light vehicles and for light vehicles with caravans or trailers, two toilets and picnic shelters. Queensland allows up to 20 hours at a rest area unless a sign says otherwise, New South Wales advice conflicts and Victorian councils can ban overnight stays, so treat them as break stops and read the sign.
tips: Dubbo, Narrabri and Goondiwindi have caravan parks
Spring Creek Rest Area suits caravans for a break
Read the sign at every rest area

sections.heading: Fuel and services
body: The sources checked give no fuel gap for the Newell. The longest town-to-town legs are Goondiwindi to Millmerran at about 147 km, Dubbo to Coonabarabran at about 145 km and West Wyalong to Parkes at about 140 km, and Gilgandra lies between Dubbo and Coonabarabran. Fuel and opening hours at each small town could not be confirmed, so fill up in the larger towns, such as Narrandera, Dubbo, Narrabri, Moree and Goondiwindi.

Heavy vehicles make up between 26 and 52 per cent of Newell traffic depending on location, according to Wikipedia, so expect trucks and allow extra time to pass on single carriageway. The Narrabri to Moree pavement upgrade, with five new overtaking lanes, was reported complete in September 2025.
tips: Fill up at the larger towns
Plenty of trucks on the Newell
Overtaking lanes added north of Narrabri

sections.heading: Road conditions, floods and tolls
body: Check Live Traffic NSW (livetraffic.com, 132 701), QLDTraffic and VicTraffic before each leg. Wikipedia says parts of the Newell flood periodically, particularly north of Moree, at Dubbo and south of Narrandera. In April 2024 the Newell closed between Boggabilla and Moree and traffic was diverted via the Carnarvon and Barwon Highways to Goondiwindi, and it has also closed between Moree and the Queensland border in later floods. No current closure was listed in the sources checked on 21 October 2026.

On the Newell and the Gore Highway you are unlikely to meet tolls, but the ends can. Linkt says its Melbourne Visitor's Pass is good for up to 30 days on any toll road in Melbourne and covers CityLink trips made up to 5 days ago and EastLink trips made up to 3 days ago, and a Queensland road pass can cover trips made up to 5 days ago on all toll roads in Queensland. Which toll roads you meet depends on where you start and finish. On the Sydney route, NSW says you have 72 hours to pay or open an account.
tips: North of Moree floods most often

sections.heading: Border rules: Victoria, New South Wales and Queensland
body: Between Victoria and New South Wales, Agriculture Victoria says the Greater Sunraysia Pest Free Area regulation ended in July 2024, so there are no longer restrictions on carrying Queensland fruit fly host produce into or out of Sunraysia, and that Mediterranean fruit fly restrictions apply statewide. No fruit fly checkpoint turned up at Tocumwal or Albury in the sources checked, so check Agriculture Victoria on 136 186 before carrying produce. The Interstate Quarantine site lists a NSW Rice Biosecurity Zone across most of the Murrumbidgee and Murray regions and a Phylloxera Infested Zone around Albury and Corowa.

At Goondiwindi and Boggabilla, Queensland is the one to watch. The Interstate Quarantine site says the whole of Queensland is a biosecurity zone for bananas, grape plants, mangoes and sugarcane, and not to take any plants, soil or items that have been in contact with these plants into Queensland. NSW DPIRD describes the fire ant infested area as about 1,111,800 ha of south east Queensland and parts of northern NSW, with roadside checks across the north of NSW, and it lists soil, mulch, hay, pallets, green waste, compost, manure and heavy vehicles as carriers. Whether the Toowoomba and Brisbane approaches sit inside the zone could not be confirmed, so check the Biosecurity Queensland map and 13 25 23, and NSW DPIRD on 1800 680 244. The interstate biosecurity guide covers the rest.
tips: No fruit fly checkpoint found at the Murray crossings
Queensland: no plants, soil or banana items

sections.heading: Dump points and the clock change
body: The AussieCamps data lists dump points at Memorial Park in Wandong, north of Melbourne, and Lions Park at Strathmerton near Tocumwal, both with a washout tap listed. It lists none within 10 km of the New South Wales and Queensland sections of the Newell, which is only the data's coverage: a guide lists a dump point at Moree Showground. Check the dump points guide and call ahead.

Queensland does not use daylight saving and Victoria and New South Wales do: NSW says it runs from Sunday 4 October 2026 to Sunday 4 April 2027, so between those dates the clock moves back one hour at the Queensland border.

Open the trip in coverage before you leave each town. AussieCamps runs on iPhone only, and it is free to download, with in-app purchases.

faq: How far is it to drive from Melbourne to Brisbane?

About 1,675 km by the inland Newell Highway route, about 1,786 km via Wagga Wagga and about 1,784 km via Sydney and the Pacific Highway, by OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data. That is about 22 hours of driving on the Newell, so plan three to four days.
Which road is the Newell Highway?

The Newell Highway (A39) runs 1,058 km from Tocumwal on the Murray River to Boggabilla and Goondiwindi, according to Wikipedia, and is the longest highway in New South Wales. Apart from short urban sections it is single carriageway with overtaking lanes, and the Gore Highway continues it to Toowoomba.
Does the Newell Highway flood?

Yes. Wikipedia says sections are subject to periodic flooding from the rivers it crosses, particularly north of Moree, at Dubbo and south of Narrandera. The Newell has closed between Moree and Boggabilla in past floods, so check Live Traffic NSW and QLDTraffic before each leg.
Can I bring soil, mulch or hay from Victoria or New South Wales into Queensland?

Be careful. Queensland is a biosecurity zone for bananas, grape plants, mangoes and sugarcane, and fire ant rules cover soil, mulch, hay and plants in south east Queensland and northern New South Wales. Check Biosecurity Queensland on 13 25 23 and NSW DPIRD on 1800 680 244 before you carry anything like that.

sydney-to-adelaide-drive.title: Sydney to Adelaide Drive 2026: Sturt Highway, Barrier Highway, Stops and Campsites
sydney-to-adelaide-drive.description: Sydney to Adelaide is about 1,412 km and 17 hours on the Sturt Highway, or about 1,591 km via Melbourne. Routes compared, overnight stops, fruit fly rules, fuel gaps and dump points.
sydney-to-adelaide-drive.region: New South Wales, Victoria and South Australia
sydney-to-adelaide-drive.imageAlt: The Murrumbidgee River at Balranald, New South Wales, with red gums leaning over the water
sydney-to-adelaide-drive.intro: Sydney to Adelaide is about 1,412 km and 17 hours of driving by the inland Sturt Highway, through Wagga Wagga, Hay, Balranald, Mildura and Renmark, by OSRM routing. The other options are the Hume Highway via Melbourne, about 1,591 km, and the remote Barrier Highway through Cobar and Broken Hill, which is a longer outback drive.

sections.heading: Sydney to Adelaide routes compared
body: The inland route follows the Hume Highway from Sydney to Tarcutta, then the Sturt Highway through Wagga Wagga, Narrandera, Hay, Balranald, Mildura, Renmark and Waikerie to Gawler and Adelaide. Wikipedia says the Sturt Highway runs 947 km from Tarcutta to Gawler, about 596 km in New South Wales, 117 km in Victoria and 234 km in South Australia, and that most of it is single carriageway. The second option is the Hume Highway to Melbourne, then the Melbourne to Adelaide road, which the coastal route guide covers. The third is the Barrier Highway, which leaves the Mitchell Highway at Nyngan and runs through Cobar, Wilcannia, Broken Hill and Yunta to Burra.

All distances and times are from OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data, checked on 3 November 2026, for a car with no stops. By that routing the Barrier Highway route is about 1,673 km. Wikipedia gives the Barrier Highway as 1,012 km from Nyngan to Giles Corner in South Australia.
tips: Via Melbourne: dual carriageway most of the way

sections.heading: Sydney to Adelaide on the Sturt Highway in four days
body: By OSRM routing, a four-day split is Sydney to Wagga Wagga about 455 km (5 h 29 min), Wagga Wagga to Hay about 269 km (3 h 19 min), Hay to Mildura about 292 km (3 h 32 min) and Mildura to Adelaide about 397 km (4 h 57 min). Along the way, Goulburn is about 194 km from Sydney, Gundagai about 181 km further, Narrandera about 97 km after Wagga Wagga, Balranald about 135 km after Hay and Renmark about 143 km after Mildura.
The Hume Highway part is dual carriageway and 110 km/h, and the Sturt Highway beyond Wagga Wagga is where the quieter, single carriageway driving starts.

sections.heading: Where to stop on the Sturt Highway
body: Wagga Wagga has BIG4 Wagga Wagga Holiday Park. Narrandera has Sandy Beach campground at Cudgel in the AussieCamps data, and Narrandera Visitors Centre rest area for a break. Hay Caravan Park is on the Sturt Highway about 1 km east of the Sturt and Cobb Highway junction, and Hay Shire's directory also lists Hay Plains Holiday Park on Nailor Street and Hay Showground Caravan and Camping Ground on Showground Road. Balranald Lions Park is a rest area with toilets, shelter, picnic tables and barbecues in the AussieCamps data.

At the Victorian border, Discovery Parks Mildura Buronga Riverside is at 71A Caravan Park Road, Buronga, and has cabins, powered and unpowered sites and a dump point. In the Riverland, Discovery Parks Renmark Riverfront is at 1 Patey Drive, Renmark. The AussieCamps data lists Loch Luna, Kaiser Strip and Moorook campgrounds nearby. Check availability with each park. Rest areas are for a break: New South Wales advice conflicts, and South Australia and Victoria have no statewide limit in the sources checked, so read the sign and the rest area guide.
tips: Hay: three parks to choose from
Mildura: Buronga on the NSW side

sections.heading: The Barrier Highway option
body: For the remote route, Rita's Outback Guide gives leg distances of Nyngan to Cobar 132 km, Cobar to Wilcannia 261 km, Wilcannia to Broken Hill 198 km, Broken Hill to Yunta 195 km and Yunta to Burra 159 km. Sydney to Dubbo is about 398 km and Dubbo to Nyngan about 165 km by OSRM. Cobar Caravan Park is at 101 Marshall Street in Cobar and Broken Hill Tourist Park has cabins, powered sites and a dump point, listed by the operator.

Wikipedia describes the area as remote and very sparsely settled. NSW National Parks says outback NSW has extreme temperatures, reaching up to 50 degrees Celsius in some places, with autumn and spring the best times for long drives, and says to stay with your vehicle if it breaks down. The road trains guide covers road train etiquette.
tips: Stay with the vehicle if it breaks down

sections.heading: Fuel and services
body: On the Barrier Highway, Rita's Outback Guide describes Emmdale Roadhouse as the only place to get fuel between Cobar and Wilcannia, and Little Topar Roadhouse as the only place for fuel, drinks and food between Wilcannia and Broken Hill. Opening hours and whether Little Topar is currently trading could not be confirmed, so ring ahead. Nyngan, Cobar and Wilcannia are towns with fuel, and Yunta has two fuel stations according to the same guide. NSW National Parks says Mutawintji National Park, a side trip from Broken Hill, has no fuel or food.

On the Sturt Highway the longest town-to-town legs are Narrandera to Hay at about 175 km and Balranald to Mildura at about 159 km by OSRM. Fuel at smaller towns such as Darlington Point, Carrathool, Oxley and Euston could not be confirmed, so fill up at Wagga Wagga, Narrandera, Hay, Balranald and Mildura. The fuel planning guide shows how to budget the distance.
tips: Barrier: fuel before Cobar and Wilcannia
Sturt: fill up in Narrandera, Hay and Balranald

sections.heading: Road conditions, tolls and heat
body: Check Live Traffic NSW (livetraffic.com), VicTraffic and, in South Australia, the DIT outback road closures page (1300 361 033). The SA page says closed outback areas are restricted to residents, landowners, accredited media and relief services and not to try to travel through affected areas. A Riverina story reported the Sturt Highway west of Hay closing to light vehicles when the Murrumbidgee spilled over it, but it is undated, so check flood status before leaving.

Sydney's M5 and M7 are tolled and meet the Hume at Prestons. Linkt says that without an account you can buy a pass within 5 days of your first trip on Sydney or Queensland toll roads, and that unpaid trips bring a notice and an admin fee to the registered owner. Transport for NSW warns drivers in heatwaves to allow extra time because high temperatures often cause more breakdowns.
tips: Live Traffic NSW and DIT outback closures

sections.heading: Border rules: South Australia's fruit fly zone
body: South Australia is the border to plan for. PIRSA says there are permanent restrictions on bringing host produce into South Australia and the Riverland Pest Free Area, as well as restrictions within declared fruit fly outbreak areas. Quarantine bins are available at key entry points into South Australia and the Riverland, and it says travellers carrying restricted items should eat them beforehand or dispose of them in the bins. PIRSA also says it puts random roadblocks in place with quarantine officers checking vehicles for fresh fruit and vegetables, and that travellers found carrying restricted items may face a fine. The fine rose on 1 July 2026, so check the current amount on the PIRSA site.

Restricted produce can move if it is canned, cooked, dried, frozen, grated or pureed. The Interstate Quarantine site says for the Riverland not to take fresh, unprocessed fruit or fruiting vegetables. Outbreak areas and end dates change, so use the PIRSA outbreak map and the Fruit Fly Hotline on 1300 666 010. In Victoria, Agriculture Victoria says the Greater Sunraysia Pest Free Area regulation lapsed in July 2024 and Mediterranean fruit fly restrictions still apply statewide. The interstate biosecurity guide has the full picture.
tips: Eat or bin fresh fruit and vegetables before South Australia

sections.heading: Dump points and the clock changes
body: The AussieCamps data lists dump points on the Sturt route at Ampol Foodary Pheasants Nest Southbound (no washout tap listed), Uranquinty Rest Area (no washout tap listed), Lions Park in Darlington Point (washout tap listed) and Greenock Centenary Park in South Australia (washout tap listed). On the Barrier route it lists Farrell Flat Dump Point in South Australia (washout tap listed), and the operators of Discovery Parks Mildura Buronga Riverside and Broken Hill Tourist Park also list dump points. That is not every dump point, so check the dump points guide.

Daylight saving began on Sunday 4 October 2026 in New South Wales, Victoria, South Australia, Tasmania and the ACT, and ends on Sunday 4 April 2027. South Australia is on central time, so it is half an hour behind Victoria and New South Wales while daylight saving runs, and your clock goes back 30 minutes when you cross near Renmark. Broken Hill is in New South Wales but keeps Australian Central time.
tips: Washout tap listed at Darlington Point and Greenock
SA is 30 minutes behind Victoria until 4 April 2027

sections.heading: Plan the Sydney to Adelaide drive in AussieCamps
body: Add the overnight stops to a trip in AussieCamps and it lists them in order with the distance and drive time of each leg, and the forecast for the day you plan to arrive. AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and a place page shows the facilities those sources publish. Save a collection of stops for the Sturt Highway and another for the Barrier Highway to compare them.

Stored place details, saved places and guides work with no signal. Map tiles, routing, weather and photos need a connection, so open the trip before the long legs between Wagga Wagga and Mildura. AussieCamps runs on iPhone only, and it is free to download, with in-app purchases.
tips: Leg times and a forecast per stop
Open the trip before the long legs

faq: How far is it to drive from Sydney to Adelaide?
About 1,412 km and 17 h 18 min by the inland Sturt Highway route, or about 1,591 km and 19 h 28 min by way of Melbourne, by OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data. Plan three or four days.
Which is the shortest road from Sydney to Adelaide?

Wikipedia calls the Sturt Highway, reached by the Hume Highway to Tarcutta, the shortest, highest-standard route between the two cities. It runs 947 km from Tarcutta to Gawler through Narrandera, Hay, Balranald, Mildura and Renmark, and most of it is single carriageway.
Can I bring fruit into South Australia?

Not fresh fruit and fruiting vegetables in most cases. PIRSA says there are permanent restrictions on bringing host produce into South Australia and the Riverland Pest Free Area, and quarantine bins and random roadblocks operate at entry points. Produce that is canned, cooked, dried, frozen, grated or pureed can move, so eat or bin fresh produce before you cross.
Is Broken Hill on a different time to Sydney?

Yes. Broken Hill is in New South Wales but uses Australian Central time, so it is half an hour behind Sydney while daylight saving runs. On the Sturt Highway route, South Australia is also half an hour behind Victoria and New South Wales until daylight saving ends on 4 April 2027.

melbourne-to-canberra-drive.title: Melbourne to Canberra Drive 2026: Hume Highway, Alpine and Monaro Routes
melbourne-to-canberra-drive.description: Melbourne to Canberra is about 650 km and 8 hours on the Hume and Barton Highways. Routes compared with the alpine and Monaro options, stops, campgrounds, snow chains and dump points.
melbourne-to-canberra-drive.region: Victoria, New South Wales and the ACT
melbourne-to-canberra-drive.imageAlt: The dual carriageway Hume Highway between Gundagai and Goulburn, with traffic on both carriageways and green hills behind
melbourne-to-canberra-drive.intro: Melbourne to Canberra is about 652 km and 7 h 53 min of driving on the Hume Highway to Yass and the Barton Highway into Canberra, by OSRM routing. The two alternatives, over the Snowy Mountains or along the Monaro Highway from the south coast, add roughly 80 to 100 km and are for drivers who want the mountains or the coast.

sections.heading: Melbourne to Canberra routes compared
body: The standard route is the Hume Highway through Seymour, Euroa, Benalla, Wangaratta, Albury, Holbrook, Gundagai and Yass, then the Barton Highway (A25) into the ACT. Wikipedia says the Hume Highway has been dual carriageway for its full length since 7 August 2013, with a 110 km/h limit, and the Barton Highway runs 52 km from Yass to Lyneham, with only about 6 km of its New South Wales section dual carriageway.

The alpine route leaves the Hume at Albury, follows the Murray Valley Highway to Corryong, crosses the Snowy Mountains on the Alpine Way from Khancoban to Jindabyne, then runs through Cooma and along the Monaro Highway to Canberra. The Monaro route follows the Princes Highway from Melbourne to Cann River, then the Monaro Highway through Bombala and Cooma. Distances and times are from OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data, checked on 3 November 2026, for a car with no stops. The alpine total is derived from OSRM legs plus the length of the Alpine Way in Wikipedia, so it is not a routed figure.
tips: Hume: fastest, dual carriageway to Yass
Alpine: steep, narrow, closed sections in winter
Monaro: the coast road, then the tablelands

sections.heading: The Hume route in one or two days
body: By OSRM routing, Melbourne to Albury is about 317 km (3 h 53 min) and Albury to Canberra about 339 km (4 h 6 min), through Holbrook about 62 km, Gundagai about 118 km further, Yass about 101 km after that and Canberra about 60 km on. If you split the drive, Albury is the usual night. BIG4 Albury Tourist Park is on Wagga Road in Lavington, Albury Central Tourist Park is on North Street and Discovery Parks Lake Hume is about 15 minutes away. Confirm availability with the park.

Further on, Gundagai Cabins and Tourist Park is at 1 Nangus Road and VisitNSW describes it as suiting a stopover on the Hume Highway. Yass Caravan Park is about five minutes off the Hume on the northern side of Yass, with cabins, camping and drive-through caravan sites. The AussieCamps data lists Victorian Hume rest areas at Mangalore, Avenel, Benalla, Winton, Glenrowan, Wangaratta South and Chiltern, with toilets, picnic tables, barbecues and a heavy vehicle area, and mostly drinking water. It lists none for the New South Wales section here, which is a gap in the data. Treat rest areas as a place for a break: Victoria has no statewide overnight limit in the sources checked, and councils can ban overnight stays.

sections.heading: Camping in the ACT
body: ACT Parks says bookings are essential at Cotter Campground, which takes general camping, camper-trailers and small vans, with water, hot showers and barbecues and no dogs. Honeysuckle Campground also needs a booking and takes up to four campervans or camper-trailers, and fees apply. Mount Clear Campground in Namadgi National Park is a remote, basic campground that ACT Parks says is unsuitable for campervans and caravans, and its site lists closures for maintenance, fire bans and access problems. The AussieCamps data lists all four: Cotter, Honeysuckle, Mount Clear and Northern Border Campground. Fees were not confirmed, so check the ACT Parks page.
The camping rules guide for the ACT covers the rules, and the Namadgi Visitor Centre on (02) 6237 5307 can help with current access.
tips: Cotter and Honeysuckle need a booking

sections.heading: The alpine and Monaro options
body: On the alpine route, NPWS describes the Alpine Way between Khancoban and Thredbo as steep, narrow and winding, with rockfalls after rain, and not recommended for large caravans. By OSRM, Corryong is about 128 km beyond Albury (1 h 49 min), Khancoban about 29 km on, Jindabyne about 107 km further on the Alpine Way, then Cooma about 61 km and Canberra about 113 km. NPWS says the road from Khancoban to Cabramurra, and many minor roads in Kosciuszko National Park, are closed in winter, and roads can close in extreme weather.

NSW says all 2WD vehicles must carry chains between the June long weekend and the October long weekend on Kosciuszko Road, the Alpine Way between Thredbo and Tom Groggin and Island Bend and Guthega Road, and recommends them on the Snowy Mountains Highway. The 2026 period has ended and starts again in June 2027. The Monaro Highway is 285.1 km from Cann River to Canberra, with Cooma about 111.6 km from Canberra, and the Australian Alps and Victoria high country guides cover the mountain camping in more detail.
tips: Chains: June to October long weekends
Monaro Highway: Cann River to Canberra 285 km

sections.heading: Fuel and services
body: The sources checked give no fuel gap on any of these routes, and no figure should be taken from the OSRM legs, which only show the distance between the towns used as waypoints. The longest of those on the Hume is Melbourne to Euroa at about 159 km. Fill up in the larger towns, such as Seymour, Benalla, Wangaratta, Albury, Gundagai and Yass. On the alpine route, Khancoban to Jindabyne is about 107 km of national park road and fuel at Thredbo could not be confirmed, so fill up at Corryong or Jindabyne. The road trip fuel guide shows how to budget the distance.
tips: Fill up in the larger Hume towns
Alpine: top up at Corryong or Jindabyne

sections.heading: Road conditions, tolls and speed
body: Check VicTraffic and Live Traffic NSW (livetraffic.com, 132 701). NPWS tells drivers to use Live Traffic NSW for conditions in Kosciuszko National Park. The Hume Highway is 110 km/h for its full length according to Wikipedia, and it is not described as tolled.

In Melbourne, Linkt says its Visitor's Pass covers CityLink, EastLink and the West Gate Tunnel for up to 30 days, and covers CityLink trips made up to 5 days ago and EastLink trips made up to 3 days ago. Whether your start in Melbourne uses a toll road depends on your route to the Hume, so check before you leave.
tips: Linkt Visitor's Pass covers Melbourne tolls

sections.heading: Border rules and the clock
body: The Interstate Quarantine site lists no fruit fly restrictions for New South Wales or Victoria, and groups the ACT with New South Wales without separate zones. That is not proof that nothing applies, and no ACT government source on carrying fruit turned up in the sources checked. Agriculture Victoria says Greater Sunraysia regulation lapsed in July 2024 and Mediterranean fruit fly restrictions still apply statewide, so check Agriculture Victoria on 136 186. The same Interstate Quarantine site says that at some stage when travelling in Australia you are likely to be inspected or asked to surrender produce in an amnesty bin.
Victoria, New South Wales and the ACT all observe daylight saving, which began on Sunday 4 October 2026 and ends on Sunday 4 April 2027, so the clock does not change on any route.
tips: No fruit fly zone listed for NSW or Victoria

sections.heading: Dump points on the way
body: The AussieCamps data lists dump points on the Hume at Memorial Park in Wandong, Airport and RV Dump Point in Benalla and Warreena Park in Wangaratta, each with a washout tap listed, and Oxley Recreation Reserve with none listed. In Canberra it lists Epic, Exhibition Park Campground in Lyneham. On the alpine route it lists Corryong Saleyards with a washout tap listed, and on the Monaro route Bruthen Lions Park with a washout tap and Brodribb River Murrungower Rest Area without. It lists none on the New South Wales Hume between Chiltern and Yass, which is only the data's coverage, so check the dump points guide.
tips: Wandong, Benalla and Wangaratta list a washout tap
No NSW Hume dump point in the data

sections.heading: Plan the Melbourne to Canberra drive in AussieCamps
body: Plan it as a trip in AussieCamps: add the stops in order, Albury, Gundagai and a Canberra campground, and it shows the distance and drive time of each leg with a forecast for the day you plan to arrive. AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, including the ACT Parks and Kosciuszko campgrounds above, and a place page shows the facilities those sources publish.

Stored place details, saved places and guides work with no signal. Map tiles, routing, weather and photos need a connection, which matters on the alpine route, so open the trip before you leave Corryong. AussieCamps runs on iPhone only, and it is free to download, with in-app purchases.
tips: Add each overnight stop in order
Open the trip before the mountains

faq: How long does it take to drive from Melbourne to Canberra?

About 652 km and 7 h 53 min of driving on the Hume Highway and Barton Highway, by OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data. Most drivers do it in a long day, and Albury is the usual place to break it into two.
Is the Hume Highway all dual carriageway?

Wikipedia says yes, since the Holbrook bypass opened on 7 August 2013, with a limit of 110 km/h. The last 52 km into Canberra on the Barton Highway from Yass is different: it is mostly single carriageway, with only about 6 km of its NSW section dual carriageway.
Do I need snow chains between Melbourne and Canberra?

Not on the Hume or Barton Highways. On the alpine alternative through Kosciuszko National Park, NSW says all 2WD vehicles must carry chains between the June long weekend and the October long weekend on roads such as the Alpine Way between Thredbo and Tom Groggin. That period has ended for 2026 and starts again in June 2027.
Is there a fruit fly checkpoint between Victoria and New South Wales on this drive?

The sources checked show none. The Interstate Quarantine site lists no fruit fly restrictions for New South Wales or Victoria, and Agriculture Victoria says Greater Sunraysia regulation lapsed in July 2024, but Mediterranean fruit fly restrictions still apply statewide in Victoria, so check Agriculture Victoria on 136 186.

brisbane-to-byron-bay-drive.title: Brisbane to Byron Bay Drive 2026: Pacific Motorway or the Gold Coast Hinterland
brisbane-to-byron-bay-drive.description: Brisbane to Byron Bay is about 170 km and 2.5 hours on the Pacific Motorway, or 237 km via Springbrook and Murwillumbah. Routes compared with stops, fire ant rules, the border clock change and camping.
brisbane-to-byron-bay-drive.imageAlt: Aerial view of Cape Byron and its lighthouse, with surf along the coast and the green headland rising from the sea
brisbane-to-byron-bay-drive.intro: Brisbane to Byron Bay is about 165 to 175 km and roughly two and a half hours on the Pacific Motorway through the Gold Coast and Tweed Heads. Take the hinterland route through Mount Tamborine, Springbrook and Murwillumbah, about 237 km and four hours, if you want waterfalls and rainforest on the way.

sections.heading: Brisbane to Byron Bay routes compared
body: The direct route is the Pacific Motorway (M1) south to the Gold Coast, Tweed Heads and Byron Bay. By OSRM routing, Brisbane to the Gold Coast is about 76 km, then about 30 km to Tweed Heads and about 66 km to Byron Bay. Travel guides built on Google Maps put it at about 166 km and 1 h 52 min from the Brisbane CBD, so use about 165 to 175 km.

The hinterland route climbs through Mount Tamborine and Springbrook National Park and comes down to Murwillumbah in the Tweed Valley. The inland route follows the Mount Lindesay Highway through Beaudesert and Rathdowney, then the Summerland Way through Kyogle and Lismore. Distances and times are from OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data, computed on 21 October 2026, for a car with no stops. No distance figure was sourced for the Gold Coast Highway coast road.
tips: Motorway: fastest, about two and a half hours
Hinterland: waterfalls and rainforest, winding roads
Inland: quiet, with a closed shortcut to avoid

sections.heading: The hinterland route in two days
body: By OSRM routing, the legs are Brisbane to Mount Tamborine about 72 km (1 h 6 min), Tamborine to Springbrook about 55 km (1 h 11 min), Springbrook to Murwillumbah about 59 km (1 h 3 min) and Murwillumbah to Byron Bay about 51 km (48 min). A trail guide describes the road to Lamington's Green Mountains as sealed but narrow, winding and with many blind corners, so allow extra time and avoid towing a long caravan on it.

In the Tweed Valley, Greenhills Caravan Park is at 488 Tweed Valley Way in South Murwillumbah and Mt Warning Rainforest Park is at 153 Mt Warning Road. At Byron Bay, Reflections Byron Bay Holiday Park is at 1 Lighthouse Road, with powered and unpowered sites and cabins. Its operator says no individual fires or firepits are permitted, and one camping guide notes that the park books out months ahead for Easter and Bluesfest. Check availability and rules with the park.

sections.heading: National park camping near the route
body: QPWS says you must book campsites in advance at The Settlement camping area in Springbrook National Park. At Lamington National Park, O'Reilly's Campground at Green Mountains is privately managed, there is another privately managed campground beside Binna Burra, and remote bush camps need a permit booked online ahead for weekends and school or public holidays. QPWS lists parts of Lamington closed for cyclone damage until 31 December 2026 and says camping permits for closed areas are suspended, and remote bush camps close from 1 December to 31 January each year for regeneration, so check the current QPWS alert before you plan around any of them.

At Mount Barney, QPWS says camping areas can only be reached on foot, with no facilities, and a camping permit is needed, booked online 6 to 8 weeks ahead for public holidays and 3 to 6 weeks ahead the rest of the year. The AussieCamps data lists the Mount Barney bush camps near the Boonah Border Gate and the Lamington camps at Illinbah, Darlington, Echo Point and others, which are walk-in or rough-road bush camps rather than drive-up campgrounds. The Queensland camping rules guide covers permits.
tips: Lamington: check the QPWS closure alert

sections.heading: Fuel, tolls and road conditions
body: Both the motorway and hinterland routes pass through towns throughout, so no fuel gap turned up in the sources checked. A fuel gap between Rathdowney and Kyogle on the inland route could not be sourced, so fill up before you leave Rathdowney. The road trip fuel guide shows how to budget the distance.

Check QLDTraffic (13 19 40) and Live Traffic NSW (132 701). Gold Coast hinterland roads including the Gold Coast-Springbrook Road and Beechmont Road have closed after landslips, and Kyogle Council says Lions Road, the shortcut from Rathdowney to Wiangaree, remained closed from Murphy Standfield Bridge to the border in an April 2026 works update, with another notice saying it is open to light traffic only and not for caravans. QPWS says the main access roads to Mount Barney National Park can flood after storms and prolonged periods of rain.

Linkt's list of Queensland toll roads names the Gateway Motorway, Logan Motorway, Clem7, Go Between Bridge, Legacy Way, AirportlinkM7 and Toowoomba Bypass, and the Pacific Motorway is not on it. Linkt says without an account you can buy a pass within 5 days of your first trip, while the Queensland Government says a toll may be paid up to 3 days after, so pay within 3 days to be safe. NSW tolls on this stretch were not researched.
tips: Avoid Lions Road with a caravan
Check QLDTraffic and Live Traffic NSW

sections.heading: Fire ants and the Queensland and New South Wales border
body: The border rule that matters is red imported fire ant control. Queensland updated its biosecurity zones from 15 April 2026 in six council areas including Logan, the Gold Coast and Scenic Rim, and lists carriers such as baled hay or straw, manure, mulch, potted plants, quarry and mining materials, soil and turf. NSW DPIRD's emergency order covers three zones: a Queensland infested area, a NSW infested area near Tweed Heads South, and NSW movement control areas within 5 km of the Murwillumbah and Wardell infestations. NSW has said moving soil, mulch, turf and hay out of its Piggabeen and Cobaki border area may require a Record of Movement Declaration and a Plant Health Certificate. Ring NSW DPIRD on 1800 680 244 or Biosecurity Queensland on 13 22 68, and check current boundaries.

No source checked says ordinary cars, caravans, camping gear or firewood are controlled, so do not take that as a clearance, and ask if you carry any of the listed materials. The Interstate Quarantine site also says that the whole of Queensland is a biosecurity zone for bananas, grape plants, mangoes and sugarcane, and not to take any plants, soil or items that have been in contact with these plants into Queensland. It lists no fruit fly restrictions for New South Wales.
tips: Fire ants: soil, mulch, turf, hay, manure
Queensland: no banana plants, grape plants, mangoes or sugarcane items

sections.heading: The clock change and Mount Warning
body: From Sunday 4 October 2026 to Sunday 4 April 2027, New South Wales is on daylight saving and Queensland is not, so the clock goes forward one hour when you cross at Tweed Heads and Coolangatta, and check-in times at Byron Bay run an hour ahead of Brisbane.

Mount Warning (Wollumbin) is reached from Murwillumbah. NPWS local alerts say the summit track and summit have been closed until further notice since 30 June 2023, while the Korrumbyn Creek picnic area, the Lyrebird walking track and visitor facilities at Breakfast Creek stay open, and penalties apply. The alert text itself did not load, so check with the Byron NPWS office on 02 6639 8300.
tips: Clocks go forward an hour into NSW

sections.heading: Dump points
body: The AussieCamps data lists no dump points within 12 km of any of the three routes, which is the data's coverage and not a statement that none exist. Beaudesert Caravan and Tourist Park, at 57 to 63 Albert Street, lists a dump point on its tourism listing, and the dump points guide has the rest.
tips: Check Beaudesert Caravan and Tourist Park for a dump point

sections.heading: Plan the Brisbane to Byron Bay drive in AussieCamps
body: Plan it as a trip in AussieCamps: add the stops, from a Springbrook or Lamington camp to a Byron Bay park, in order and it shows the distance and drive time of each leg, with a forecast for the day you plan to arrive. AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and a place page shows the facilities those sources publish.

Stored place details, saved places and guides work with no signal. Map tiles, routing, weather and photos need a connection, so open the trip before you climb into the hinterland. AussieCamps runs on iPhone only, and it is free to download, with in-app purchases.
tips: Open the trip before the hinterland

faq: How far is it from Brisbane to Byron Bay?

About 165 to 175 km and roughly two and a half hours on the Pacific Motorway (M1) through the Gold Coast and Tweed Heads, by OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data. The Gold Coast hinterland route is about 237 km and 4 hours, and the inland route via Beaudesert and Kyogle about 339 km and 6 hours.
Is there a time difference between Queensland and Byron Bay?

Yes, from 4 October 2026 to 4 April 2027. New South Wales runs daylight saving in that period and Queensland does not, so the New South Wales side of the border is one hour ahead and clocks go forward an hour at Tweed Heads.
Can I take soil, mulch or turf from Queensland into New South Wales?

Not without checking. Red imported fire ant rules cover carriers such as soil, mulch, turf, manure and baled hay moving out of the infested areas, and NSW says moving soil, mulch, turf and hay out of its border zone may need a Record of Movement Declaration and a Plant Health Certificate. Ring NSW DPIRD on 1800 680 244 or Biosecurity Queensland on 13 22 68.
Can I climb Mount Warning (Wollumbin) on the way?

NPWS local alerts say the summit track and summit have been closed until further notice since 30 June 2023, while the Korrumbyn Creek picnic area and the Lyrebird walking track stay open. The alert text itself did not load when checked, so confirm with the NSW National Parks Byron office on 02 6639 8300 before you go.

darwin-to-alice-springs-drive.title: Darwin to Alice Springs Drive 2026: Stuart Highway Stops, Fuel and Quarantine
darwin-to-alice-springs-drive.description: Darwin to Alice Springs is about 1,500 km and 15 hours on the Stuart Highway. Day-by-day stops, rest areas, fuel advice, wet season closures, speed limits, fruit quarantine rules and dump points.
darwin-to-alice-springs-drive.imageAlt: A split granite boulder at Karlu Karlu (Devils Marbles) Conservation Reserve in the Northern Territory, with other orange boulders behind it
darwin-to-alice-springs-drive.intro: Darwin to Alice Springs is about 1,500 km, or 1,492 km and 15 h 12 min of driving by OSRM routing, and it is one road: the Stuart Highway through Katherine, Daly Waters, Tennant Creek and Karlu Karlu. Plan four days, check Road Report NT before each leg, and read the fruit rules, because produce restrictions apply on this drive.

sections.heading: One road: the Stuart Highway
body: There is only one realistic sealed route between Darwin and Alice Springs, the Stuart Highway, which Tourism NT calls the Explorers Way. It runs through Adelaide River, Pine Creek, Katherine, Mataranka, Daly Waters, Elliott, Tennant Creek, Karlu Karlu (Devils Marbles), Barrow Creek and Ti Tree. Wikipedia gives 1,499 km from Darwin to Alice Springs, and OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data, checked on 3 November 2026 for a car with no stops, gives 1,492 km, so about 1,500 km is the safe figure.

The detours are Kakadu, Nitmiluk (Katherine Gorge) at Katherine and Litchfield, which the Darwin, Kakadu and Litchfield loop covers. After Alice Springs, the Red Centre Way and the Adelaide to Uluru road trip cover what comes next.

table.caption: Darwin to Alice Springs on the Stuart Highway, OSRM routing checked 3 November 2026, with Tourism NT leg distances where they exist.
head: Leg
Distance
Drive time

sections.heading: Four days on the Stuart Highway
body: By OSRM, a four-day split is Darwin to Katherine about 315 km (3 h 26 min), Katherine to Daly Waters about 273 km (2 h 48 min), Daly Waters to Tennant Creek about 405 km (4 h 4 min) and Tennant Creek to Alice Springs about 506 km (5 h 3 min, via Karlu Karlu). Tourism NT's itineraries give Katherine to Darwin as 316 km, Mataranka to Katherine 106 km, Daly Waters to Mataranka 167 km and Alice Springs to Tennant Creek 510 km, which agree with OSRM within a few kilometres.

Katherine is the base for Nitmiluk. At Mataranka, NT Parks says the thermal pool in Elsey National Park holds a steady 34 degrees all year and that an NT Parks Visitor Pass is needed, bought before arriving, with NT residents exempt. At Daly Waters, Tourism NT describes the Daly Waters Historic Pub as a place to eat, drink and stay, with camping, powered sites, safari tents and cabins. Named caravan parks at Katherine, Mataranka and Tennant Creek could not be confirmed, so book ahead by phone.

sections.heading: Karlu Karlu (Devils Marbles)
body: Tourism NT says entry to Karlu Karlu, about 96 km south of Tennant Creek, requires an NT Parks Visitor Pass, which is a separate pass from the Kakadu and Uluru-Kata Tjuta passes. It says you must book online and pay a fee to camp, and that you will not be able to pay at the site. Tourism NT describes a bush camping area with fireplaces. Fees were not confirmed, so check the booking site before you go.
Wauchope, about 9 km south of Karlu Karlu, has fuel and limited supplies, according to an NT Government fact sheet. Wycliffe Well is 130 km south of Tennant Creek and 380 km north of Alice Springs.

sections.heading: Rest areas on the Stuart Highway
body: The AussieCamps data lists rest areas along the road that you can use for a break: Bridge Creek, King River and Warloch Ponds with toilets, drinking water, shelter, picnic tables and barbecues, Newcastle Waters and Attack Creek with the same, Taylor Creek and Prowse Gap with toilets, and Dingo Hill, Bonney Well, Central Mount Stuart and Connors Well with no toilets listed.

Northern Territory policy says road users may not stay at any one rest area longer than 24 hours, and the Territory lists which stops allow 24-hour overnight camping and marks some as camping not permitted. The list could not be opened for this guide, so read the sign at the stop and check the NT list. The rest area guide has the rules.
tips: Read the sign at each stop
24 hours at most at one rest area
Bridge Creek km 147, King River km 365

sections.heading: Fuel and services
body: Tourism NT says that when travelling to remote parts of the Territory you should use a vehicle with a long range fuel tank and take extra fuel, and that remote service stations have restricted opening hours. Wikipedia says fuel and other facilities are usually available about every 200 km on the Stuart Highway. No official roadhouse-to-roadhouse table was available, so no longest gap is named here: fill up at every roadhouse you pass and ask at the last one about the next.
The Barkly Highway junction at Threeways Roadhouse is about 25 km north of Tennant Creek. The fuel planning guide shows how to budget the distance.
tips: Hours are restricted at remote stations
Threeways is 25 km north of Tennant Creek

sections.heading: Road conditions, speed limits and road trains
body: Road Report NT (roadreport.nt.gov.au or 1800 246 199) is the live source. Tourism NT says some roads may be closed by flooding from November to April, that you must not drive on closed roads and that heavy fines may apply. An NT Government flood study found the Stuart Highway closed 100 times between October 2005 and March 2024, for about 35 hours on average. The wet season guide covers cyclones, crocodiles and storms.

NT regulations say the limit outside built-up areas is 110 km/h, but 130 km/h applies where speed-limit signs show it, and NT Government says some sections of the Barkly, Stuart, Victoria and Arnhem Highways have a maximum of 130 km/h as indicated. Speed cameras are used across the Territory. Many roads are unfenced, and Tourism NT says animals appear especially at dawn, dusk and night and not to swerve to avoid them.

NT Government says road trains can be over 50 m long with up to three trailers, overtaking can take up to 2.5 km at 100 km/h and you need at least 1 km of clear road ahead. The road trains guide covers the rest.
tips: The sign sets the limit, 110 or 130 km/h

sections.heading: Fruit and vegetable rules
body: Quarantine applies on this drive. The Interstate Quarantine site, quoting the Northern Territory, says the following produce must not be carried south along the Stuart Highway beyond the Adelaide River township: beans, capsicum, chilli, cucumber, eggplant, melons, mango fruit and mango plants (unless treated against leaf hopper), okra, pumpkin, silverbeet, squash, tomato and zucchini. It aims to stop the spread of melon thrips.

The same site says the Ti Tree Fruit Fly Exclusion Zone extends from Tennant Creek to Alice Springs, and not to take fruit, including capsicum, chilli, tomato, eggplant, cucumber, zucchini and squash, into the zone. Northern Territory Government says that if you are travelling to Ti Tree, north of Alice Springs, you must dispose of any fruit you have brought from interstate, and quarantine bins are at Alice Springs Airport and railway station. No highway checkpoint was found in the sources checked. The interstate biosecurity guide covers the wider rules.
tips: Do not carry listed produce south past Adelaide River
No fruit in the Tennant Creek to Alice Springs zone

sections.heading: Dump points, clocks and crocodiles
body: The AussieCamps data lists dump points at Darwin Greyhound Club in Winnellie, Coomalie Creek RV Park, Adelaide River, Pine Creek, two in Katherine, King River and Mataranka, and in Alice Springs at the Alice Springs Dump Point, Olive Pink Botanic Gardens and the Showground. It lists none between Mataranka and Alice Springs, which is the data's coverage and not a statement that none exist, so check the dump points guide.

The Northern Territory does not use daylight saving, according to the Australian Government, so there is no clock change on this drive. NT Government's Be Crocwise advice is to swim only where a swimming area sign is displayed, camp at least 50 m from the water's edge, and its table lists Mataranka thermal pool and Bitter Springs as open all year except during extreme flooding.
tips: Dump points to Mataranka, then none listed
No daylight saving in the NT
Camp 50 m from the water's edge

sections.heading: Plan the Darwin to Alice Springs drive in AussieCamps
body: Plan the four days as a trip in AussieCamps: add each night in order and it shows the distance and drive time between them, and a forecast for the day you plan to arrive. AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and the Stuart Highway rest areas above show their toilets, drinking water and shelter.

Stored place details, saved places and guides work with no signal. Map tiles, routing, weather and photos need a connection, and there is little coverage between the towns, so open the trip while you are in range. AussieCamps runs on iPhone only, and it is free to download, with in-app purchases.

faq: How far is it from Darwin to Alice Springs?

About 1,500 km, which is 1,492 km and 15 h 12 min of driving by OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data, all on the Stuart Highway. Most people take four days, with nights at Katherine, Daly Waters and Tennant Creek.
What is the speed limit on the Stuart Highway?

Tourism NT says the open-road limit is 110 km/h unless signed otherwise, and that certain highways allow up to 130 km/h. NT regulations say 130 km/h applies where speed-limit signs show it, so the sign decides.
Can I take fruit and vegetables from Darwin to Alice Springs?

Not all of them. The Interstate Quarantine site lists produce including beans, capsicum, chilli, cucumber, eggplant, melons, mango, pumpkin, tomato and zucchini that must not be carried south along the Stuart Highway beyond Adelaide River, and says not to take fruit into the Ti Tree Fruit Fly Exclusion Zone, which runs from Tennant Creek to Alice Springs.
Does the Stuart Highway flood in the wet season?

Yes. Tourism NT says some roads may be closed by flooding from November to April, and an NT Government study found the Stuart Highway closed 100 times between October 2005 and March 2024, for about 35 hours on average. Check Road Report NT or 1800 246 199 each day.

cairns-to-darwin-drive.title: Cairns to Darwin Drive 2026: Savannah Way or the Sealed Barkly Route
cairns-to-darwin-drive.description: Cairns to Darwin is about 2,900 km by the sealed Barkly route or about 2,400 to 2,500 km on the part-unsealed Savannah Way. Routes compared, fuel gaps, wet season closures, border rules and dump points.
cairns-to-darwin-drive.imageAlt: Cathedral termite mounds beside a fence along the Burke Developmental Road near Stokes in the Queensland Gulf Country
cairns-to-darwin-drive.intro: Cairns to Darwin is about 2,900 km by the sealed route through Townsville, Cloncurry, Mount Isa, Camooweal and the Barkly and Stuart Highways, by OSRM routing. The Savannah Way across the Gulf Country is shorter, about 2,400 to 2,500 km direct, but part of it is unsealed and wet season closures can shut it from December to March.

sections.heading: Cairns to Darwin routes compared
body: The main route is all sealed. It follows the Bruce Highway to Townsville, the Flinders Highway through Charters Towers and Cloncurry, the Barkly Highway through Mount Isa, Camooweal and Barkly Homestead to Threeways, and the Stuart Highway north through Daly Waters and Katherine. Wikipedia describes the Barkly Highway as the only sealed road between Queensland and the Northern Territory. A variant goes inland through Mareeba, Georgetown, Croydon and Normanton, then the Burke Developmental Road to Cloncurry.

The Savannah Way goes through Georgetown, Croydon, Normanton, Burketown, Hells Gate Roadhouse and Borroloola to the Stuart Highway or the Roper Bar route. The tourism body says it uses sealed and unsealed roads, with sealed roads from Borroloola onwards, and that a 4WD is needed. Its own 3,530.7 km figure is for a longer 17-day tour including Karumba, Boodjamulla and Kakadu, so it is not comparable to the direct figure below. All other figures are from OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data, computed on 21 October 2026, for a car with no stops. OSRM times on unsealed roads are unreliable, so none are shown for the Savannah Way.
tips: Main route: all sealed, any vehicle
Do not trust drive times on gravel

sections.heading: The main route in six days
body: By OSRM routing, a six-day split is Cairns to Charters Towers about 483 km, Charters Towers to Cloncurry about 649 km, Cloncurry to Camooweal about 312 km, Camooweal to Tennant Creek about 472 km, Tennant Creek to Katherine about 682 km and Katherine to Darwin about 315 km. The legs are Cairns to Townsville about 347 km (4 h 43 min), Townsville to Charters Towers about 136 km (1 h 41 min), Charters Towers to Cloncurry about 649 km (7 h 55 min), Cloncurry to Mount Isa about 121 km (1 h 34 min), Mount Isa to Camooweal about 191 km (2 h 16 min), Camooweal to Barkly Homestead about 250 km (2 h 27 min), Barkly Homestead to Tennant Creek about 222 km (2 h 11 min), Tennant Creek to Daly Waters about 406 km (4 h 5 min) and Daly Waters to Katherine about 276 km (2 h 55 min).

Tourism NT gives Katherine to Darwin as 316 km and Tennant Creek to Daly Waters as about 400 km. Threeways Roadhouse is where the Barkly meets the Stuart Highway, about 25 km north of Tennant Creek. The Darwin to Alice Springs drive guide covers the Stuart Highway north of Threeways, and the east coast guides cover Cairns and Townsville.

sections.heading: Where to stop and where to take a break
body: The AussieCamps data lists national park campgrounds near the main route at Jourama Falls, Big Crystal Creek in Mount Spec, Alligator Creek in Mount Elliot, Broadwater and Scraggy Point, and it lists nothing between Charters Towers and Katherine. On the Gulf side it lists Kauri Creek, Downfall Creek and Platypus in the Tablelands, and Cannabullen Creek and Koolmoon Creek. At Karumba, Carpentaria Shire Council says overnight parking is not permitted on roadsides and other public land within 5 km of Normanton and Karumba, and it runs a seasonal free camping site on the Norman River at Normanton with limited permits. Listings name Karumba Point Tourist Park, Gulf Country Caravan Park and Karumba Lodge Caravan Park, so book ahead by phone.

Rest areas in the AussieCamps data for a break include Babinda, Georgetown and Croydon in Queensland, and Avon Downs, 41 Mile Bore, Attack Creek and Newcastle Waters in the Northern Territory. Queensland allows up to 20 hours at a rest area unless a sign says otherwise, and heavy vehicle rest areas are for heavy vehicles only. The Northern Territory says no more than 24 hours at any one rest area. Read the sign and the rest area guide.
tips: Nothing in the app data between Charters Towers and Katherine
No roadside camping within 5 km of Normanton and Karumba

sections.heading: Fuel gaps
body: The Savannah Way site says to plan your fuel stops with hundreds of kilometres between roadhouses, and Tourism NT says to use a vehicle with a long range fuel tank and take extra fuel in remote parts of the Territory. The best-sourced gaps are Roper Bar to Cape Crawford, where Tourism NT says there are no fuel stops for 338 km, and Hells Gate Roadhouse to Borroloola at about 317 km, a figure from the AussieCamps data and a Savannah Way guide. Borroloola to Roper Bar is a further 377 km with no fuel on the unsealed route, according to the same guide.

On the Barkly route, Camooweal to Barkly Homestead is about 260 km and Barkly Homestead to Tennant Creek about 220 km, with the Homestead the stop in between. Barkly Homestead has had a kitchen fire and closure in the past, so check it is open. Fuel at Normanton, Burketown, Borroloola, Hughenden, Richmond and Julia Creek could not be confirmed, so ask at each stop about the next. The fuel planning guide shows how to budget the distance.
tips: Hells Gate to Borroloola: about 317 km
Roper Bar to Cape Crawford: 338 km, no fuel

sections.heading: Wet season closures and road conditions
body: Check QLDTraffic and Road Report NT (roadreport.nt.gov.au or 1800 246 199) each day. The Savannah Way says sections of the route are closed during the wet season, December to March, that access in April and May depends on rainfall easing, and that May to October is best. Tourism NT says some Territory roads may be closed by flooding from November to April. In March 2026, QLDTraffic and Carpentaria Shire reported the Gulf Developmental Road between Normanton and the Croydon Shire boundary closed to all traffic for long-term flooding, so flood closures are a real risk. No current closure was found for 21 October 2026. The wet season guide covers cyclones and crocodiles.

In the Northern Territory the limit outside built-up areas is 110 km/h, with 130 km/h where signs show it. Tourism NT says four-wheel drive vehicles are best for dirt roads and that unsealed conditions can change quickly in wet weather or with large numbers of road trains and cattle trucks. NT Government says road trains can be over 50 m long and overtaking can take up to 2.5 km at 100 km/h. The road trains guide covers etiquette, and the Queensland Outback Way guide covers more of the Queensland outback.
tips: Savannah Way best May to October
Sealed route is the safe choice

sections.heading: Border rules and the clock change
body: No checkpoint turned up in the sources checked at either border crossing, but rules apply. The Interstate Quarantine site says the whole of Queensland is a biosecurity zone for bananas, grape plants, mangoes and sugarcane, and not to take any plants, soil or items that have been in contact with these plants into Queensland. It also lists zones around Cairns, including a Melon Thrips North Queensland Restricted Area covering areas inland and south of Cooktown, Cairns and Innisfail down to Bowen, and a Cercospora Leaf Spot Affected Area in the Mareeba Shire. What a driver may carry out of those zones could not be confirmed, so ring Queensland DAF on 13 25 23.

Entering the Northern Territory, NT Government restrictions cover fruit and vegetables and the plants that produce them, seed and grain, soil, compost and potting mix, plant packaging and farm or earthmoving equipment, and it says uncertified bananas from North Queensland are not allowed into the Territory. If you are unsure, check Interstate Quarantine or contact NT Plant Biosecurity. The Northern Territory is on central time and Queensland on eastern time, and neither uses daylight saving, so clocks go back half an hour at the border. The interstate biosecurity guide covers the wider rules.
tips: No uncertified North Queensland bananas into the NT
Clocks back 30 minutes at the border

sections.heading: National parks, crocodiles and dump points
body: Boodjamulla (Lawn Hill) needs a camping permit and Queensland Parks says to pre-book from March to October, with access from Gregory Downs unsealed for 100 km. Limmen National Park needs an NT Parks Visitor Pass bought before you arrive, with NT residents exempt, and all campsites must be booked online before your visit. Estuarine crocodiles occur throughout the Gulf of Carpentaria, and Queensland says there is a possibility that crocodiles may be present in any water body north of Gladstone. NT Government says swim only where a swimming area sign is displayed and camp at least 50 m from the water's edge.

The AussieCamps data lists dump points on the main route at Ingham, Bluewater, Cloncurry, Barkly Homestead, Mataranka, Katherine, Pine Creek, Adelaide River and Darwin, and on the Savannah Way at Hells Gate Roadhouse and Borroloola. It lists none between Townsville and Cloncurry or between Mount Isa and Barkly Homestead, which is only the data's coverage. Carpentaria Shire lists council dump points at Normanton and Karumba. The dump points guide has more.
tips: Boodjamulla: book ahead from March to October
Camp 50 m from the water's edge

sections.heading: Plan the Cairns to Darwin drive in AussieCamps
body: Plan it as a trip in AussieCamps: add the nights in order and it shows the distance and drive time of each leg, with a forecast for the day you plan to arrive. AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and the rest areas and dump points above show the facilities those sources publish.

Stored place details, saved places and guides work with no signal. Map tiles, routing, weather and photos need a connection, and there is long distance without coverage on both routes, so open the trip in range before each long leg. AussieCamps runs on iPhone only, and it is free to download, with in-app purchases.
tips: Open the trip before the long legs

faq: How far is it to drive from Cairns to Darwin?

About 2,900 km by the sealed main route through Townsville, Cloncurry, Mount Isa and the Barkly and Stuart Highways, by OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data. The Savannah Way direct is about 2,400 to 2,500 km, but part of it is unsealed and suits a 4WD.
Is the Savannah Way sealed?

Partly. The Savannah Way tourism body says the route uses sealed and unsealed roads, with sealed roads from Borroloola onwards, and that a 4WD is needed. A 2019 visitor guide describes the roads from Normanton to Burketown and beyond as largely unsealed, so check each section before you go.
Can I drive from Cairns to Darwin in the wet season?

Not reliably on the Gulf roads. The Savannah Way says sections are closed during the wet season, December to March, and that access in April and May depends on rainfall easing, with May to October the best time. Tourism NT says some roads may be closed by flooding from November to April.
Is there a time change between Queensland and the Northern Territory?

Yes. The Northern Territory is on central time and Queensland on eastern time, and neither uses daylight saving, so the Territory is half an hour behind Queensland all year and your clock goes back half an hour at the border.

perth-to-exmouth-drive.title: Perth to Exmouth Drive 2026: Route, Fuel Gaps, Stops and Ningaloo Campsites
perth-to-exmouth-drive.description: Perth to Exmouth is about 1,260 to 1,280 km and 15 hours of driving, usually over three days. Route options, the 475 km Geraldton to Carnarvon stretch, cyclone recovery, fruit rules, Ningaloo camping and dump points.
perth-to-exmouth-drive.imageAlt: A sandy Ningaloo coast beach at sunset, with a low reef offshore and dunes with low scrub behind
perth-to-exmouth-drive.intro: Perth to Exmouth is about 1,260 to 1,280 km, which is 1,256 km and 14 h 54 min by OSRM routing, all in Western Australia. The usual route is Brand Highway to Geraldton, then the North West Coastal Highway to Carnarvon and the Minilya to Exmouth Road, and it works as a three-day drive.

sections.heading: Perth to Exmouth routes compared
body: The main route follows the Brand Highway north from Perth to Geraldton, the North West Coastal Highway to the Minilya turn-off, then the Minilya to Exmouth Road. Wikipedia describes the North West Coastal Highway as a sealed two-lane single carriageway, mostly signed at 110 km/h, with 50, 60 or 70 km/h in built-up areas. A Kalbarri detour goes from Geraldton through Northampton to Kalbarri and rejoins the highway near the Overlander Roadhouse junction. An inland option runs up the Great Northern Highway through Bindoon and Dalwallinu to Geraldton, and Main Roads WA's rest area guide has a separate map for it.

All figures here are from OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data, computed on 21 October 2026, for a car with no stops and no caravan. No road authority publishes a Perth to Exmouth total, so treat them as a guide. Main Roads WA gives Geraldton to Carnarvon as 475 km, and by OSRM the Kalbarri detour is 401 km from Geraldton to the Overlander junction, against 279 km direct, so about 120 km extra.
