sections.heading: The drive in three days
body: A three-day split is Perth to Geraldton, about 417 km and 5 h 3 min, Geraldton to Carnarvon, 475 km by Main Roads WA, and Carnarvon to Exmouth, about 364 km and 4 h 14 min. The legs by OSRM are Perth to Jurien Bay 218 km (2 h 42 min), Jurien Bay to Geraldton 199 km (2 h 21 min), Geraldton to the Overlander junction 279 km (3 h 18 min), Overlander to Carnarvon 197 km (2 h 16 min), Carnarvon to Minilya 140 km (1 h 39 min), Minilya to Coral Bay 98 km (1 h 9 min) and Coral Bay to Exmouth 152 km (1 h 47 min).

A longer trip adds a night at Jurien Bay or Cervantes on the first day, and one at Coral Bay on the third. The Minilya to Exmouth Road leaves the highway about 7 km north of Minilya Roadhouse, according to Wikipedia. The Perth to Broome road trip guide covers the coast north of Carnarvon, so this guide stays with Exmouth.

sections.heading: Where to stop and where to take a break
body: No caravan park at Geraldton, Carnarvon or Jurien Bay could be confirmed on an operator page for this guide, so none is named: use the local visitor centres and ring ahead. Australia's Coral Coast says Coral Bay Peoples Park and Ningaloo Coral Bay (Bayview) are open, and a camping blog says Coral Bay has just two caravan parks that book out, so check availability. At Exmouth the same page lists RAC Exmouth Cape Holiday Park as partially open and Exmouth Escape Resort, Ningaloo Lodge Exmouth, Sal Salis Ningaloo Reef and Camp Easy Ningaloo as open.

The AussieCamps data lists campgrounds on the Ningaloo coast, 7 to 10 km off the route at Warroora: Sandy Point (Nyinggulu), Stans Camp overflow camping, The Ridge and 14 Mile, with Bruboodjoo about 8 km off the route further north. DBCA says 14 Mile sites 12 to 28 are closed and the whole campground closes from 1 January 2027 for cyclone recovery works. Rest areas in the data for a break include Nilgen near Gingin, Galena North and South near Northampton, Nerren Nerren, and Edagee and Yalabia near Carnarvon. Main Roads WA says its 24-hour rest areas are not intended for camping, and stopping should not exceed 24 consecutive hours. The rest area guide and the Western Australia rules guide cover this.
tips: Ring ahead for Geraldton and Carnarvon parks
Rest areas are for a break

sections.heading: Fuel gaps
body: The longest stretch without a town is Geraldton to Carnarvon, 475 km by Main Roads WA. Wikipedia says the only settlements over that stretch, apart from Northampton, are four roadhouses: Binnu, Billabong, Overlander and Wooramel. Fuel availability and opening hours at each roadhouse could not be confirmed, so fill up at Geraldton and ask at Billabong and Overlander about the next stop.

North of Carnarvon, Minilya Roadhouse is the only roadhouse before the Exmouth turn-off, about 140 km from Carnarvon by OSRM. Fuel at Coral Bay could not be confirmed, and Exmouth is a further 152 km from there. Main Roads WA says to carry extra fuel on long distances and enough food and water for two to three days past your intended travel time, and it notes that stops can be limited. The fuel planning guide shows how to budget the distance, and UHF channel 40 is the road user channel on this route in Main Roads WA's 2015 rest area guide.
tips: Minilya is the only roadhouse before the turn-off
Carry food and water for 2 to 3 days extra

sections.heading: Road conditions, cyclones and recovery
body: Check the Main Roads WA Travel Map or ring 138 138 before each leg. Main Roads WA says the wet season in the north of WA generally runs from November to April, and the Bureau of Meteorology's tropical cyclone season runs from 1 November to 30 April. Severe Tropical Cyclone Narelle hit the Gascoyne coast on 27 March 2026. Main Roads WA announced on 8 April 2026 that it had lifted road restrictions into Exmouth, and Australia's Coral Coast says the North West Coastal Highway reopened from the south into Carnarvon on 31 March.

The Shire of Exmouth says the town is re-open to visitors, that accommodation options remain limited as recovery and rebuilding continues, and that visitors should confirm with their accommodation provider before arrival. It also says Horizon Power has scheduled outages across the town. A Shire emergency overflow camping facility opened on 29 April 2026 for self-contained campers, according to Australia's Coral Coast. The Shire's phone number is (08) 9949 3000. Main Roads WA warns that many major rural highways are unfenced and to watch for animals at dusk and dawn, and to overtake road trains only on a long straight stretch that is completely clear. The road trains guide covers etiquette.
tips: Main Roads WA Travel Map or 138 138

sections.heading: Fruit rules and the Carnarvon request
body: Perth to Exmouth is entirely in Western Australia, so there is no state border and no interstate checkpoint on this drive. The Shire of Carnarvon page says Medfly is present in all parts of Western Australia except the Ord River Irrigation Area. It asks visitors from elsewhere in the state not to bring fruit or vegetables: either eat it or dispose of your fruit before you arrive in Carnarvon, or better yet, buy as you go. It says to bag any fruit and use the yellow rubbish bins in the parking bays outside the town. The page mentions no road checkpoint and no formal restriction, so it is the Shire's request.

No current Perth fruit fly notice or formal Gascoyne movement order for travellers could be confirmed, so check DPIRD (dpird.wa.gov.au) before you leave. The interstate biosecurity guide covers the rules that apply when you cross a state border instead.
tips: Shire of Carnarvon asks: no fruit
Use the yellow bins outside town

sections.heading: Cape Range, Ningaloo camping and dump points
body: Cape Range National Park entry is $17.00 per standard vehicle and $10.00 for a concession, according to Explore Parks WA, and a valid park pass covers the fees. The page says no dogs or other pets are allowed in the park. DBCA says to book Ningaloo Coast campsites at parkstay.dbca.wa.gov.au, with bookings opening at 10:00am AWST on the first Tuesday of the month. Its guide lists stays in June 2027 opening on 1 December 2026 and July 2027 opening on 5 January 2027. The maximum stay is up to 14 nights if any night is in a WA school holiday, and up to 28 nights otherwise.

ParkStay shows the Nyinggulara National Park campsites at Janes Bay, North Lefroy, Point Billie, South Lefroy and Winderabandi closed until further notice. The Yardie Creek crossing to Boat Harbour and One K needs a low tide, according to ParkStay listings, and a DBCA note from 21 April 2026 gave 1 August as the estimated reopening for Boat Harbour and One K, so check current status. For dump points, the AussieCamps data lists Cadiz Street in Cervantes and Hampton Gardens in Northampton, both free, and rest areas at Nilgen, Galena, Nerren Nerren, Edagee and Yalabia list one. Main Roads WA says blackwater may only be disposed of in rest areas displaying the dump point sign or at the nearest town's dump site. The dump points guide has more.

sections.heading: Plan the Perth to Exmouth drive in AussieCamps
body: Plan it as a trip in AussieCamps: add the nights in order and it shows the distance and drive time of each leg, with a forecast for the day you plan to arrive. AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and the rest areas and dump points above show the facilities those sources publish.

Stored place details, saved places and guides work with no signal. Map tiles, routing, weather and photos need a connection, and the long stretches north of Geraldton have little coverage, so open the trip in range before each leg. AussieCamps runs on iPhone only, and it is free to download, with in-app purchases.
tips: Open the trip before the long legs

faq: How far is it from Perth to Exmouth?

About 1,260 to 1,280 km, which is 1,256 km and 14 h 54 min of driving by OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data via Jurien Bay, Geraldton, Carnarvon and the Minilya to Exmouth Road. Most people take three days, with nights at Geraldton and Carnarvon.
Is there a long stretch without towns?

Yes. Main Roads WA gives Geraldton to Carnarvon as 475 km, and Wikipedia says that apart from Northampton, 50 km out, the only settlements on the stretch are four roadhouses. Fill up in Geraldton and check each roadhouse is open.
Can I take fruit to Carnarvon?

The Shire of Carnarvon asks you not to. Its page says to eat or dispose of your fruit before you arrive, or buy as you go, and to use the yellow bins in the parking bays outside the town. It describes this as a request, and it mentions no road checkpoint.
Are the Ningaloo campgrounds open after Cyclone Narelle?

Some are not. DBCA says all Ningaloo Coast campgrounds were affected by Severe Tropical Cyclone Narelle in 2026, and ParkStay shows the Nyinggulara National Park campsites closed until further notice. Check ParkStay before you book.

broome-to-darwin-drive.title: Broome to Darwin Drive 2026: Kimberley Route, Fuel Gaps, Stops and Border Rules
broome-to-darwin-drive.description: Broome to Darwin is about 1,880 km and 21 hours on sealed highways, usually five days. Fuel gaps, Kununurra and Katherine stops, wet season closures, the WA/NT border checkpoint and dump points.
broome-to-darwin-drive.imageAlt: A giant boab tree inside a low fence at a rest area on the Great Northern Highway in the Kimberley, with red dirt in front of it
broome-to-darwin-drive.intro: Broome to Darwin is about 1,880 km, which is 1,874 km and 20 h 54 min by OSRM routing, and it is sealed all the way on the Great Northern, Victoria and Stuart Highways. A five-day drive puts nights at Fitzroy Crossing, Halls Creek, Kununurra and Katherine, and the leg to Darwin is the last 314 km.

sections.heading: Broome to Darwin routes compared
body: There is one sealed through route. The Great Northern Highway runs from Broome through Fitzroy Crossing and Halls Creek to the junction with the Victoria Highway, which crosses the WA/NT border and runs to Katherine. The Stuart Highway then goes north to Darwin. Visit Kununurra says Kununurra is 46 km along the Victoria Highway from that junction, so the town is a detour off the line, and the OSRM figure below is routed through it.

The Gibb River Road from Derby to Kununurra is an unsealed 4WD alternative that Main Roads WA lists on its own rest area map. It is not a shortcut for caravans, and no distance is taken here. The Gibb River Road guide covers it. Sandfire Roadhouse is on the Perth to Broome side, so it is not a stop on this drive. All figures are from OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data, computed on 21 October 2026, for a car with no stops. No road authority publishes a Broome to Darwin total.
tips: Sealed all the way on the main route

sections.heading: The drive in five days
body: By OSRM routing, the legs are Broome to Fitzroy Crossing 398 km (4 h 38 min), Fitzroy Crossing to Halls Creek 290 km (3 h 25 min), Halls Creek to Kununurra 358 km (4 h 12 min), Kununurra to Timber Creek 228 km (2 h 22 min), Timber Creek to Katherine 285 km (2 h 50 min) and Katherine to Darwin 314 km (3 h 25 min). Main Roads WA's 2015 rest area guide gives Fitzroy Crossing to Halls Creek as 289 km and Halls Creek to Kununurra as 359 km, which matches OSRM within a kilometre.

A five-day split is Broome to Fitzroy Crossing, Fitzroy Crossing to Halls Creek, Halls Creek to Kununurra, Kununurra to Katherine through Timber Creek (about 513 km, 5 h 12 min), then Katherine to Darwin. The middle two legs can be combined into one long day of 648 km, about 7 h 37 min. The Darwin to Alice Springs guide covers the Stuart Highway south of Katherine, and the Darwin, Kakadu and Litchfield guide covers the area around the end of the drive.

sections.heading: Where to stop and where to take a break
body: At Kununurra, Hidden Valley Kununurra Caravan Park sits next to Mirima National Park, according to its operator, Summerstar Tourist Parks. At Timber Creek, tourism listings name Timber Creek Hotel and Caravan Park and WIRIB Tourism Park. No named park in Fitzroy Crossing, Halls Creek or Katherine could be confirmed on an operator page for this guide, so ring ahead and use the visitor centres. Doon Doon Roadhouse and Warmun (Turkey Creek) are roadhouses with camping between Halls Creek and Kununurra, according to search extracts of tourism listings. Warmun is about 160 km from Halls Creek.

The AussieCamps data lists three Gregory National Park campgrounds in the Northern Territory, each with a camping fee: Big Horse Creek, about 0.3 km off the route, Sullivan Creek, about 0.1 km off, and Gumil, about 5 km off. These are national park campgrounds, not caravan parks. Rest areas in the data for a break are Cockburn in Western Australia, and Saddle Creek, Mathison Creek and Bridge Creek in the Northern Territory. Main Roads WA says its 24-hour rest areas are not intended for camping. The Northern Territory says no more than 24 hours at any one rest area. The rest area guide has the rules by state.
tips: Parks: ring ahead at Fitzroy, Halls Creek, Katherine
Gregory campgrounds have a camping fee
Rest areas are for a break

sections.heading: Fuel gaps
body: Australia's North West says fuel outlets are at Broome, Roebuck Roadhouse, Willare Bridge, Fitzroy Crossing, Halls Creek, Warmun, Wyndham and Kununurra, and that the greatest distance between fuel outlets on the Great Northern Highway is 295 km between Fitzroy Crossing and Halls Creek. Main Roads WA gives that stretch as 289 km. Halls Creek to Kununurra is 359 km, with Warmun in between. Whether Doon Doon sells fuel today could not be confirmed.

East of Kununurra, it is 228 km to Timber Creek and a further 91 km to Victoria River Roadhouse, by OSRM, and Katherine is 195 km beyond that. A tourism listing calls Victoria River Roadhouse the main fuel, food and drink stop, but fuel at Timber Creek and Victoria River Roadhouse could not be confirmed on an operator page, so fill up at Kununurra and ask again at both. Main Roads WA says to carry extra fuel on long distances and enough food and water for two to three days past your intended travel time. The fuel planning guide shows how to budget the distance.
tips: Fitzroy to Halls Creek: 289 to 295 km
Carry food and water for 2 to 3 days extra

sections.heading: Wet season, road conditions and speed limits
body: Check the Main Roads WA Travel Map (travelmap.mainroads.wa.gov.au, 138 138) and Road Report NT (roadreport.nt.gov.au) before each day, as Visit Kununurra recommends. Main Roads WA says the wet season in the north of WA generally runs from November to April. Wikipedia says the Victoria River crossing near Timber Creek is flood-prone from November to April, that floodwater can cut the link for days or weeks, and that a replacement bridge completed in May 2008 is 7 m higher but floods of roughly one-in-twenty-year size will still overtop it. Main Roads WA flood updates describe the new Fitzroy River Bridge opening in late 2023, after the original was badly damaged in early 2023. No current closure was confirmed for 21 October 2026. The wet season guide covers cyclones and crocodiles.

In the Northern Territory the default speed limit is 110 km/h unless a sign says otherwise, and some signposted sections of the Stuart and Victoria Highways allow 130 km/h, so the sign decides. Main Roads WA says to overtake road trains only on a long straight stretch that is completely clear, and not to cut in front of them. Many major rural highways in WA are unfenced, so watch for animals at dusk and dawn. The road trains guide covers etiquette.
tips: Travel Map and Road Report NT

sections.heading: Border rules and the clock change
body: Visit Kununurra says there is no border checkpoint when leaving Western Australia to enter the Northern Territory, so a driver from Broome is not stopped. The DPIRD checkpoint page lists the WA/NT Road Checkpoint on the Victoria Highway at Lake Argyle, operating 24 hours, every day of the year, on 08 9168 7354, and that checkpoint checks traffic entering WA. DPIRD says generally no fresh fruit and vegetables are allowed into Western Australia except the items it lists, so read its page on the drive back. The Shire of Carnarvon says Medfly is present in all parts of WA except the Ord River Irrigation Area near Kununurra, so check DPIRD before carrying fruit and vegetables into Kununurra. No Northern Territory rule for travellers entering from WA was researched for this guide, so check the interstate biosecurity guide.
The Northern Territory is on central time and Western Australia on western time. Neither uses daylight saving, so the Northern Territory is 1.5 hours ahead of Western Australia all year.
tips: NT is 1.5 hours ahead of WA

sections.heading: Parks, Lake Argyle and dump points
body: Nitmiluk (Katherine Gorge) is about 30 km from Katherine, and entry needs an NT Parks Pass, with Northern Territory residents exempt. Camping there is booked and paid in advance. Lake Argyle Resort and Caravan Park is at the end of a sealed road, about 35 km off the highway, and tourism sources put the turn-off about 35 km east of Kununurra. Purnululu (the Bungle Bungles) is reached by the 53 km Spring Creek Track off the Great Northern Highway, which is 4WD high clearance only and a dry season trip, so check DBCA for the opening dates. The Gibb River Road guide covers the Kimberley 4WD routes.

For dump points, the AussieCamps data lists Cockburn rest area in Western Australia, and in the Northern Territory Victoria River Roadhouse, Mathison Rest Area at Delamere, which lists a washout tap, Limestone Creek near Manbulloo, two in Katherine, Pine Creek, Adelaide River and Coomalie Creek RV Park, then Batchelor and Darwin Greyhound Club at Winnellie. That is the data's coverage, not every dump point. The dump points guide has more.
tips: Dump points are the data's coverage

sections.heading: Plan the Broome to Darwin drive in AussieCamps
body: Plan it as a trip in AussieCamps: add the nights in order and it shows the distance and drive time of each leg, with a forecast for the day you plan to arrive. AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and the rest areas and dump points above show the facilities those sources publish.

Each place page has a weather forecast and the places nearby. Stored place details, saved places and guides work with no signal. Map tiles, routing, weather and photos need a connection, and the Kimberley has long stretches without coverage, so open the trip in range before each leg. AussieCamps runs on iPhone only, and it is free to download, with in-app purchases.
tips: Open the trip before the long legs

faq: How far is it from Broome to Darwin?

About 1,880 km, which is 1,874 km and 20 h 54 min of driving by OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data through Fitzroy Crossing, Halls Creek, Kununurra, Timber Creek and Katherine. Most people take five days.
What is the longest gap between fuel stops?

Australia's North West says the greatest distance between fuel outlets on the Great Northern Highway is 295 km between Fitzroy Crossing and Halls Creek. Main Roads WA gives that stretch as 289 km. Ask at Timber Creek and Victoria River Roadhouse about the next fuel as well.
Is there a quarantine checkpoint on the way to Darwin?

Not leaving Western Australia. Visit Kununurra says there is no border checkpoint when leaving WA to enter the Northern Territory. The 24-hour WA/NT road checkpoint on the Victoria Highway checks traffic entering WA, so it matters on the drive back.
Can I drive Broome to Darwin in the wet season?

Roads can close. Main Roads WA says the wet season in the north of WA generally runs from November to April, and Wikipedia says the Victoria River crossing near Timber Creek can be cut for days or weeks by floods. Check the Travel Map and Road Report NT.

adelaide-to-melbourne-drive.title: Adelaide to Melbourne Drive 2026: Inland Route, Coastal Option, Border Rules and Stops
adelaide-to-melbourne-drive.description: Adelaide to Melbourne is about 730 km and 9 hours on the Dukes and Western Highways. Inland and coastal routes compared, with stops, rest areas, fruit rules, roadworks and dump points.
adelaide-to-melbourne-drive.imageAlt: The A8 Dukes Highway north of Ki Ki in South Australia, with mallee scrub, green paddocks and cloud above the road
adelaide-to-melbourne-drive.intro: Adelaide to Melbourne is about 730 km and 9 h 10 min to 9 h 45 min of driving on the inland route, by OSRM routing: the Dukes Highway to the border, then the Western Highway through Horsham and Ballarat. Most drivers split it with a night at Horsham or Nhill, and the coastal alternative through Mount Gambier is about 874 km and 11 h 20 min of driving before any detour.

sections.heading: Adelaide to Melbourne routes compared
body: The inland route leaves Adelaide on the South Eastern Freeway, takes the Princes Highway across the Murray at Murray Bridge to Tailem Bend, then follows the Dukes Highway (A8) through Coonalpyn, Tintinara, Keith and Bordertown. Wikipedia describes the Dukes Highway as 190 km from Tailem Bend to the border, mostly one lane each way with 36 overtaking lanes. It becomes the Western Highway at the Victorian border, which runs through Kaniva, Nhill, Horsham, Stawell, Ararat and Ballarat to Melbourne.

The coastal route follows the Princes Highway through Mount Gambier, Warrnambool and Geelong, and the Great Ocean Road adds a further detour between Warrnambool and Torquay. This guide does not repeat that route: the Melbourne to Adelaide coastal route guide covers the Limestone Coast, the Coorong and the camping. Every distance and drive time below comes from OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data, run on 21 October 2026 for a car driving straight through.
tips: Inland: the quickest and the most direct
Coastal: about 150 km longer, and slower
Great Ocean Road: a detour, not a shortcut

sections.heading: The inland route in one or two days
body: By OSRM routing, Adelaide to Murray Bridge is about 76 km (1 h 2 min), Tailem Bend about 24 km further, Keith about 130 km after that and Bordertown about 46 km on. Across the border it is about 44 km to Kaniva, 39 km to Nhill, 75 km to Horsham, 67 km to Stawell, 31 km to Ararat, 94 km to Ballarat and 114 km to Melbourne. Adelaide to Horsham adds up to about 434 km (5 h 36 min), which is why Horsham is the usual night.

Horsham Riverside Caravan Park, at 190 Firebrace Street, is listed by Visit Wimmera Mallee with a dump point, drive-through sites, a camp kitchen and laundry. Nhill Holiday Park, at 93 Victoria Street on the Western Highway, is run by Hindmarsh Shire Council with powered, unpowered and ensuite sites booked online. Confirm availability with each park. The AussieCamps data lists free Victorian rest areas at Serviceton, Lawloit near Nhill, Pink Lake near Dimboola, Green Lake, Golton, Deep Lead and Bungaree, each with toilets, drinking water, picnic tables and barbecues. It lists none in South Australia on this road, which is a gap in the data. Treat rest areas as a place for a break and see the guide on overnight stays and the camping rules guides before you sleep at one.

sections.heading: Western Highway roadworks and speed limits
body: The Victorian Big Build page, as shown in search extracts of its pages and a May 2026 government release, lists the 55 km from Ballarat to Buangor as complete and duplicated. It says Buangor to Ararat, about 12 km, will start construction before the end of 2026, with all works expected by mid-2029 subject to approvals, and Ararat to Stawell is at the initial planning stage. The Stawell Times reported in March 2026 that no completion date was confirmed for the stretch west of Buangor.

The same sources say interim safety measures, including reduced speed limits and better signage, are in place between Buangor and Ararat. The extracts do not give the limits, so this guide does not quote a number: follow the posted signs. Wikipedia says the Western Highway is the second-busiest national highway in Australia for freight, with more than 4,000 freight vehicles a day at Anthony's Cutting, so expect trucks on the single carriageway sections. The South Eastern Freeway out of Adelaide has its own rule: Wikipedia says vehicles with five or more axles must keep left and slow to 60 km/h between the Crafers Interchange and the old tollhouse.
tips: Buangor to Ararat: construction due before the end of 2026

sections.heading: Camping and side trips off the highway
body: Mount Buangor State Park sits on the Western Highway at Buangor, and the AussieCamps data lists its Ferntree, Bailes and Middle Creek camping areas from Parks Victoria, with toilets and drinking water at each. Further west, the data lists the Grampians National Park campgrounds at Stapylton, Coppermine and Troopers Creek, and Ackle Bend Camping Area in Little Desert National Park. Fees are not in the data, so check Parks Victoria before you book.

The Grampians and Little Desert are detours from the highway of different lengths, so they suit a second day rather than a fast run. If you want a longer trip with the coast one way and the Grampians the other, the Melbourne to Adelaide coastal route guide lays out the comparison.
tips: Grampians and Little Desert: plan a detour

sections.heading: Fuel, services and dump points
body: No road authority or operator source checked gives a fuel gap on this route, so no figure should be taken from the OSRM legs, which only show distance between the towns used as waypoints. The longest of those is Tailem Bend to Keith at about 130 km, and Melbourne to Ballarat is about 114 km. Fill up in the larger towns, such as Murray Bridge, Keith, Bordertown, Nhill, Horsham, Stawell, Ararat and Ballarat, rather than waiting for the last town before a long stretch. Work out your fuel budget for the full distance with the road trip fuel guide.

The AussieCamps data lists dump points at Mount Barker Recreation Grounds and Callington Oval, each with a washout tap, and at Coonalpyn Caravan Park with none listed. In Victoria it lists Scallan Street Car Park in Stawell and Green Hill Lake Camping in Ararat, each with a washout tap. Horsham Riverside Caravan Park lists its own dump point. That is only the data's coverage, so check the dump points guide for the rest.
tips: Fill up at Keith, Nhill, Horsham and Stawell
Do not wait for the last town
Mount Barker, Callington, Stawell and Ararat list a washout tap

sections.heading: Road conditions, tolls and the clock
body: Check Traffic SA for the South Australian section and VicTraffic for Victoria. VicEmergency carries fire warnings and emergency incidents, and a tourism page for the Great Ocean Road says the commonest closure there is rockfall between Lorne and Apollo Bay after heavy rain, so check before taking the coast.

In Melbourne, Linkt says its Visitor's Pass covers CityLink and EastLink for up to 30 days, with an opening fee of $3.50 online or $5.00 by phone, and covers CityLink trips made up to 5 days ago and EastLink trips made up to 3 days ago. Whether your route into Melbourne uses a toll road depends on where you are going, so check before you leave. South Australia and Victoria both observe daylight saving, which began on Sunday 4 October 2026 and ends on Sunday 4 April 2027. South Australia is 30 minutes behind Victoria all year, so put your watch forward half an hour at the border.
tips: Linkt Visitor's Pass covers Melbourne tolls

sections.heading: Fruit and vegetables at the border
body: None of the sources checked describes a fruit fly checkpoint on the Victorian side. Agriculture Victoria asks people travelling to Victoria from South Australia and Western Australia not to bring fruit or fruiting vegetables, to keep Mediterranean fruit fly out of the state, which Victoria is free from. That is a request, from a search extract of its page that blocks scripts, so check Agriculture Victoria on 136 186. The Interstate Quarantine site lists no fruit fly zone for Victoria, and says signs on major roads show when you are entering a Phylloxera Exclusion Zone. It also says quarantine stations and fruit disposal bins are placed throughout South Australia and that mobile quarantine stations can operate anywhere in the state at any time.

The stricter rules apply the other way. The Melbourne to Adelaide coastal route guide and the interstate biosecurity guide cover them, and PIRSA says that for travellers from Victoria fresh fruit is not permitted into South Australia, while processed, dried, preserved, cooked, frozen and canned fruit and vegetables are allowed. The Riverland rules are separate and not on this route.
tips: Eat fresh fruit before you cross
Victoria: a request, not a stated ban

sections.heading: Plan the Adelaide to Melbourne drive in AussieCamps
body: Plan it as a trip in AussieCamps: add the stops in order, Keith or Nhill, Horsham and a campground at Mount Buangor or the Grampians, and it shows the distance and drive time of each leg with a forecast for the day you plan to arrive. AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, including the Parks Victoria campgrounds above, and a place page shows the facilities those sources publish.

Place details, saved places and guides stay readable with no signal. Map tiles, routing, weather and photos need a connection, so open the trip before you leave Tailem Bend. The app is iPhone only and free to download, with in-app purchases.
tips: Add each overnight stop in order
Open the trip before the long stretches

faq: How long does it take to drive from Adelaide to Melbourne?

About 730 km and 9 h 10 min to 9 h 45 min of driving on the Dukes Highway and Western Highway, by OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data, depending on the waypoints used. Most drivers split it with a night at Horsham or Nhill, because a day of driving plus fuel and rest stops is long.
Is the Adelaide to Melbourne drive on one highway?

Nearly. The A8 runs from Tailem Bend as the Dukes Highway, becomes the Western Highway at the border, then joins the Western Freeway at Buangor for the dual carriageway into Melbourne. Wikipedia describes the Dukes Highway as mostly one lane each way, and the Western Highway as single carriageway from the border to just west of Buangor.
Can I take fruit from South Australia into Victoria?

Agriculture Victoria, in a search extract of its medfly page, asks people travelling to Victoria from South Australia and Western Australia not to bring fruit or fruiting vegetables, to keep Mediterranean fruit fly out. It is described as a request. The Interstate Quarantine site lists no fruit fly zone for Victoria. Eat or leave behind fresh fruit and fruiting vegetables before you cross, and check Agriculture Victoria on 136 186.
Is the Western Highway being upgraded?

Yes. The Victorian Big Build page lists Ballarat to Buangor as complete, Buangor to Ararat as due to start construction before the end of 2026 with all works expected by mid-2029, and Ararat to Stawell in early planning. Reduced speed limits have been installed between Buangor and Ararat as an interim measure, so watch the signs.

brisbane-to-cairns-drive.title: Brisbane to Cairns Drive 2026: Bruce Highway Legs, Flood Season, Fatigue and Fuel
brisbane-to-cairns-drive.description: Brisbane to Cairns is about 1,700 km and 22 hours on the Bruce Highway. Daily legs, the inland variant, wet-season closures, fire ant rules, rest areas and dump points.
brisbane-to-cairns-drive.imageAlt: The Bruce Highway approaching Tully in North Queensland, with steam rising from the sugar mill and low cloud over the hills
brisbane-to-cairns-drive.intro: Brisbane to Cairns is about 1,700 km and 22 hours of driving on the Bruce Highway, by OSRM routing, which five legs of 300 to 400 km keep to about five hours a day. The only inland alternative leaves the Bruce at Rockhampton and adds about 245 km, and the cyclone and flood season from November to April matters more than the route.

sections.heading: Brisbane to Cairns routes compared
body: The Bruce Highway is the route almost everyone drives. Wikipedia gives it as about 1,679 km, entirely sealed, dual carriageway from Brisbane to Curra, where the Gympie bypass opened on 15 October 2024, and mostly two lanes north of there. The limit is 110 km/h from Caboolture to Curra, generally 100 km/h between Maryborough and Rockhampton, and lower through towns such as Childers, Gin Gin and Miriam Vale. It runs through Gympie, Bundaberg, Gladstone, Rockhampton, Mackay, Bowen, Townsville, Ingham and Innisfail to Cairns.

The inland variant leaves the Bruce at Rockhampton, takes the Capricorn Highway to Emerald, the Gregory Highway to Clermont and the Gregory Developmental Road to Charters Towers, then the Flinders Highway to Townsville and the Bruce on to Cairns. Wikipedia says the Gregory route is used by many road trains, and none of the sources checked says how much of it is sealed, so this guide does not call it a fast road. OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data supplied the distances and times here, computed on 21 October 2026 for a car that does not stop.
tips: Bruce Highway: sealed all the way

sections.heading: Five daily legs
body: By OSRM routing, five legs keep each day to about five hours of driving. Brisbane to Bundaberg is about 362 km (4 h 42 min), Bundaberg to Rockhampton about 294 km (4 h 1 min), Rockhampton to Mackay about 335 km (4 h 16 min), Mackay to Townsville about 396 km (5 h 17 min) and Townsville to Cairns about 347 km (4 h 45 min). The longest of those, Mackay to Townsville, passes Proserpine and Bowen.

The camping and sights on this road are already in the Brisbane to Cape Tribulation guide and the Sydney to Cairns guide, so this guide does not repeat them. The AussieCamps data lists Queensland Parks and Wildlife campgrounds close to the route at Wongi Waterholes near Maryborough, Alligator Creek at Mount Elliot near Townsville, Big Crystal Creek in the Mount Spec section and Jourama Falls near Ingham. Fees are not in the data, so check the camping rules guide for Queensland and book through the park agency.

sections.heading: Wet season, floods and cyclones
body: Get Ready Queensland says the state's cyclone season officially runs from 1 November to 30 April, and cyclones can occur at other times. A Queensland road closure document, as shown in a search extract, says that during the Wet, from November to April, areas across Queensland can have flooding and landslips. Wikipedia says the Bruce Highway is prone to frequent flooding in a number of places, and that the Goorganga Plains south of Proserpine can be closed for days.

Transport and Main Roads, in a project page extract, says flooding closes the Bruce Highway at one or more places on the 16 km between Ingham and Innisfail about every two years in the wet season, often more than once, and the Gairloch floodway usually closes first. No source checked shows a closure for today, so check QLDTraffic and do not drive through floodwater. If your dates fall between November and April, keep a spare day in the plan.
tips: Ingham to Innisfail floods in most wet seasons

sections.heading: Fatigue, rest stops and dump points
body: Queensland guidance in police and Transport and Main Roads statements is to take a break every two hours at a rest area or Driver Reviver site. The same extracts say to stop if you are drowsy, find it hard to keep your head up or cannot remember the last few minutes of driving. Some Driver Reviver sites are being handed to local councils or closed while staying open as rest areas, so use QLDTraffic, which lists rest areas and heavy vehicle rest areas, rather than a site list from an old guide.

The AussieCamps data lists one rest area in the corridor, Babinda rest area north of Innisfail, with toilets, drinking water, a shelter and picnic tables. That is a gap in the data, not a count of rest areas on the Bruce. The road trip fatigue and wildlife guide covers dusk and dawn driving, and the guide on overnight stays covers whether you can sleep at a rest area.

The AussieCamps data lists dump points at Wyllie Park in Petrie, Alf Larson Lions Park in Miriam Vale, the Tourist Information Centre in Curtis Park at Allenstown near Rockhampton, Cedric Archer Park in Gracemere, Railway Square in Sarina, Bluewater Park at Bluewater and the Hinchinbrook Visitor Information Centre in Ingham. Wyllie Park, Curtis Park, Cedric Archer Park and Bluewater Park list a washout tap. That is only the data's coverage, and QLDTraffic also has a dump point layer, so check the dump points guide and the map before a long leg.
tips: Dump points: Petrie, Rockhampton and Bluewater list a washout tap

sections.heading: Fuel and services
body: No road authority or operator source checked gives a fuel gap on the Bruce Highway, so no figure should be taken from the OSRM legs, which show only the distance between the towns used as waypoints. The longest of those is Rockhampton to Mackay at about 335 km, and it passes through towns, so fill up in the larger centres such as Gympie, Bundaberg, Gladstone, Rockhampton, Mackay, Proserpine, Townsville and Ingham rather than running low. On the inland variant, Clermont to Charters Towers is about 391 km with no waypoint between, which is distance only and not a confirmed fuel gap, so ask in Clermont and fill up there. Use the road trip fuel guide to budget fuel for that distance.
tips: Fill up in the larger towns
Do not run low between centres

sections.heading: Road conditions, QLDTraffic and tolls
body: QLDTraffic, from Transport and Main Roads, shows traffic alerts for crashes, hazards, flooding and roadworks, flood cameras, rest areas, dump points, truck restrictions and the BOM rain radar. A Queensland Government extract gives 13 19 40 as its phone line. Check it each morning, and again at midday in the wet season.

The sources checked do not describe a toll on the Bruce Highway north of Brisbane. Whether your route out of Brisbane uses a Brisbane toll road depends on where you start, so check the operator before you leave.

sections.heading: Fire ants when leaving Brisbane
body: Queensland's fire ant biosecurity zones were updated from 15 April 2026 and cover parts of the Logan, Gold Coast, Moreton Bay, Lockyer Valley, Scenic Rim and Sunshine Coast council areas. The Biosecurity Regulation 2016 sets procedures for moving or storing fire ant carriers from within the zones, and a biosecurity instrument permit is needed if you cannot meet them. A summary of the zones lists baled hay or straw, manure, mulch, potted plants, quarry and mining materials, soil and turf as carriers, and says ants can hitch a ride in equipment or materials that have been in contact with soil or stored outdoors.

The search extracts do not mention caravans, campervans or camping gear, and the fireants.org.au pages block scripts, so this guide cannot say how the controls apply to them. Zones are reviewed monthly, so check the zone map and movement rules on fireants.org.au for the suburb you start from.
tips: Soil, mulch, hay, turf, potted plants: carriers
Check the map for your suburb

sections.heading: Plan the Brisbane to Cairns drive in AussieCamps
body: Plan it as a trip in AussieCamps: add the five overnight stops in order, and it shows the distance and drive time of each leg with a forecast for the day you plan to arrive. AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and a place page shows the facilities, rules and RV sites those sources publish, as on the Cape Hillsborough National Park page near Mackay.

With no signal, place details, saved places and guides still open on the phone. Map tiles, routing, weather and photos need a connection, so open the trip before you leave town. AussieCamps is an iPhone app, free to download, with in-app purchases.
tips: Add each overnight stop in order
Open the trip before a long leg

faq: How long does it take to drive from Brisbane to Cairns?

About 1,700 km and 22 hours of driving on the Bruce Highway, by OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data (1,693 km and 21 h 57 min direct). Wikipedia gives the Bruce Highway as about 1,679 km. Five legs of about 300 to 400 km keep each day to about five hours of driving.
Is there an inland route from Brisbane to Cairns?

Only a variant. You can leave the Bruce at Rockhampton, take the Capricorn Highway to Emerald, then the Gregory Highway and Gregory Developmental Road through Clermont to Charters Towers and the Flinders Highway to Townsville. By OSRM it is about 1,938 km, roughly 245 km longer than the Bruce, and Wikipedia says the Gregory route is used by many road trains.
When is the Bruce Highway most likely to flood?

Queensland's cyclone season officially runs from 1 November to 30 April, and a Queensland road closure document says the Wet runs from November to April. Wikipedia says the Bruce is prone to frequent flooding, and a Transport and Main Roads extract says the 16 km between Ingham and Innisfail closes in most wet seasons. Check QLDTraffic before each leg.
Are there fire ant rules when driving out of Brisbane?

Queensland's fire ant biosecurity zones cover parts of Logan, Gold Coast, Moreton Bay, Lockyer Valley, Scenic Rim and Sunshine Coast council areas. The rules control moving carriers such as soil, mulch, hay, manure, potted plants, turf and quarry materials out of the zones. The sources checked do not mention caravans or camping gear, so check fireants.org.au before you leave.

sydney-to-canberra-drive.title: Sydney to Canberra Drive 2026: Hume and Federal Highway Route, Tolls, Stops and Camping
sydney-to-canberra-drive.description: Sydney to Canberra is about 294 km and 3.5 hours on the Hume and Federal Highways. Tolls for visitors, Goulburn and Lake George, fuel, rest areas, ACT camping and the Kings Highway option.
sydney-to-canberra-drive.region: New South Wales and the ACT
sydney-to-canberra-drive.imageAlt: The Federal Highway curving above the green Lake George basin in New South Wales, with a few cars on the road and low cloud over the hills
sydney-to-canberra-drive.intro: Sydney to Canberra is about 294 km and 3 h 34 min of driving on the Hume Highway to Goulburn and the Federal Highway into the ACT, by OSRM routing. It is a day trip rather than a two-day drive, and the choices that matter are how you pay Sydney tolls as a visitor, where you stop at Goulburn and whether you book an ACT campground before you leave.

sections.heading: Sydney to Canberra routes compared
body: The standard route leaves Sydney by the M5 or M7, which Wikipedia says meet at Prestons where the Hume Highway (M31) begins, and follows the Hume through Campbelltown, Mittagong, Marulan and Goulburn. Wikipedia describes the Prestons to Berrima motorway as dual carriageway, the Hume as generally dual outside urban areas, and the limit on its full length as 110 km/h. At Yarra, south-east of Goulburn, the Federal Highway (M23) takes over for the 72.7 km to Canberra.

The coastal alternative follows the coast through Wollongong, Nowra and Batemans Bay, then the Kings Highway over Clyde Mountain through Braidwood and Bungendore to Canberra. Wikipedia gives the Kings Highway as 139 km from Batemans Bay to Canberra and says a 40 km section over the Great Dividing Range, including Clyde Mountain, recorded about 22% of the road's crashes. This guide found no road authority page that publishes it as a Sydney to Canberra route, and the Southern Highlands and Kangaroo Valley roads are the same, so it compares only these two. The figures are OSRM results on OpenStreetMap data from 21 October 2026, worked out for a car without any stops.
tips: Hume and Federal: the quick route
Clyde Mountain is the steep section

sections.heading: Goulburn, Lake George and the stops between
body: By OSRM routing, Sydney to Goulburn is about 194 km (2 h 22 min) and Goulburn to Canberra about 100 km (1 h 17 min). Wikipedia says Goulburn is about 195 km south-west of Sydney and 90 km north-east of Canberra, and that the 1992 Hume bypass removed about 23,000 cars a day from the city. Its landmark is the Big Merino, which Wikipedia calls the world's largest concrete sheep. South Goulburn Caravan Park, at 149 Hume Street, is listed by Visit NSW with large drive-through caravan sites with power and water, unpowered tent sites and cabins. Confirm availability with the park.

Lake George lies beside the Federal Highway, which runs along its western shore. Wikipedia says it is about 25 km long and 10 km wide, averages about 1 m deep, dried completely in November 2002 and stayed dry until 2010, and was full again in December 2021, so what you see depends on recent rain. It describes no formal lookout, so use a rest area for a break rather than stopping on the shoulder.
tips: Lake George: the water level changes
Check the park before you book

sections.heading: Tolls: how a visitor pays in Sydney
body: The NSW Government says that if you travel on a toll road without an active toll account or pass, you have 72 hours to pay or create a toll account, and otherwise a Toll Payment Demand is issued that adds a video matching fee. Service NSW says visitors can use the eMU Casual Pass, listed for visiting NSW or up to 30 days of NSW toll road use, and that you can open an account or buy a pass up to 72 hours after you travel on a toll road.

The NSW Government lists E-Toll for the Sydney Harbour Bridge and Sydney Harbour Tunnel, and Linkt for the Cross City Tunnel, Eastern Distributor, Hills M2, Lane Cove Tunnel, M5 South-West Motorway, NorthConnex, WestConnex and Westlink M7, each payable online or by phone. Which of these your drive meets depends on where you start in Sydney, so check your route before you leave. Wikipedia does not describe tolls on the Hume Highway or Federal Highway.
tips: 72 hours to pay or open an account
eMU Casual Pass covers up to 30 days
E-Toll for the Harbour Bridge and Tunnel, Linkt for the rest

sections.heading: Fuel, rest areas and dump points
body: No source checked gives a fuel gap on this route, and the longest OSRM leg between the towns used as waypoints is Campbelltown to Mittagong at about 63 km. The Australian National University tells visitors there are plenty of 24/7 food and fuel stops on the highway. The road trip fuel guide is the place to budget fuel for the distance.

The AussieCamps data lists free rest areas at Appin Park in the Wollondilly area, with toilets, a shelter, picnic tables, barbecues, a heavy vehicle area and a playground, and the Anderson VC Rest Area in the Yass Valley area, with toilets, a shelter, picnic tables and barbecues. Treat them as places for a break: the guide on overnight stays and the camping rules guide for New South Wales cover sleeping in a vehicle. The data lists a dump point at the Ampol Foodary at Pheasants Nest, southbound, with toilets and showers listed and no washout tap listed, and at Epic, Exhibition Park Campground in Lyneham. The list shows only what the data covers, and the dump points guide explains where else to look.
tips: Dump points: Pheasants Nest and Lyneham

sections.heading: Road conditions, speed and the clock
body: Check Live Traffic NSW (livetraffic.com) before you leave. No official page opened for this guide described snow, fog or fire closures on this route, so none are described here. Wikipedia says the Federal Highway is a continuous 110 km/h northbound in NSW, a southbound section near Yarra and Rowes Lagoon is 100 km/h with many lower advisory signs, and in the ACT the limit falls to 100, 80 and then 70 km/h on the way into the city.

The Interstate Quarantine site lists no fruit fly restrictions for New South Wales, and groups the ACT with New South Wales without separate zones. That is not proof that nothing applies, and no ACT government source on carrying fruit was found, so no border checkpoint is described here. New South Wales and the ACT both observe daylight saving, which began on Sunday 4 October 2026 and ends on Sunday 4 April 2027, so the clock does not change.
tips: Limits fall as you enter the ACT

sections.heading: Camping in the ACT
body: ACT Parks says, in a search extract of its pages, that bookings are essential at Cotter Campground, which takes general camping, camper-trailers and small vans, with water, hot showers and barbecues and no dogs. Booking is needed at Honeysuckle Campground too, which takes up to four campervans or camper-trailers and charges fees. Mount Clear Campground in Namadgi National Park is remote and basic, and ACT Parks says it is unsuitable for campervans and caravans. The AussieCamps data lists all four ACT Parks campgrounds, with Northern Border Campground, and fees were not confirmed, so check the ACT Parks page.

Closer to Goulburn, NPWS says Bungonia campground has caravan, camper trailer and beside-vehicle sites, toilets, showers and drinking water, and park entry of $8 a vehicle a day that is not included in the camping fee. It is always open but may close at times for high fire danger or park operations, so call the park before you drive there. The camping rules guide for the ACT covers the rules.
tips: Cotter and Honeysuckle need a booking
Bungonia: entry fee on top of camping

sections.heading: Plan the Sydney to Canberra drive in AussieCamps
body: Plan it as a trip in AussieCamps: add the stops in order, Goulburn, a break at Lake George and a Canberra campground, and it shows the distance and drive time of each leg with a forecast for the day you plan to arrive. AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, including the ACT Parks and NPWS campgrounds above, and a place page shows the photos, weather and facilities those sources publish.

Saved places, place details and guides keep working when the signal drops. Because map tiles, routing, weather and photos need a connection, open the trip while you are still inside Sydney's coverage. It runs on iPhone and is free to download, with in-app purchases. The Melbourne to Canberra guide covers the southern side.
tips: Open the trip before you leave Sydney

faq: How long does it take to drive from Sydney to Canberra?

OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data gives 294 km and 3 h 34 min via the Hume Highway and Federal Highway. The Australian National University tells visitors the drive takes about three hours on the Hume. Most drivers do it in a morning or an afternoon, with a stop at Goulburn.
Are there tolls between Sydney and Canberra?

Wikipedia says the M5 and M7, which meet where the Hume Highway starts at Prestons, are tolled, and does not describe tolls on the Hume Highway or Federal Highway themselves. The NSW Government says that if you use a toll road without an account or pass you have 72 hours to pay or create a toll account, and Service NSW suggests the eMU Casual Pass for visitors, which covers up to 30 days.
Is the Federal Highway dual carriageway?

Wikipedia says the whole 72.7 km route has two lanes in each direction, with the last dual section completed in 2000. It gives a continuous 110 km/h northbound in NSW, a 100 km/h southbound section near Yarra and Rowes Lagoon, and 100, 80 and then 70 km/h in the ACT as you near the city.
Can I take the coast road from Sydney to Canberra?

Yes, by the Kings Highway from Batemans Bay through Braidwood and Bungendore. By OSRM routing it is about 426 km and 6 h 31 min, so about 130 km longer than the Hume. No road authority page was found that publishes it as a Sydney to Canberra route, so treat it as a day of scenery rather than a shortcut.

perth-to-albany-drive.title: Perth to Albany Drive 2026: Albany Highway, South Western Highway, Fuel and Stops
perth-to-albany-drive.description: Perth to Albany is about 410 km and under five hours by Albany Highway, or about 540 km through Manjimup and Denmark. Route options, rest areas, fuel, Stirling Range and Porongurup entry fees, dump points and fruit fly rules.
perth-to-albany-drive.imageAlt: Albany Highway running south towards Mount Barker, with paddocks on the left and a forested hill with a radio tower ahead
perth-to-albany-drive.intro: Perth to Albany is about 410 km, which is 408 km and 4 h 43 min by Main Roads WA and 426 km and 5 h 25 min by OSRM routing, via Albany Highway. It works as a long day's drive, and a night at Kojonup or Mount Barker makes it comfortable. The South Western Highway through Manjimup and Denmark is about 540 km and suits a slower trip.

sections.heading: Perth to Albany routes compared
body: There are two real choices. Albany Highway (State Route 30) is the direct road through Armadale, Williams, Kojonup, Cranbrook and Mount Barker. Wikipedia describes it as a sealed two-lane single carriageway outside Perth, with overtaking lanes in some undulating areas. The South Western Highway runs south through Pinjarra, Harvey, Donnybrook and Manjimup, then on to Walpole, where it continues as South Coast Highway through Denmark. Wikipedia says the section south of Bunbury is sparsely populated and heavily forested, especially from Manjimup.

A third option links the two. Muirs Highway runs 161 km between Mount Barker and Manjimup, according to Wikipedia, as a single carriageway through karri and jarrah forest, with Rocky Gully as the only village. Wikipedia calls it mainly a freight route for plantation timber trucks and long interstate vehicles. Driving down Albany Highway and back by Muirs Highway and Donnybrook is about 508 km from Albany to Perth by OSRM. Main Roads WA's figures come from its 2015 rest area guide, which it says can go out of date.
tips: Albany Highway is the direct route
South Western Highway adds about 130 km

sections.heading: Albany Highway, leg by leg
body: Main Roads WA's distance guide puts Armadale at 30 km, Williams at 160.5 km, Kojonup at 256 km, Mount Barker at 359 km and Albany at 408 km. That makes Williams to Kojonup 95 km and Kojonup to Mount Barker about 103 km. By OSRM the legs are Perth to Armadale 37 km (35 min), Armadale to Williams 131 km (1 h 34 min), Williams to Kojonup 95 km (1 h 09 min), Kojonup to Cranbrook 70 km (51 min), Cranbrook to Mount Barker 41 km (32 min) and Mount Barker to Albany 51 km (42 min).

Wikipedia says the road has many traffic lights in the south-eastern suburbs of Perth, where it runs four to six lanes for about 15 km. Between towns it is a two-lane road, and Wikipedia gives Williams, Kojonup and Mount Barker as about 100 km apart. The Albany Ring Road opened on 19 May 2024 and diverts heavy vehicles around the city, according to the State Government's project page, which says a flyover at Menang Drive and Chester Pass Road is due for completion in 2026, so expect works near Albany.

sections.heading: Fuel, rest areas and where to stop
body: Wikipedia lists roadhouses on Albany Highway at North Bannister, Crossman and Arthur River. Fuel availability and opening hours at each could not be confirmed, so fill up in Armadale or Williams and again at Kojonup. Main Roads WA says to pack extra food, water and fuel in case of emergency or breakdown, especially when rest stops are limited. The fuel planning guide covers how to budget range.

Main Roads WA's 2015 guide marks rest areas at Glen Eagle Forest, Williams Lion, Martup Pool, Crapella, Tunney and Orup Creek. It says 24 hour rest areas are not intended for camping, and stopping is not to exceed 24 consecutive hours. They are for a break, so use a caravan park or the Kojonup RV stay for the night. The rest area guide and the Western Australia rules guide cover the rules.

At Kojonup, the Shire's visitor site describes an RV stay on the corner of Albany Highway and Gordon Street, next to the Giant Wool Wagon. It costs $5.00 per night, with a maximum continuous stay of 3 nights, and you need a permit from the Kojonup Visitors Centre. It says you must be self-sufficient and that generators are not allowed. In Mount Barker, the Shire of Plantagenet lists Mount Barker Caravan Park at 31720 Albany Highway and Porongurup Range Tourist Park at 7 Box Hill Road. At Albany, BIG4 Emu Beach Holiday Park says on its site that it has a caravan and camping area. Ring ahead in each case, because rates and availability could not be confirmed.
tips: Fuel at Armadale, Williams and Kojonup
Rest areas are for a break only
Kojonup RV stay: $5 a night, 3 nights

sections.heading: Road conditions and wildlife at dusk
body: Check the Main Roads WA Travel Map or ring 138 138 before you leave. No current Albany Highway roadworks could be confirmed for this guide, so the Travel Map is the place to look for closures and works on the day. Main Roads WA's guide says many major rural highways are unfenced, so there are no barriers to stop wild or pastoral animals crossing. It says to be alert for animals on the road, particularly dusk and dawn, and to slow down and sound your horn if you meet one.

The Main Roads WA long-distance page adds that if animals are on the road, you should be ready to stop suddenly and avoid swerving. It says to overtake road trains only when you have a long straight stretch ahead that is completely clear, and to swap drivers every two hours. If you leave Perth late, plan the last stretch into Albany so it does not fall at dusk or dawn. The road trains guide covers overtaking.

sections.heading: Stirling Range and Porongurup side trips
body: Both parks sit close to Albany Highway, and DBCA lists the same entry fee at each: $17.00 for a standard vehicle of 12 or fewer occupants, $10.00 concession, $10.00 for a motorcycle, and $8.00 per person ($3.50 concession) for a large vehicle. A valid park pass covers the fees, and DBCA says no dogs or other pets are allowed in either park. The Shire of Plantagenet says Porongurup is about 20 km east of Mount Barker, and OSRM gives 28 km and 30 minutes from Mount Barker to Castle Rock. DBCA describes the Castle Rock Trail as 4.7 km return, which climbs 670 m to the top on the Granite Skywalk.

DBCA says Bluff Knoll in the Stirling Range is 4.5 hours south of Perth and 1.5 hours from Albany. The walk is 6.8 km return, Grade 4, to 1,098 m, on a steep path with many steps, and DBCA warns of rapid, unpredictable changes in the weather. It advises against entering the bush or using footpaths on days of extreme fire danger. Moingup Spring Campground is in the AussieCamps data, and DBCA says bookings are essential, drinking water is not provided and no dogs are allowed. A camping fee and a park entry fee both apply, and bookings go through ParkStay. By OSRM it is 77 km from Cranbrook and 97 km from Albany. In Albany itself, Torndirrup National Park has the same fee, and DBCA warns of a notorious record for accidents and deaths from people washed off the coast. Check alerts.dbca.wa.gov.au before you go, and see the South West WA camping loop for the rest of Albany.
tips: Same $17 vehicle fee at both parks

sections.heading: Fruit rules and Western Australia
body: Perth to Albany is entirely in Western Australia, so there is no state border and no interstate checkpoint. One fruit rule does matter at the Perth end. DPIRD has a Quarantine Area Notice for Queensland fruit fly over a 15 km radius around the corner of South Terrace and Sandgate Street, South Perth, in force until 11:59pm on 31 March 2027, following an amendment on 22 September 2026. DPIRD's page says host fruit must not be moved outside the Orange Zone, a 15 km radius around the detection points, unless it has been treated. The notice lets fruit move out after cooking, processing or freezing for at least 24 hours, and DPIRD says breaking it could bring a fine.

The notice also covers fruit entering or passing through the area: it must travel under secure conditions, such as fully enclosed packaging or vehicles free from gaps over 1.6 mm. DPIRD's page does not address travellers directly, so ring its Pest and Disease Information Service on (08) 9368 3080 if you are unsure. DPIRD says Medfly is found throughout WA from Esperance to Carnarvon, and no Medfly rule for travellers on this route could be confirmed. The interstate biosecurity guide covers rules at state borders.
tips: Treated fruit only out of the area

sections.heading: Dump points and the AussieCamps data
body: The Shire of Plantagenet says a dump point and potable water are available at the Mount Barker Visitor Centre on Albany Highway, and the Kojonup visitor site says both are at the Railway Station Reserve. Main Roads WA says blackwater may only be disposed of in rest areas displaying the effluent dump point sign, or at the nearest town's dump site. The AussieCamps data lists no campground, dump point or rest area within 12 km of Albany Highway, which reflects its coverage and not what is on the road, so use the Shire pages above.

On the South Western Highway, the data lists free dump points with a washout tap at Snells Park in Harvey and on Boyanup-Picton Road in Dardanup. It also lists campgrounds at Shannon, and Banksia Camp and Black Point near Walpole, so check the booking and facility rules with DBCA before you rely on them. The dump points guide explains how to use them.
tips: Mount Barker Visitor Centre has a dump point
Data coverage is not every dump point

sections.heading: Plan the Perth to Albany drive in AussieCamps
body: Plan it as a trip in AussieCamps: add Kojonup, Mount Barker and Albany as nights and it shows the distance and drive time of each leg, with a forecast for the day you plan to arrive. AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and each place page shows the facilities those sources publish, with a notes field of your own.

Place details, saved places and guides load without reception. Map tiles, routing, weather and photos need a connection, so open the trip in range before the long stretches between Williams and Kojonup. The iPhone app is free to download, with in-app purchases.
tips: Open the trip before the long legs

faq: How far is it from Perth to Albany?

Main Roads WA gives 408 km and 4 h 43 min via Albany Highway, in its 2015 rest area guide. OSRM routing on OpenStreetMap data gives 426 km and 5 h 25 min, centre to centre. Most people do it in one day, or split it with a night at Kojonup or Mount Barker.
Is Albany Highway or the South Western Highway better?

Albany Highway is the direct route and about 130 km shorter. Main Roads WA gives Bunbury to Albany via South Western Highway as 364 km and 4 h 40 min, and Perth to Bunbury as 172 km, so that way is about 536 km. It suits a trip through Manjimup, Walpole and Denmark rather than the quickest drive.
Do I pay to enter the Stirling Range and Porongurup?

Yes. DBCA lists $17.00 for a standard vehicle (12 or fewer occupants) and $10.00 concession at both parks, and says a valid park pass covers the fees. DBCA also says no dogs or other pets are allowed in either park.
Can I take fruit out of Perth?

Check DPIRD first. A Queensland fruit fly Quarantine Area Notice covers a 15 km radius around South Perth until 11:59pm on 31 March 2027, and DPIRD's page says host fruit must not be moved outside the area unless it has been treated. The rest of the route is in Western Australia, with no state border.

perth-to-margaret-river-drive.title: Perth to Margaret River Drive 2026: Route, Fuel, Caves Road and Park Bookings
perth-to-margaret-river-drive.description: Perth to Margaret River is about 275 to 290 km and four hours by Forrest Highway and Bussell Highway. Route options, Caves Road, free Leeuwin-Naturaliste entry, campground bookings, dump points and fruit fly rules.
perth-to-margaret-river-drive.imageAlt: A rocky coast with a grassy headland and low heath under a pale evening sky, north of Sugarloaf Rock in Leeuwin-Naturaliste National Park
perth-to-margaret-river-drive.intro: Perth to Margaret River is about 275 to 290 km, which is 273 km by Main Roads WA and 287 km and 3 h 55 min by OSRM routing, via Kwinana Freeway, Forrest Highway and Bussell Highway. It is a one-day drive past Mandurah, Bunbury and Busselton, with Caves Road as the slower scenic finish.

sections.heading: Perth to Margaret River routes compared
body: The standard route is Kwinana Freeway to Mandurah, Forrest Highway to Bunbury, then Bussell Highway through Capel and Busselton to Margaret River. Wikipedia gives Kwinana Freeway as 72 km, a controlled-access freeway signed up to 110 km/h at its southern end, and Forrest Highway as 95.67 km with two lanes each way, a median and a 110 km/h limit. Main Roads WA says the Wilman Wadandi Highway, a 27 km four-lane road that opened in December 2024, links Forrest Highway to Bussell Highway and saves 11 to 18 minutes depending on destination and traffic. Main Roads also says the Bussell Highway duplication is complete, with all four lanes open to traffic on 17 April 2025.

The alternative is the South Western Highway through Pinjarra, Harvey and Donnybrook, then across to Busselton. By OSRM it is 297 km and 4 h 05 min to Busselton, against 237 km on the main route, so it adds about 60 km. Vasse Highway is real, but it does not shorten the trip. Wikipedia describes it as a 151 km road from Busselton through Nannup and Pemberton, in jarrah and karri forest, so it suits a trip on to Pemberton rather than the way to Margaret River. The South West WA camping loop covers that country.
tips: South Western Highway adds about 60 km
Vasse Highway runs to Nannup and Pemberton

sections.heading: The drive leg by leg
body: By OSRM the legs are Perth to Mandurah 72 km (57 min), Mandurah to Bunbury 111 km (1 h 26 min), Bunbury to Busselton 54 km (46 min) and Busselton to Margaret River 50 km (44 min). Main Roads WA's distance guide puts Bunbury at 172 km, Busselton at 224 km and Margaret River at 273 km, so Bunbury to Busselton is about 52 km and Busselton to Margaret River 49 km.

Main Roads WA says its 2015 figures can go out of date. It also says some finishing works were still under way on the Wilman Wadandi Highway between Paris Road and Bussell Highway until late August 2026, with speeds reduced to 80 km/h and lane closures. That date has passed, but check the Travel Map for any works on the day.

sections.heading: Fuel and rest areas
body: This route passes through towns the whole way, so fuel is not a planning problem the way it is further north. Wikipedia says twin roadhouses opened on Forrest Highway in late 2017, about 5 km south of Greenlands Road, but fuel availability and opening hours could not be confirmed. Fill up in Mandurah, Bunbury or Busselton, and again before leaving Margaret River for the Caves Road coast. The fuel planning guide covers range for longer trips.

Main Roads WA's 2015 guide marks rest areas named Settlers, Myalup and Rotary Park on the route, with more unnamed along Bussell Highway. It says 24 hour rest areas are not intended for camping, and stopping is not to exceed 24 consecutive hours, so treat them as a place for a break and book a campground or caravan park for the night. For the full rules, read the rest area guide and the Western Australia camping rules guide.
tips: Rest areas are for a break only
Fill up before the Caves Road coast

sections.heading: Road conditions and wildlife
body: Before you set off, open the Main Roads WA Travel Map or call 138 138. Main Roads WA says many major rural highways are unfenced, with no barriers to stop wild or pastoral animals crossing, and to be alert for animals on the road, particularly dusk and dawn. It says to slow down if you meet an animal, and to be ready to stop suddenly without swerving. The road trains guide covers overtaking.

No official source for school-holiday traffic on this route could be found for this guide, so it is not assessed here. Caves Road is narrow and winding in most parts, according to Wikipedia, and OSRM gives about 88 km and 1 h 30 min from Busselton to Margaret River that way, against 50 km and 43 minutes on Bussell Highway. Allow the extra time, and avoid the road at dusk and dawn when animals are active.
tips: Caves Road takes about twice as long

sections.heading: Leeuwin-Naturaliste National Park fees and bookings
body: DBCA says entry to Leeuwin-Naturaliste National Park is free, and no dogs or other pets are allowed in the park. Admission fees apply at the caves: DBCA lists Mammoth, Lake, Jewel and Ngilgi caves, and points to the cave operator's page for opening hours and prices. DBCA puts Mammoth Cave 11 km south of Margaret River along Caves Road, and the entry to Jewel Cave about 45 km south of Margaret River via Bussell Highway and Caves Road. Lake Cave and Jewel Cave have one-hour guided tours, and Mammoth Cave has a self-guided audio tour.

DBCA lists four bookable campgrounds in the park: Conto, Point Road, Boranup and Jarrahdene. Each page says bookings are essential, and Boranup, Point Road and Jarrahdene can be booked up to 180 days ahead, for one campsite only. A per person camping fee applies and is paid by Mastercard or VISA when booking. DBCA says drinking water is not provided, toilets are no-flush pit toilets, no dogs are allowed, and generators are not permitted at Boranup, Point Road or Jarrahdene. Boranup has only seven campsites, suitable for tents and small campervans only. Its page also says December to April can be extremely hot and the risk of bushfire can be very high. Hamelin Bay Holiday Park is privately operated, according to DBCA. The camp-by-camp guide stays in the South West WA camping loop.
tips: Park entry is free, caves charge
No drinking water at DBCA campgrounds

sections.heading: Fruit rules and Western Australia
body: The whole drive stays inside Western Australia, so no state border or interstate checkpoint is crossed. DPIRD has a Queensland fruit fly Quarantine Area Notice for a 15 km radius around the corner of South Terrace and Sandgate Street, South Perth, in force until 11:59pm on 31 March 2027 after an amendment on 22 September 2026. Under the DPIRD page, host fruit cannot leave the Orange Zone, which is a 15 km radius around the detection points, unless it has been treated. The notice also says fruit entering or passing through the area must travel under secure conditions, such as fully enclosed packaging or vehicles without gaps over 1.6 mm.

DPIRD says Medfly's main area of infestation runs from Perth through Bunbury, Bridgetown, Donnybrook and Manjimup, but no Medfly rule for travellers on this route could be confirmed. DPIRD's Pest and Disease Information Service is on (08) 9368 3080. Breaking the notice could bring a fine, according to DPIRD. The Perth to Albany guide has the same notice from the other side, and the interstate biosecurity guide covers state borders.
tips: Treated fruit only out of the area

sections.heading: Dump points
body: The councils publish dump points along the way. The Shire of Capel lists one on Buchanan Road, off Capel Drive, with a lock and an access code on its page, and asks that nothing but effluent is disposed of. The City of Busselton lists one at Churchill Park, on the corner of Brown Street and Adelaide Street, also locked, and its tourism page says most caravan parks in the City provide dump points for visitors. The Shire of Augusta Margaret River says its Margaret River dump point, at the western end of Gloucester Park next to the Recreation Centre, and its Cowaramup dump point, on Hall Road, are operational all year and free of charge.

The AussieCamps data lists free dump points with a washout tap at Snells Park in Harvey and on Boyanup-Picton Road in Dardanup, which reflects its coverage and not every dump point. DBCA says Jarrahdene Campground has a chemical toilet dump point, and says not to empty portable toilet waste into campground toilets. Blackwater goes only to a rest area with the effluent dump point sign or to the nearest town's dump site, according to Main Roads WA. The dump points guide has more.
tips: Margaret River dump point is free
Data coverage is not every dump point

sections.heading: Plan the Perth to Margaret River drive in AussieCamps
body: Plan it as a trip in AussieCamps: add the stops in order and it shows the distance and drive time of each leg, with a forecast for the day you plan to arrive. The app holds 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points taken from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and a place page has a notes field for your own remarks beside the published facilities.

Even in a dead spot, the stored place details, saved places and guides open. Map tiles, routing, weather and photos need a connection, so open the trip in range before the Caves Road coast. On iPhone it is free to download, with in-app purchases.
tips: Open the trip before the coast

faq: How far is it from Perth to Margaret River?

Main Roads WA's 2015 rest area guide puts Margaret River at 273 km from Perth on the Forrest Highway and Bussell Highway route. By OSRM on OpenStreetMap data the drive is 287 km and 3 h 55 min between town centres. It is an easy one-day drive with no overnight needed.
Is there an entry fee for Leeuwin-Naturaliste National Park?

No. DBCA lists no park entry fee, though it does not allow dogs or other pets in the park. The caves are different: DBCA says admission fees apply at Mammoth, Lake, Jewel and Ngilgi caves, and points to the cave operator for opening hours and prices.
Do I need to book a campground in the park?

Yes. DBCA lists Conto, Point Road, Boranup and Jarrahdene as bookable campgrounds, and each page says bookings are essential. Boranup, Point Road and Jarrahdene can be booked up to 180 days ahead, for one campsite only, and DBCA says drinking water is not provided at any of them.
Can I take fruit out of Perth?

Check DPIRD first. A Queensland fruit fly quarantine notice currently covers South Perth, and DPIRD says host fruit cannot be moved out of that area unless treated; read the notice for the end date. The rest of the drive has no state border.

hobart-to-launceston-drive.title: Hobart to Launceston Drive 2026: Midland Highway, Roadworks, Stops and Biosecurity
hobart-to-launceston-drive.description: Hobart to Launceston is about 200 km and under three hours on the Midland Highway. Towns, rest areas, free stopovers, dump points, roadworks at Campbell Town, wildlife at dusk and Tasmania's fruit and vegetable rules.
hobart-to-launceston-drive.imageAlt: The sandstone arches of Ross Bridge over the Macquarie River in the Tasmanian Midlands, under a blue sky
hobart-to-launceston-drive.intro: Hobart to Launceston is about 200 km by the Midland Highway, which is 181 km by Wikipedia's figure and 201 km and 2 h 41 min by OSRM routing, centre to centre. It is an easy half-day drive through Kempton, Oatlands, Ross and Campbell Town, so most people do it in one go. The east-coast alternatives add 70 to 150 km.

sections.heading: Hobart to Launceston routes compared
body: The Midland Highway (National Highway 1, signed A1) is the direct road. Wikipedia describes it as mostly two lanes, one in each direction, with overtaking options and at-grade intersections, and with small portions of grade-separated dual carriageway at the Hobart and Launceston ends. It is also called the Midlands Highway, and in the 2000s it carried the label The Heritage Highway.

Two longer options leave it. The Lake Leake Highway (B34) meets the Midland Highway near Campbell Town, according to Wikipedia, and links it to Swansea on the east coast. The Esk Highway (A4) is 82 km long and joins the Midland Highway at Conara Junction, just north of Campbell Town. Wikipedia says it passes Avoca, Fingal and St Marys, then climbs the curvy 6 km St Marys Pass to meet the Tasman Highway near Falmouth. Conditions on both roads could not be confirmed for this guide, so check the weather before you take them.
tips: The Midland Highway is the direct route
Lake Leake Highway joins it near Campbell Town
Esk Highway joins it at Conara Junction
