sections.heading: The Midland Highway, town by town
body: By OSRM the legs are Hobart to Kempton 49 km (42 min), Kempton to Oatlands 35 km (26 min), Oatlands to Ross 37 km (28 min), Ross to Campbell Town 12 km (11 min), Campbell Town to Epping Forest 23 km (18 min) and Epping Forest to Launceston 46 km (34 min). Oatlands, Ross and Campbell Town are all on the highway, so it works as a trip with short stops rather than one with a long gap.

Ross has a stone bridge over the Macquarie River, which is the photo at the top of this guide. Ross Caravan Park and the Campbell Town stopover below are listed by Northern Midlands Council, and Kempton and Oatlands by Southern Midlands Council. The Tasmania camping loop covers the rest of the island, so this guide stays on the Hobart to Launceston road.

sections.heading: Roadworks and winter conditions
body: Look at the RoadsTas roadworks map before you set off. A search extract of an Australian Government release says safety upgrades at the Midland Highway and Lake Leake Road intersection in Campbell Town were due to start on Monday 21 September 2026. Work was to run 7am to 6pm, Monday to Friday, with lane closures and a reduced speed limit during working hours, and completion was expected by the end of the year, weather permitting. Whether it started on time could not be confirmed.

A search extract of a Tasmanian Government release dated 5 September 2026 says the final 10 km stage, Campbell Town North to Conara, has its environmental approvals. It says a construction contract was expected in the coming weeks, with work starting in late 2026 and running until late 2028. That stage adds widening, sealed shoulders, overtaking lanes in both directions and flexible safety barriers. The State Growth and Premier's pages for these projects blocked scripts, so the details come from the extracts. Obey signposted limits through any works, because current limits on the highway could not be confirmed.

Cold weather is a real factor in the Midlands. The Tasmanian Road Safety Advisory Council warns of black ice and moss on the road, especially in shady areas, and says fog, snow and ice can be experienced in some areas. It advises you to check the weather forecast before setting out. A statement from the Department of State Growth on ice or snow on the Midland Highway could not be confirmed. Tasmania Police's Community Alerts page is where it directs motorists for road conditions and closures.

sections.heading: Driving rules, wildlife and fuel
body: The Tasmanian Road Safety Advisory Council lists the default limits as 50 km/h in urban areas, 100 km/h on rural roads and 80 km/h on gravel roads, unless signposted. It says to always drive on the left and to pull over in a safe place to let others pass from behind. It also says travelling 150 km may take 2 hours, and to plan no more than 300 km per day and take frequent breaks.

The same pages say to slow down and look out for animals on the road, especially at dawn and dusk. For a late departure from Hobart, aim to be off the Midlands stretch before dark. Fuel stations and their opening hours along the highway could not be confirmed, so start with a full tank in Hobart or Launceston and add fuel in a town before the tank runs low. The fuel planning guide has the range sums.
tips: Look out for animals at dawn and dusk

sections.heading: Where to stop and sleep
body: AussieCamps data lists no campground within 12 km of the route, so overnight options come from councils. Southern Midlands Council lists the Kempton Roadside Stopover near Station Park: free with a donation suggested, 48 hours maximum, for self-contained vehicles only. At Oatlands it lists the Lakeside Stopover off High Street on the Esplanade, free with a donation suggested and a 72-hour maximum. Ross Caravan Park appears on Northern Midlands Council's 2023/24 schedule of caravan parks, with fees set by the lessee, so ring the park for rates and availability.

In Campbell Town, Northern Midlands Council describes a free 48-hour area for self-contained caravans and mobile homes in Blackburn Park Reserve, on the south-eastern side of the Red Bridge. A permit is required, free for up to 48 hours, through the council's online form or on (03) 6397 7303 in business hours. Showering, washing, toilet use, cooking and sleeping must all be done inside the vehicle. The council says liquid waste must not go onto the ground, near trees or into the river, with a fine of up to $205 per unit, and it says you cannot reserve a place.

The rest areas in the AussieCamps data are St Peters Pass near Oatlands (toilets, picnic tables, barbecues), the Campbell Town Weighbridge rest area (a heavy vehicle area) and Conara (picnic tables, barbecues). Use them for a leg stretch. Whether a night there is allowed is a separate question, answered in the overnight rest area guide and the Tasmania camping rules guide.

sections.heading: Dump points on the Midland Highway
body: Southern Midlands Council lists a free dump point with water on Williams Street at Wellington Street in Oatlands, open 24 hours, which it describes as size ok for greater than 20 metres. Its Kempton dump point is on Old Hunting Ground Road behind Victoria Hall, open 24 hours and free with water. The council says it suits cassette toilets only and is difficult for large motorhomes to reverse into.

At Campbell Town, the Northern Midlands page lists no dump point, but a Spirit of Tasmania listing, valid to 6 October 2027, places a free one at King Street Oval with potable and rinse water. Ask the council if you are unsure. The only one the AussieCamps data holds on this corridor is Brighton Showground at Pontville, free with toilets, about 29 km from Hobart, so a gap in the data is not proof of a gap on the road. The dump points guide shows how to use one.

sections.heading: Tasmania's fruit and vegetable rules
body: Tasmania has its own biosecurity rules, so they matter for anyone arriving from the mainland. Biosecurity Tasmania's food page lists these as not permitted: fresh fruit and vegetables, including potatoes, fresh herbs, garlic, ginger and onion. It lists cooked, baked, hard frozen, canned, preserved, commercially dried, freeze dried and home dehydrated after cooking as permitted. The page says fresh and processed plant foods must be declared on arrival and inspected. For the Spirit of Tasmania, it says you can bring food to eat on board but must dispose of it in the bins or at the Biosecurity Inspection point when leaving the terminal.

The page does not set out a separate rule for arrivals from mainland Australia, and it does not cover moving produce within Tasmania, so nothing about the Hobart to Launceston drive itself could be confirmed. You can ring Biosecurity Tasmania on 1300 368 550. The interstate biosecurity guide covers other borders.
tips: Fresh fruit and vegetables not permitted

sections.heading: Plan the Hobart to Launceston drive in AussieCamps
body: Build the drive as a trip in AussieCamps. Put Oatlands, Campbell Town and Launceston in as stops, and each leg shows its distance and drive time, plus a forecast for the day you expect to get there. The app holds 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points taken from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and a place page lists the facilities those sources publish, with a notes field for your own remarks.

You can read stored place details, open saved places and use the guides when there is no signal. Map tiles, routing, weather and photos need a connection, so load them before the Midlands stretch. The app is for iPhone only, free to download, with in-app purchases.

faq: How far is it from Hobart to Launceston?

Roughly 180 to 200 km, depending on who measures. Wikipedia gives the Midland Highway as 181 km, while OSRM, a routing engine on OpenStreetMap data, returned 201 km and 2 h 41 min between the two city centres on 21 October 2026. Allow a half day if you want to walk across Ross Bridge or look around Oatlands.
Is there a quicker road than the Midland Highway?
None came up in this research. The detours through Swansea and the Lake Leake Highway or via Bicheno and the Esk Highway run 272 km and 353 km by OSRM, so they are for sightseeing on the east coast.
What fruit and vegetables are banned in Tasmania?

Biosecurity Tasmania's food page names fresh fruit and vegetables, with potatoes, fresh herbs, garlic, ginger and onion as examples. Items that are cooked, baked, hard frozen, canned, preserved or commercially dried are on its permitted list, and plant foods have to be declared on arrival.
Does wildlife make night driving risky on this road?

The Tasmanian Road Safety Advisory Council names animals on the road as a hazard, most of all at dawn and dusk, and mentions roadkill at night and in the early morning. Its advice is to slow down and keep daily driving to 300 km at most.

alice-springs-to-uluru-drive.title: Alice Springs to Uluru Drive 2026: Stuart and Lasseter Highways, Fuel, Park Fees and Camping
alice-springs-to-uluru-drive.description: Alice Springs to Uluru is about 450 km and five hours by the Stuart and Lasseter Highways. Fuel at Erldunda, Curtin Springs and Yulara, park pass prices, heat, Yulara camping, alcohol limits, road trains and dump points.
alice-springs-to-uluru-drive.imageAlt: A straight sealed stretch of the Lasseter Highway running through red-soil scrub in central Australia, with two 100 km/h signs
alice-springs-to-uluru-drive.intro: Alice Springs to Uluru is about 450 km by road, which is 452 km and 5 h 11 min by OSRM routing, down the Stuart Highway to Erldunda and then west along the Lasseter Highway. It is a one-day drive for most people, with the longest fuel gap at the start, and the Red Centre Way through Kings Canyon is the slower option that adds about 180 km.

sections.heading: Alice Springs to Uluru routes compared
body: The direct route is the Stuart Highway south for about 200 km to the Erldunda junction, then the Lasseter Highway west. Wikipedia describes the Lasseter Highway as 244 km and fully sealed, running from the Stuart Highway at Erldunda to the national park, with Curtin Springs and Mount Ebenezer along the way. The Red Centre Way is the loop through Watarrka National Park and Kings Canyon, and it has its own guide, so it appears here only as a comparison.

By OSRM the Kings Canyon route is 633 km and 7 h 15 min, using the Stuart Highway, Ernest Giles Road and Luritja Road. The surface of Ernest Giles Road could not be confirmed. The Mereenie Loop, which links Kings Canyon to the West MacDonnell side, is described by Discover Central Australia as the unsealed section of the Red Centre Way, and its permit is listed at $5.00, valid for three days, sold in person at outlets including the Alice Springs Visitor Information Centre.
tips: Mereenie Loop is unsealed and needs a permit

A longer trip with Kings Canyon; see the Red Centre Way guide

sections.heading: The legs: Erldunda, Curtin Springs and Yulara
body: OSRM splits the direct drive into three legs: Alice Springs to Erldunda 203 km (2 h 09 min), Erldunda to Curtin Springs 164 km (2 h) and Curtin Springs to Yulara 85 km (1 h 02 min). Discover Central Australia, a regional tourism site, puts Erldunda 200 km from Alice Springs and 246 km from Yulara, and Curtin Springs 361 km from Alice Springs and 85 km from Yulara.

Erldunda sits at the junction of the two highways. The same tourism site says Erldunda Desert Oaks Resort stocks petrol and diesel, with the general store open 6:30am to 9pm and reception 8am to 6pm. Curtin Springs is a station on the highway with a roadhouse, and its own website lists fuel, rooms, meals and a free campground. Yulara has the closest fuel to the park.

sections.heading: Fuel and the longest gap
body: The fuel page on Discover Central Australia lists Erldunda, Curtin Springs (open 7am to 7pm) and Shell Yulara at 257 Yulara Drive (open 7am to 8pm daily), which it calls the closest fuel to the national park. It lists no stop between Alice Springs and Erldunda, so the first gap is about 200 km. Mount Ebenezer is on the highway too, but fuel and hours there could not be confirmed.

Tourism NT says to keep your tank full because fuel may not be available in remote areas, and that remote stations have limited hours and banking. The regional page adds that anyone towing a caravan, driving a motorhome or travelling outside business hours should plan ahead and carry enough for the next stop with a margin. Work out your range with the fuel planning guide before the first 200 km.
tips: About 200 km from Alice Springs to the first fuel
Check hours before relying on a stop

sections.heading: Speed limits, road trains and wet-season closures
body: Tourism NT's roads page gives the open-road limit as 110 km/h unless signposted otherwise, and says the maximum on the Stuart, Barkly, Victoria and Arnhem Highways is 130 km/h. The Lasseter Highway is not in that list, so follow the signs. For current conditions the page points to Road Report NT at roadreport.nt.gov.au or on 1800 246 199.

The same page says road trains can have three trailers and be over 50 m long and 2.5 m wide, and to allow plenty of room before overtaking because they may sway. It says animals are most active at sunrise, sunset or at night, and never to swerve to avoid one. It also says some roads may be closed by flooding from November to April, and that heavy fines may apply for using a closed road. Stop for 15 minutes every two hours, the page says. The road trains guide covers overtaking.
tips: Floods can close roads from November

sections.heading: Where to stop and rest areas
body: The AussieCamps data lists five rest areas along the way: Mount Polhill, Finke River and Desert Oaks on the Stuart Highway, with toilets, drinking water, shelter, picnic tables and barbecues at each, and Boxwood Dam and Black Swamp on the Lasseter Highway, with drinking water, shelter, tables and barbecues but no toilets listed. Use them for breaks. The data lists no campground along this route, so overnight options below come from the operators.

Curtin Springs's campground page says unpowered sites are free, first come and not bookable, while powered sites cost $65 per site per night and should be booked ahead. It lists showers, a barbecue area and water tank filling for $10, says there is no camp kitchen, and describes the sites as red dirt with limited shade. The page also says camping in the road corridor in the Northern Territory is illegal. Erldunda has camp sites and a caravan parking area, according to Tourism Central Australia. Prices and availability there could not be confirmed. The Northern Territory rules guide covers the rest.
tips: Rest areas are for a break
No camping in the road corridor

sections.heading: Uluru-Kata Tjuta entry, hours and heat
body: Parks Australia charges adults (18 and over) $38 for a 3-day pass and $50 for an annual pass, and children and teenagers under 18 go free. A $109 annual vehicle pass is available only for vehicles registered in the Northern Territory, and not for tour or hire vehicles. Buy online at book.parksaustralia.gov.au or get one at the entry station. At the gate, you scan the QR code in the left-hand lane.

The park's visitor guide gives December, January and February hours as 5:00am to 9:00pm. It says the park closes overnight and no camping is permitted in the park, and that camping is available at the resort. The guide also says temperatures regularly reach 30 degrees and can exceed 40 degrees in summer, and strongly recommends not walking after 11:00am in summer. It advises carrying at least one litre of water per person per hour. Its maps carry no-drone signs, and the Mala walk with a ranger is free.

sections.heading: Yulara camping, alcohol and dump points
body: Ayers Rock Campground is inside the Ayers Rock Resort complex at Yulara. Tourism NT's listing gives 198 powered sites and 220 unpowered sites, with rates starting from $30, and bookings through the resort by phone on 1300 134 044 or email. It lists a camp kitchen, barbecue, laundry, pool, playground and gas. Discover Central Australia says free camping is not permitted in or around the national park.

Ayers Rock Resort's bottle shop page says takeaway alcohol is restricted to resort guests. It opens from 12:00pm to 9:00pm and sets a daily limit per person, of up to six bottles of beer or ready-to-drink spirits, or one bottle of wine. Alice Springs takeaway rules could not be opened, so check nt.gov.au before you leave town.

For waste, the AussieCamps data includes the Ayers Rock Resort dump point (free, washout tap) and the Yulara Caravan dump point, and at the Alice Springs end Olive Pink Botanic Gardens, Alice Springs Dump Point and the Showground at Ilparpa. That list reflects the data only. Curtin Springs's page says black water may only be disposed of at Ayers Rock Resort or Alice Springs.
tips: Dump points at Yulara and Alice Springs

sections.heading: Plan the Alice Springs to Uluru drive in AussieCamps
body: Set the drive up as a trip in AussieCamps with Erldunda, Curtin Springs and Yulara as the stops. Each leg shows its distance and driving time, and the forecast for the day you arrive. The app carries 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points sourced from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and a place page shows the facilities those sources publish, plus a notes field for you.

Without a signal you can still open stored place details, saved places and the guides. Map tiles, routing, weather and photos need a connection, so load the trip before leaving Alice Springs. The app is for iPhone, and free to download, with in-app purchases.
tips: Load the trip in Alice Springs

faq: How long does it take to drive from Alice Springs to Uluru?

Plan on five to six hours of wheel time. OSRM, a routing engine built on OpenStreetMap data, returned 452 km and 5 h 11 min on 21 October 2026, and that excludes fuel and meal stops. Leave early if you want to reach the park before dark.
Is the Red Centre Way via Kings Canyon a good alternative?

It is a different trip rather than a shortcut. OSRM gave 633 km and 7 h 15 min through Kings Canyon Resort, and the Mereenie Loop part of the Red Centre Way is unsealed and needs a permit. The Stuart and Lasseter Highway drive stays on the sealed highway.
How much does it cost to enter Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park?

Adults pay $38 for a 3-day pass or $50 for an annual pass, and children and teenagers under 18 go free. A $109 annual pass exists for vehicles registered in the Northern Territory, though not for tour or hire vehicles. Parks Australia sells passes online, and you can also get one at the entry station.
Can I buy alcohol at Yulara to take back to my campsite?

Only if you are a guest. Ayers Rock Resort says takeaway alcohol is restricted to resort guests, with a bottle shop that opens from 12 pm to 9 pm and a daily limit per person. Bring what you need from Alice Springs, and check the Northern Territory Government's rules there first.

adelaide-to-port-lincoln-drive.title: Adelaide to Port Lincoln Drive 2026: Augusta and Lincoln Highways, Stops, Parks and Fruit Fly
adelaide-to-port-lincoln-drive.description: Adelaide to Port Lincoln is about 650 km and eight hours by the Augusta, Eyre and Lincoln Highways via Port Augusta, Whyalla, Cowell and Tumby Bay. Legs, fuel, caravan parks, dump points, Lincoln and Coffin Bay park fees and fruit fly rules.
adelaide-to-port-lincoln-drive.imageAlt: The Lincoln Highway running straight north of Cowell through low mallee scrub on the Eyre Peninsula
adelaide-to-port-lincoln-drive.intro: Adelaide to Port Lincoln is about 650 km, and OSRM routing gives 7 h 44 min, up the Augusta Highway to Port Augusta and then down the Eyre Peninsula on the Lincoln Highway through Whyalla and Cowell. It is a long day or an easy two days, and the road does not go near the sea for much of the way, so towns are the natural stops.

sections.heading: Adelaide to Port Lincoln: the road and the distances
body: The way out of Adelaide is Port Wakefield Road, which becomes the Augusta Highway (A1) at Port Wakefield. Wikipedia gives the Augusta Highway as 208.1 km to Port Augusta, mainly single carriageway with occasional overtaking lanes. It also says the first section, Port Wakefield to Lochiel, was duplicated, with about 29 km of dual carriageway largely completed by March 2025, and that a 10-year freight upgrade program from 2023 includes more overtaking lanes. Wikipedia says the Augusta Highway was once called the Princes Highway, though it does not join the Princes Highway in the south-east.

At Port Augusta you take the Eyre Highway for about 25 km by OSRM, then turn south-west at Lincoln Gap onto the Lincoln Highway (B100). Wikipedia says that road is 315 km, sealed, with one lane in each direction, few overtaking lanes and a mostly 110 km/h limit. It passes Whyalla, Cowell, Port Neill and Arno Bay, with the gulf visible only in glimpses, and ends at Port Lincoln. Tumby Bay sits off the highway near the Bratten Way junction.
tips: Augusta Highway: 208 km to Port Augusta
Tumby Bay is off the highway

table.caption: Adelaide to Port Lincoln in legs. Distances and times come from OSRM on OpenStreetMap data, worked out on 21 October 2026 for a car with no stops, with waypoints in each town centre.
head: Leg
Distance

sections.heading: Fuel and the longer gaps
body: No fuel station or opening time on this route could be confirmed for this guide, so treat every town as a place to check before you rely on it. What the highway tables do show is spacing. On the Lincoln Highway, Wikipedia puts Whyalla 47 km, Cowell 161 km, Arno Bay 198 km, Tumby Bay turn-off 269 km and Port Lincoln 315 km from Lincoln Gap. The widest gap between named towns is therefore Whyalla to Cowell, at about 107 km by OSRM and 114 km by those figures, with only a turn-off to the Middleback Range between.
Fill up in Port Augusta or Whyalla before that stretch, and top up again at Cowell or Arno Bay. The road trip fuel guide has the sums for your tank and any towing.

sections.heading: Road conditions on the Augusta and Lincoln Highways
body: Traffic SA is the state's page for roadworks, incidents and planned events, with a map of closures and delays. Roadworks on the route today could not be confirmed, and the department's pages blocked scripts. The freight upgrade on the Augusta Highway is a 10-year program, so allow for works between Port Wakefield and Port Augusta.

With few overtaking lanes on the Lincoln Highway, a long straight run behind a slower vehicle is likely, and Wikipedia describes the road as having many straight stretches and few steep inclines. Plan the day so the last leg into Port Lincoln does not fall at dusk.
tips: Check Traffic SA before you go
Expect works on the Augusta Highway
Few overtaking lanes on the Lincoln Highway

sections.heading: Where to stop and dump points
body: The AussieCamps data lists one campground near the road, Baroota Campground, 4.7 km off the route about 263 km from Adelaide, with no facilities listed. The towns hold the caravan parks. Discovery Parks lists Whyalla Foreshore Holiday and Caravan Park at 51 Broadbent Terrace, with a dump point, a camp kitchen and a laundry, and dogs allowed on sites and selected cabins. The South Australian Tourism Commission lists Cowell Foreshore Caravan Park on the Esplanade, with unpowered and powered sites, a camp kitchen and a dump point, and Tumby Bay Caravan Park at 47 Tumby Terrace, with powered sites from $43 for two people and a dump point. Ring the park before you arrive, because rates and availability may have changed.

The data lists dump points at Bunyip Park in Koolunga (10 km off the route, free, washout tap) and Point Gibbon near Cowell (5 km off, free, washout tap, toilets and showers). It lists no roadside rest areas within 15 km of the route, so nothing about rest areas is claimed here. The South Australia camping rules guide covers where you may and may not sleep.
tips: Caravan parks at Whyalla, Cowell and Tumby Bay
Dump points at Koolunga and Point Gibbon

sections.heading: Lincoln National Park and Coffin Bay National Park
body: Both parks are close to Port Lincoln, and the SA parks site lists the same vehicle entry fee for each: $14.40 per vehicle, paid before you arrive. Camping is from $23.10 a night, with fees paid before arrival, and the site says dogs are not permitted in either park. Lincoln National Park's entrance is 13 km south-west of Port Lincoln via Proper Bay Road. The site says there is no water in the park and you must bring your own, and that the park closes on Catastrophic Fire Danger days and may close on Extreme days. For closures it points to the CFS website or 1800 362 361.

Lincoln National Park's Surfleet, Taylors Landing and September Beach campgrounds suit caravans, camper vans and tents, and other sites are 4WD only. Coffin Bay National Park is 50 km west of Port Lincoln. Yangie Bay campground is 2WD and suits caravans, and its other named campgrounds are 4WD only. The site says not to tow vans along the Gunyah Beach track or beyond Yangie because of the difficult terrain. It also says to check tide times and avoid driving on beaches at high tide.
tips: No water in Lincoln National Park

sections.heading: Fruit fly rules in South Australia
body: Adelaide to Port Lincoln stays inside South Australia, so there is no border check. The state has its own fruit fly outbreaks, though. A search extract of the PIRSA outbreak page, updated on 12 October 2026, lists an Elizabeth East outbreak of Queensland fruit fly with an end date of 12 December 2026, and Riverland outbreaks with an end date of 3 January 2027. It describes a 1.5 km outbreak area and a 15 km suspension area around each detection. The extract says restrictions on moving fruit and vegetables grown within the red outbreak area remain in place.

The Riverland is not on this route. Whether the Elizabeth East zones touch your way out of Adelaide could not be confirmed, and PIRSA's pages blocked scripts, so check the outbreak map. The extract gives the fruit fly hotline as 1300 666 010. The interstate biosecurity guide covers produce at state borders.

sections.heading: Plan the Adelaide to Port Lincoln drive in AussieCamps
body: Build the drive as a trip in AussieCamps, adding Whyalla, Cowell and Port Lincoln as stops so each leg shows its distance and drive time, with a forecast for the day you arrive. The app holds 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and a place page lists the facilities those sources publish, plus a notes field for your own details.

Stored place details, saved places and guides open with no signal, while map tiles, routing, weather and photos need a connection, so load the trip before the Eyre Peninsula. The app is made for iPhone, and costs nothing to download, with in-app purchases.
tips: Check the forecast for each night

faq: How far is Port Lincoln from Adelaide by road?

About 650 km. OSRM, a routing engine running on OpenStreetMap data, returned 650 km and 7 h 44 min for the direct drive on 21 October 2026, or 673 km and 8 h 16 min when the route is forced through the centres of Whyalla, Cowell, Arno Bay and Tumby Bay. Most travellers split it with a night at Whyalla or Cowell.
Is the road to Port Lincoln mostly dual carriageway?

Only in parts. Per Wikipedia, the dual carriageway covers about 29 km out of Port Wakefield, and beyond it you share a two-way road to Port Augusta and all the way down the Lincoln Highway. Passing places are scarce on that second road, so a slow caravan can hold up a queue.
Do I pay to enter Lincoln National Park and Coffin Bay National Park?

Yes. The South Australian parks site lists vehicle entry at $14.40 for each park, with entry paid before you arrive, and camping from $23.10 a night. It says dogs are not permitted in either park, so pets need another plan.
Does the Riverland fruit fly outbreak affect this drive?

The Riverland is not on the route. PIRSA lists a separate outbreak at Elizabeth East in northern Adelaide, with an end date of 12 December 2026. Look at the PIRSA outbreak map before you leave to see whether its zones cover your way out of the city.

melbourne-to-mildura-drive.title: Melbourne to Mildura Drive 2026: Calder Highway Route, Fruit Fly Rules, Fuel and Camping
melbourne-to-mildura-drive.description: Melbourne to Mildura is about 542 km and 6 hours 45 minutes on the Calder Highway. Compared with the Sunraysia Highway, the 2024 fruit fly change, fuel, Hattah-Kulkyne camping and VicTraffic.
melbourne-to-mildura-drive.imageAlt: The Calder Highway curving past scrub and a vineyard at Merbein near Mildura under a clear blue sky
melbourne-to-mildura-drive.intro: Melbourne to Mildura is about 542 km and 6 h 46 min of driving on the Calder Freeway and Calder Highway through Bendigo, Charlton, Sea Lake and Ouyen, by OSRM routing. It is a long day or an easy two, and the things worth checking before you go are the 2024 change to fruit fly rules in Sunraysia, where you will fuel and rest between towns, and how heat affects a drive through the Mallee.

sections.heading: Melbourne to Mildura routes compared
body: The standard route leaves Melbourne on the Calder Freeway (M79) and becomes the Calder Highway (A79) near Bendigo. Wikipedia describes the Melbourne to Bendigo section as four-lane dual carriageway, and says that elsewhere in the Mallee the highway is a two-lane single carriageway, with a four-lane dual carriageway through southern Mildura and Irymple. It gives the limit as 110 km/h between Red Cliffs and Wycheproof. Wikipedia lists the distances from the Mildura end as Ouyen 123.9 km, Sea Lake 209.1 km, Wycheproof 288.0 km, Charlton 318.3 km and Bendigo 423.6 km.

The alternative is the Western Freeway to Ballarat, then the Sunraysia Highway (B220) through St Arnaud and Donald to Ouyen, where it meets the Calder Highway for the last 101 km to Mildura. Wikipedia gives the Sunraysia Highway as 330.2 km from Ouyen to Ballarat and says Mildura is reached by the Calder Highway, the main Melbourne to Mildura road. Every distance and time below comes from OSRM, run on OpenStreetMap data on 21 October 2026 for a car without stops. The Murray Valley Highway and a Horsham route were not researched, so only these two are compared.
tips: Mildura to Ouyen is single carriageway

sections.heading: Bendigo, Charlton, Sea Lake and Ouyen
body: By OSRM routing, the legs on the Calder route are Melbourne to Bendigo 151 km (1 h 57 min), Bendigo to Charlton 106 km (1 h 30 min), Charlton to Wycheproof 30 km (25 min), Wycheproof to Sea Lake 77 km (57 min), Sea Lake to Ouyen 89 km (1 h 03 min) and Ouyen to Mildura 101 km (1 h 16 min). Going through the middle of Bendigo adds about 13 km to the direct 542 km figure. If you split the drive, Bendigo is the natural place to stop at about 151 km, with 404 km and 5 h 14 min still to go to Mildura.

Lake Tyrrell is a short detour from Sea Lake. Wikipedia says it is 6 km north of the town, that its lookout is 7 to 8 km from the township, and that it is Victoria's largest salt lake at about 20,860 hectares. The page describes no camping at the lake. Wikipedia lists no facilities or fees for the lake, so check locally for access and rules. Mildura is the largest settlement in Sunraysia, with 35,652 people at the 2021 census, according to Wikipedia.
tips: Bendigo is the natural overnight at 151 km
Lake Tyrrell is 6 km north of Sea Lake

sections.heading: Fruit fly: what changed in Sunraysia
body: Agriculture Victoria says a Greater Sunraysia Pest Free Area was in place from 2006 to 2024, and that its regulation lapsed and ceased to exist in July 2024. The department says there are no longer restrictions around bringing Queensland fruit fly host produce into or out of the Sunraysia area, that the requirements for moving fruit to interstate Queensland fruit fly sensitive markets have not changed, and that signs and quarantine bins were being removed during 2025. Agriculture Victoria's own pages block automated requests, so these quotes come from search extracts of its page, and North West Farmer reported the same statement on 12 July 2024.

That is a change from older travel pages, including tourism pages that told drivers to put fruit in roadside bins before Mildura. The same department statement says restrictions on Mediterranean fruit fly host produce, which apply statewide, do not change, and the Lindsay Point Order for north-west Victoria remains in place to help South Australia keep its pest free area status in the Riverland. This guide could not confirm that every sign and bin has gone, so follow any that you meet. If you carry on into South Australia, Interstate Quarantine says a zero tolerance approach is in place and that quarantine stations and fruit disposal bins are placed throughout the state, so read the interstate biosecurity guide and the Melbourne to Adelaide guide before you cross.
tips: Greater Sunraysia area lapsed in July 2024
South Australia is the border that matters now

sections.heading: Fuel, rest areas and dump points
body: No operator or government source was found that lists the fuel stations or the gaps between them on the Calder Highway, so this guide gives only the OSRM distances between the towns: Wycheproof to Sea Lake 77 km, Sea Lake to Ouyen 89 km and Ouyen to Mildura 101 km. Those are the longest stretches between towns, so top up in a town rather than running the tank low, and confirm that a station is open before you count on it. The fuel planning guide helps you budget range.

Within 15 km of this route the AussieCamps data holds no roadside rest area and no dump point, and that reflects what the data covers, not what exists. Its nearest dump points are Lowan Park at Manangatang (free, with toilets and showers, about 23 km off the route) and Godfrey Street (Nolans Park) at Boort (about 31 km off). Whether you may sleep at a rest area you find is a separate question, answered in the overnight rest area guide and the Victorian camping rules, and the dump points guide has more places to empty a cassette.
tips: Longest town gap is Ouyen to Mildura, 101 km
No rest areas in the data on this road
Dump points are off the route

sections.heading: Road conditions, tolls and heat
body: Open VicTraffic on the morning you leave. The Department of Transport and Planning says it shows real-time road conditions, traffic alerts, incidents and planned roadworks, including road closures and emergency events such as bushfires or flooding, and a search extract gives the VicRoads Traffic Management Centre on 13 11 70. VicEmergency does not issue separate road closure warnings, according to its support page, which leaves VicTraffic as the place to look for closures. No official closure, flood or roadworks notice for the Calder Highway was found on 21 October 2026, so none is described here.

Wikipedia gives Mildura a January mean daily maximum of 33.3 C and a record of 48.6 C, so carry plenty of water and start early in summer. The Calder Freeway meets the Tullamarine Freeway at Airport West, and whether your start in Melbourne uses a toll road depends on where you set off. Linkt says its Visitor's Pass covers CityLink and EastLink for up to 30 days, for $3.50 online or $5.00 by phone, and covers CityLink trips made up to 5 days ago and EastLink trips made up to 3 days ago. The fatigue and wildlife guide covers driving at dawn and dusk.

sections.heading: Camping on the way: Hattah-Kulkyne National Park
body: Hattah-Kulkyne National Park, near Hattah, is the one campground area the AussieCamps data lists within 15 km of this route: Lake Hattah and Lake Mournpall camping areas, each about 6 km off the highway. Parks Victoria says fees apply at both, that dogs are not allowed, and its Lake Hattah page also lists no horses, no generators and no firearms. Its pages send you to the Parks Victoria booking site and give 13 1963 for fees, and they did not list the rate or the facilities, so check them before you go. Wikipedia describes the park as about 48,000 hectares, with most lakes and streams drying out in the dry season.

Parks Victoria's park page lists works in the northern part of the park under the Victorian Murray Floodplain Restoration Project to December 2026, with increased heavy vehicle movement and temporary track closures, and track closures at Raak Track and Goosefoot Track because of fire impacts. Read the park notices on the day. For rules on free camping and rest areas, see the camping rules guide for Victoria. The Victorian high country guide covers the other end of the state.
tips: Fees apply: check the booking site
Read the Parks Victoria notices on the day

sections.heading: Plan the Melbourne to Mildura drive in AussieCamps
body: Build this drive as a trip in AussieCamps with a Bendigo stop, a fuel stop at Sea Lake or Ouyen and a Hattah-Kulkyne campground. Each leg shows its distance and drive time, plus a forecast for your arrival day, which counts in Mallee heat. The app holds 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points drawn from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, Parks Victoria campgrounds among them, and each place page carries the photos, weather and facilities those sources publish.

With no signal you still have stored place details, saved places and guides, but map tiles, routing, weather and photos need a connection, so load the trip while you are still in Melbourne. It runs on iPhone only and costs nothing to download, with in-app purchases on offer. For the road west from here, read the Melbourne to Adelaide guide.
tips: A forecast for each arrival day

faq: How many hours is Melbourne to Mildura by car?
Allow roughly 6 h 46 min of wheel time for the 542 km up the Calder, before fuel and food stops. A night in Bendigo splits it into a short first day and a 5 h 14 min second one.
Do I have to give up fruit when I arrive in Mildura or Sunraysia?

The old bin-and-sign system ended with the pest free area itself. Agriculture Victoria's current page says Queensland fruit fly host produce can now move in and out of Sunraysia without those restrictions, while its statewide Medfly rules are unchanged. Older travel pages still mention roadside bins, so go by the department's page rather than by them.
Is the Sunraysia Highway via Ballarat a quicker way to Mildura?
No, it adds about 15 km and 38 minutes. The OSRM figure for the Ballarat, St Arnaud, Donald and Ouyen line is 557 km and 7 h 24 min, which makes it a scenic choice rather than a shortcut.
Where can I camp between Melbourne and Mildura?

The AussieCamps data has Lake Hattah and Lake Mournpall camping areas in Hattah-Kulkyne National Park, between Ouyen and Mildura, with fees and no dogs per Parks Victoria. Nothing else sits within 15 km of the highway in the data, so look up caravan parks in the larger towns before you set off.

townsville-to-mount-isa-drive.title: Townsville to Mount Isa Drive 2026: Flinders Highway Route, Flood Closures, Fuel and Free Camps
townsville-to-mount-isa-drive.description: Townsville to Mount Isa is about 905 km and 11 hours on the Flinders and Barkly Highways. Legs, wet season flood closures, QLDTraffic, fuel, road trains, Julia Creek and Porcupine Gorge camping.
townsville-to-mount-isa-drive.imageAlt: A cattle road train driving past a blue and yellow monument on a street in Hughenden, Queensland, on the Flinders Highway
townsville-to-mount-isa-drive.intro: Townsville to Mount Isa is about 905 km and 11 h 06 min of driving along the Flinders Highway, known as the Overlanders Way, and then the Barkly Highway from Cloncurry. Plan two days at least, and decide on the season before the stops: the stretch around Richmond and Julia Creek has closed under floodwater in recent wet seasons, and towns are the only fuel and shade you can count on.

sections.heading: The Flinders Highway route and its legs
body: Only one route is covered here, because this guide checked no other road between the two cities. Wikipedia gives the Flinders Highway as route A6, 775 km from Townsville to Cloncurry and sealed throughout, with the last section finished in November 1976, and says the Barkly Highway (A2) runs west from Cloncurry to Mount Isa. It describes the Overlanders Way as a Queensland State Strategic Touring Route that continues to Tennant Creek. RACQ puts the Townsville to Mount Isa distance at approximately 905 km and recommends April to October for the trip.

The legs below are OSRM figures from town centre to town centre, computed on 21 October 2026, so they add up to about 909 km against the 905 km direct. Tourism NT's itinerary splits the middle as Hughenden to Richmond 115 km and Richmond to Julia Creek 149 km, which the Hughenden to Julia Creek leg includes.
tips: April to October is the RACQ window

sections.heading: Where to stop overnight
body: Hughenden is the natural halfway stop: OSRM puts it 384 km and 4 h 44 min from Townsville, leaving 521 km to Mount Isa. Visit Hughenden describes a council RV park designed for fully self-contained travellers, with a stay of up to 7 nights and a permit by self-registration on site, and its page gives no fee. It also lists Allen Terry Caravan Park on Resolution Street, with amenities, laundry, a fire pit, a dump point and a vehicle wash-down bay.

Julia Creek is the second stop. McKinlay Shire Council describes a designated free camping area on the water's edge, 1.3 km on the eastern side of town, for self-contained RVs, and says portable showers do not count as self-contained. Permits are free and valid for 96 hours, from the camp hosts from April to September and from the Julia Creek Visitor Information Centre from October to March. The council's page lists no open fires and no dumping of black or grey water. Out of Townsville, the AussieCamps data lists Alligator Creek camping area in the Mount Elliot area, about 25 km from the start and 9 km off the highway, with toilets, drinking water and camper trailer sites. Fees and bookings were not checked, so look at the Queensland Parks page before you go. Cloncurry and Mount Isa camping could not be confirmed from council pages, so book a caravan park there before you leave.
tips: Julia Creek permit: 96 hours, self-contained only
Book Cloncurry and Mount Isa ahead

sections.heading: Wet season floods and live road information
body: Check QLDTraffic, which the Department of Transport and Main Roads runs and which maps hazards, crashes, flooding, roadworks and special events. Drive North West QLD gives the number 13 19 40 for current conditions and says summer travel, November to April, can be affected when rain and storms impede plans. McKinlay Shire Council's Flinders Highway road report, current at 4.30 pm on 11 March 2026, showed Julia Creek to Richmond closed by flooding on Boundary Creek and Julia Creek to Cloncurry closed at Eastern Creek Bridge with 300 mm of water over it.

A Queensland Government statement of 15 February 2019 described the highway closed between Richmond and Julia Creek, with traffic detoured through the Landsborough Highway, Winton and Hughenden, and said the worst-hit sections would stay shut for some time. Drive North West QLD adds that water crossings should not be attempted if you are unsure of your vehicle's capabilities. If you are travelling between November and April, leave slack in the plan and expect to wait in a town rather than push on.
tips: March 2026: closed at Boundary and Eastern Creeks
Leave slack from November to April

sections.heading: Fuel, road trains and tiredness
body: No fuel station list from an operator or a Queensland Government source turned up for this road, so no station is recommended by name here. Drive North West QLD says fuel stops on major highways are rarely more than 200 km apart and that a no fuel sign means none is available. Wikipedia's highway table shows Torrens Creek at 284 km from Townsville, 162 km after Charters Towers at 122 km, and an Outback Queensland listing for the Oasis Exchange Hotel there mentions a petrol station, though it is undated. The table lists no town between Julia Creek (637 km) and Cloncurry (759 km), so fill up at the town you leave rather than hoping for the next one.

The road trains guide covers overtaking and passing in detail. Drive North West QLD says that when a road train approaches to overtake you, you should move as far left as possible and stop if necessary, and that you should allow plenty of room when passing because they may move from side to side. It also says long, unchanging stretches can make a driver very tired and advises avoiding night driving as much as possible. The road trip fuel guide helps you budget range.
tips: Fill up in the town you leave
Move left and stop for an overtaking road train

sections.heading: Porcupine Gorge National Park
body: Porcupine Gorge is a side trip north of Hughenden on the Kennedy Developmental Road. Queensland Parks says, in a search extract of its page, that the access to the lookout and camping area is fully sealed, that the lookout turn-off is 60 km north of Hughenden, and that the Pyramid camping area, day-use area and walking track turn-off is a further 11.7 km north. It says camping at the Pyramid area needs a permit booked online before your visit, well ahead in peak season from April to October, and that fees apply. The fee amounts were not available to this guide.

Visit Hughenden says the Pyramid campground suits tents, caravans, camper trailers and motorhomes, with composting toilets and picnic tables, that campfires are allowed only in the steel fire rings and you must bring your own firewood, and that generators are not permitted. It says pets are not allowed because it is a national park. The Queensland camping rules guide covers the wider rules.
tips: Book Pyramid online before you go
Sealed all the way from Hughenden

sections.heading: Rest areas and dump points
body: Within 15 km of the route the AussieCamps data lists no roadside rest area, which only describes what the data holds. The overnight rest area guide explains where sleeping in a vehicle is and is not allowed. The data does list a free dump point at Cloncurry/Mary Kathleen Memorial Park, with drinking water, toilets and accessible parking, and no washout tap shown. Visit Hughenden says Allen Terry Caravan Park has a dump point, and the dump points guide lists others to look up.
Mobile coverage along the highway was not confirmed from any official source, so download the route and your bookings before you leave Townsville and tell someone your plan.
tips: Dump point at Cloncurry in the data
Another at Allen Terry Caravan Park

sections.heading: Plan the Townsville to Mount Isa drive in AussieCamps
body: Build the drive as a trip in AussieCamps: Townsville, Hughenden, Julia Creek, Cloncurry and Mount Isa as stops, so each leg shows its distance, drive time and a forecast for the day you expect to arrive. The app holds 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points sourced from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and a place page for a Queensland park shows its photos, facilities and the weather forecast.

Out of signal, stored place details, saved places and guides still open, whereas map tiles, routing, weather and photos want a connection, so set the trip up in Townsville. It is iPhone only and costs nothing to download, with in-app purchases available. For the coast road north, read the Brisbane to Cairns guide, and the Queensland Outback Way guide covers the outback road to the south.
tips: Set it up while you have signal

faq: How far is Townsville to Mount Isa by road?

RACQ gives the Overlanders Way from Townsville to Mount Isa as approximately 905 km, and an OSRM calculation lands on the same figure with about 11 hours of wheel time. Two driving days is the practical minimum, and Hughenden sits close to the middle.
Does the Flinders Highway flood?

Yes. In March 2026 a McKinlay Shire Council road report showed the highway shut at Boundary Creek west of Richmond and at Eastern Creek Bridge near Julia Creek, and in February 2019 a Queensland Government statement described it closed for some time after major flooding. A sealed road does not mean an open one in the wet, so look at QLDTraffic before each leg.
Is there free camping between Townsville and Mount Isa?

Two council sites are confirmed. McKinlay Shire runs a free RV site at Julia Creek for fully self-contained vehicles, and Visit Hughenden describes a council RV park for self-contained travellers. Both are for self-contained vehicles only, and camping at the Cloncurry and Mount Isa end could not be confirmed from council pages.
Can I camp at Porcupine Gorge without booking?
No booking, no site. Queensland Parks says camping at the Pyramid area needs a permit booked online before you visit, and that fees apply. The road in from Hughenden is sealed all the way.

melbourne-to-perth-drive.title: Melbourne to Perth Drive 2026: Route, Days, Fuel Stops and Camping Across the Nullarbor
melbourne-to-perth-drive.description: Melbourne to Perth is about 3,400 km and five to seven days by Adelaide and the Nullarbor. Day-by-day stops, fuel gaps, the WA border checkpoint, free camps and caravan parks.
melbourne-to-perth-drive.region: Victoria, South Australia and Western Australia
melbourne-to-perth-drive.imageAlt: The Eyre Highway running straight across the flat Nullarbor Plain under a wide blue sky
melbourne-to-perth-drive.intro: Melbourne to Perth is about 3,400 km, the longest standard drive between two Australian capitals, and most of it is a single line across South Australia and the Nullarbor. Done in five to seven days it is a steady drive rather than a race, with a few big decisions: where to sleep each night, how to cover the fuel gaps and what to eat before the Western Australian border.

sections.heading: The route and how many days to allow
body: The usual route leaves Melbourne on the Western Highway through Ballarat and Horsham, crosses into South Australia and joins the Princes Highway to Adelaide, then takes the Augusta Highway to Port Augusta and the Eyre Highway west across the Nullarbor to Norseman. From Norseman you either turn south-west to Perth by Ravensthorpe and Wagin or go through Kalgoorlie and the Great Eastern Highway, which is the more common choice with a campervan.

Five days works if you are happy to drive six to eight hours a day. Seven is kinder, and the extra days are better spent near Adelaide or the Nullarbor cliffs than on the road. The Adelaide to Melbourne guide covers the first leg in more detail, and the Nullarbor guide covers the second.
tips: Five days at six to eight hours
Adelaide is the natural halfway stop

table.caption: A realistic five to seven day split. Distances are approximate.
head: Leg
Distance

Where to stop
rows: Port Augusta, Iron Knob or Ceduna

sections.heading: Fuel, water and the long gaps
body: Between Ceduna and Norseman the roadhouses are the only fuel, and the gaps are long enough that you should fill up at every one rather than push on to a cheaper price. Fuel on the Nullarbor is dearer than in the cities, and diesel or petrol sometimes runs short at a small roadhouse, so do not arrive at the last stop on fumes.

Carry more water than you think you need, drink it and keep spare in the van. The road trip fuel planning guide shows how to work out a range for a campervan, and the road trains guide explains how to pass the long trucks safely on the single carriageway.

sections.heading: Camping across the Nullarbor
body: Most nights on this drive are in caravan parks, roadhouse camps or free rest areas. Port Augusta, Ceduna, Eucla, Balladonia and Norseman all have a roadhouse or park with powered and unpowered sites, and there are free rest areas and bush stops between them where overnight stays are allowed. Rules differ by state, so check the camping rules guides for South Australia and Western Australia, and the overnight rest area guide before you plan a free night.

The Nullarbor guide lists the cliff and bight lookouts and the best free camps. Arrive before dusk: kangaroos, emus and wedge-tailed eagles are active at dawn and dusk and the road has little lighting.
tips: Roadhouse camps are the easy option
Free rest areas exist but check the rules
Avoid driving at dusk and dawn

sections.heading: The Western Australian border checkpoint
body: Western Australia runs a quarantine checkpoint on the Eyre Highway near Eucla, and it is strict about fresh fruit, vegetables, honey, plants and some other items. Eat what you can before the border and put the rest in the bin at the checkpoint. The biosecurity guide explains the rules for each state and what happens if you carry something you should not.

The border also changes the clock. South Australia and Western Australia are in different time zones, and the area around Eucla keeps an unofficial time in between, so your phone may jump forward or back at unexpected moments. Plan the last day with that in mind so you do not arrive in Perth in the dark.
tips: No fresh fruit or veg over the border

sections.heading: Plan the Melbourne to Perth drive in AussieCamps
body: Build the drive as a trip in AussieCamps: add Adelaide, Port Augusta, Ceduna, Eucla, Norseman and Kalgoorlie in order and it shows the distance and drive time of each leg, with a forecast for the day you expect to arrive. AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and each place page shows the facilities those sources publish.
Open the trip before you leave Adelaide, because map tiles, routing and weather need a connection and the Nullarbor has very little. The iPhone app is free to download, with in-app purchases.
tips: Add each overnight stop in order
Open the trip before the Nullarbor

faq: How long does it take to drive from Melbourne to Perth?

It is about 3,400 km by the Western Highway, the Princes Highway through Adelaide and the Eyre Highway across the Nullarbor, which is roughly 38 to 42 hours behind the wheel. Most people take five to seven days so that nobody drives more than six or seven hours a day.
What is the longest gap without fuel between Melbourne and Perth?
The longest stretches are on the Nullarbor, where roadhouses can be 150 to 200 km apart. Fill up at every roadhouse and carry water; the fuel planning guide covers the numbers for a campervan.
Can I take fruit and vegetables across the Western Australian border?
No. Western Australia runs a quarantine checkpoint at Eucla and the Nullarbor, and fresh fruit, vegetables, honey and some other items are not allowed in. Eat or bin them before the border.
Does the clock change on the way to Perth?

Yes. South Australia is on its own time, the Eucla area keeps an unofficial time between the two, and Western Australia is two or three hours behind Victoria depending on the season. Allow for it when you plan a day's driving.

perth-to-darwin-drive.title: Perth to Darwin Drive 2026: Route, Days, Fuel and Camping Along the West Coast and Kimberley
perth-to-darwin-drive.description: Perth to Darwin is about 4,000 km and eight to fourteen days by the coast, the Pilbara, Broome and the Kimberley. Day-by-day plan, fuel gaps, dry season timing, free camps and caravan parks.
perth-to-darwin-drive.region: Western Australia and the Northern Territory
perth-to-darwin-drive.imageAlt: A boab tree beside the Great Northern Highway in the Kimberley under a clear dry-season sky
perth-to-darwin-drive.intro: Perth to Darwin is about 4,000 km along the west coast, through the Pilbara and across the Kimberley, and it is one of the great Australian road trips. It is sealed the whole way and can be done in about eight days at a stretch, but ten to fourteen days lets you stop at Karijini, Broome and Kununurra and is the version most people remember.

sections.heading: The route and how long it takes
body: From Perth the Brand and North West Coastal Highways run north past Geraldton and Carnarvon to the Pilbara, then the Great Northern Highway continues through Port Hedland and Broome. From Broome the Great Northern Highway swings inland through Fitzroy Crossing and Halls Creek to Kununurra, and the Victoria Highway carries you across the border to Katherine, then the Stuart Highway north to Darwin.

The Perth to Broome guide covers the first half in detail and the Broome to Darwin guide covers the second, so this page is the plan that joins them up. On the coast you can break the trip at Kalbarri, Coral Bay and Karijini; in the Kimberley you can add the Bungle Bungles or the Gibb River Road with extra days.
tips: Eight days is a hard minimum
Add Karijini, Broome or Kununurra on the way

sections.heading: Fuel, water and long gaps
body: Services are spaced out on this road, and some stretches in the Pilbara and the Kimberley are 150 to 300 km between fuel stops. Fill up at every roadhouse and town, and carry spare water, food and a basic kit in case of a breakdown. The road trip fuel planning guide shows how to work out the range for a campervan.

Road trains use the highway, so give them room and pass them with care. The driving with road trains guide covers the rules, and the fatigue guide covers the rest breaks that matter on a drive this long.

sections.heading: When to go
body: The dry season, from about May to September, is the sensible time to drive from Perth to Darwin: skies are clear, nights are cool and the roads are open. In the wet season, from roughly November to April, heat, storms and cyclones can close roads and some camps and gorges, and the wet season camping guide for the Top End and northern Western Australia covers what changes.
School holidays and the dry season mean popular camps and caravan parks in Broome and Kununurra fill early, so book ahead for those nights.
tips: May to September is the safe window
Wet season closes roads and camps

sections.heading: Camping on the way
body: Caravan parks and roadhouse camps carry most nights: Geraldton, Carnarvon, Karratha, Port Hedland, Broome, Fitzroy Crossing, Kununurra and Katherine all have parks, and there are free rest areas and bush camps between towns. The camping rules guides for Western Australia and the Northern Territory explain where overnight stays are allowed, and the overnight rest area guide covers the common sign and rule differences.
Check camp availability and any national park booking before you drive to Karijini, Cape Range or Purnululu, as these are busy in the dry season.

body: Build the drive as a trip in AussieCamps: add Geraldton, Carnarvon, Karratha, Broome, Kununurra and Katherine in order and it shows the distance and drive time of each leg, with a forecast for the day you expect to arrive. AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and each place page shows the facilities those sources publish.
Open the trip while you still have a connection, because map tiles, routing and weather need one and the Pilbara and Kimberley have little. The iPhone app is free to download, with in-app purchases.
tips: Add each overnight stop in order
Open the trip before the long legs

faq: How far is Perth to Darwin by road?

It is about 4,000 km by the Great Northern Highway to Broome and the Great Northern and Victoria Highways on to Darwin. Allow at least eight to ten days if you want to camp and see things on the way, and two weeks or more if you add Karijini, the Kimberley and Kakadu.
What is the best time of year to drive Perth to Darwin?
The dry season, from about May to September, is the sensible window. In the wet season, from roughly November to April, heat, storms and flooding can close roads and some camps and gorges.
Do I need a 4WD to drive from Perth to Darwin?
No. The main route is sealed all the way, and a campervan or a car handles it. A 4WD is only needed if you add side trips such as the Gibb River Road.
Where do I stop for fuel on the way to Darwin?

Roadhouses and towns such as Geraldton, Carnarvon, Port Hedland, Broome, Fitzroy Crossing, Kununurra and Katherine are the main fuel stops. Gaps between them can be 150 to 300 km, so fill up at each one.

brisbane-to-darwin-drive.title: Brisbane to Darwin Drive 2026: Outback Route via Mount Isa and the Barkly, Fuel and Camping
brisbane-to-darwin-drive.description: Brisbane to Darwin is about 3,400 km and six to ten days across the Queensland outback and the Barkly Tableland. Route, fuel gaps, road trains, caravan parks and free camps.
brisbane-to-darwin-drive.imageAlt: A road train on the Barkly Highway crossing the flat grass plains of the outback
brisbane-to-darwin-drive.intro: Brisbane to Darwin is about 3,400 km across the heart of the outback, from Queensland's coast to the Top End. It is a big, quiet road with long gaps between towns, and it rewards a few extra days at Longreach, Mount Isa and Katherine rather than a straight-through race.

sections.heading: The route and the days it takes
body: The usual route leaves Brisbane on the Warrego Highway through Toowoomba and Roma, then takes the Landsborough Highway through Charleville, Longreach and Winton to Cloncurry and Mount Isa. West of Mount Isa the Barkly Highway crosses the Barkly Tableland to Three Ways, where it meets the Stuart Highway, and from there you turn north through Daly Waters and Katherine to Darwin.

Allow six days at a steady pace, or ten if you want to see Longreach, Mount Isa and Katherine Gorge properly. The Townsville to Mount Isa guide covers a northern alternative, and the Cairns to Darwin guide covers a route along the Gulf.
tips: Six days at seven hours a day
Ten if you want to see things
Mount Isa is the natural halfway stop

sections.heading: Fuel, water and road trains
body: Fuel stops are widely spaced on the Barkly and Stuart Highways, and a long stretch between Camooweal and Barkly Roadhouse has nothing in between. Fill up at every roadhouse and carry spare water and food in case of a delay. The road trip fuel planning guide covers range for a campervan.

Road trains, the very long trucks that run on these roads, need a lot of room to stop and overtake. The road trains guide explains how to pass them and when to pull over, and the fatigue guide covers the breaks that matter on a drive this long.
tips: Give road trains plenty of room

sections.heading: Camping on the Brisbane to Darwin drive
body: Caravan parks and roadhouse camps carry most nights, with free rest areas and bush camps between them. Charleville, Longreach, Winton, Mount Isa, Tennant Creek and Katherine all have parks, and the camping rules guides for Queensland and the Northern Territory explain where overnight stays are allowed on public land.
Check the overnight rest area guide for the common rest area rules. In the dry season, from about May to September, outback camps fill, so book Longreach, Mount Isa and Katherine early.

faq: How far is Brisbane to Darwin by road?
About 3,400 km by the Warrego, Landsborough, Barkly and Stuart Highways via Mount Isa and Tennant Creek. It is roughly 40 hours of driving, so most people take six to ten days.
Which route is best from Brisbane to Darwin?

The usual route goes west through Charleville and Longreach or Cloncurry to Mount Isa, then across the Barkly Tableland to the Stuart Highway at Three Ways and north through Katherine. The east coast route via Cairns is longer and slower.
Are there long gaps without fuel on this drive?
Yes. The Barkly Highway and the Stuart Highway north of Tennant Creek have long stretches between roadhouses, so fill up at every one and carry water.
Can I drive Brisbane to Darwin in a 2WD campervan?
Yes. The route is sealed all the way, so a standard campervan or car is fine. Watch for road trains, livestock and wildlife.

brisbane-to-adelaide-drive.title: Brisbane to Adelaide Drive 2026: Route, Days, Fuel and Camping Through the Inland
brisbane-to-adelaide-drive.description: Brisbane to Adelaide is about 2,050 km and three to four days through the Newell Highway, Dubbo and Mildura. Route, stops, fuel, biosecurity rules, caravan parks and free camps.
brisbane-to-adelaide-drive.region: Queensland, New South Wales, Victoria and South Australia
brisbane-to-adelaide-drive.imageAlt: The Newell Highway running through flat wheat country in northern New South Wales
brisbane-to-adelaide-drive.intro: Brisbane to Adelaide is about 2,050 km inland through three states, the quickest way across the east of the country without going near the coast. It is a working road, mostly the Newell Highway, with wheat and cotton country in the middle and the Murray River at the end, and three or four days gives time to enjoy it.

sections.heading: The route and how long it takes
body: From Brisbane the usual route climbs to Toowoomba, crosses the border at Goondiwindi and follows the Newell Highway through Moree, Narrabri and Dubbo, where it meets the Mitchell Highway. From Dubbo you can continue to Parkes and Condobolin, then take the Mid-Western Highway or the Cobb Highway towards the Murray River at Mildura or Balranald, and the Sturt and Dukes Highways on to Adelaide.

The Melbourne to Brisbane guide covers the Newell Highway in more detail, and the Sydney to Adelaide guide covers the Murray end of the drive. Allow three days if you are happy to drive eight to ten hours, or four for a more relaxed pace.
tips: Dubbo and Mildura are good stops

sections.heading: Fuel, towns and driving
body: Towns are close together on the Newell Highway, so fuel is easy, but the Mid-Western and Sturt Highways to the Murray have longer gaps. Fill up when you pass half a tank, and take rest breaks every two hours. The fuel planning guide covers range for a campervan, and the fatigue guide covers the stops that matter.

The Newell Highway carries a lot of trucks and road trains, so give them room and pass on the dual carriageway where you can. In the evening and early morning kangaroos and livestock are common beside the road.
tips: Fill up at half a tank

sections.heading: Camping and caravan parks
body: Caravan parks carry most nights: Toowoomba, Goondiwindi, Moree, Narrabri, Dubbo, Parkes, Mildura and Renmark all have parks, and there are free rest areas and bush camps between the towns. The camping rules guides for New South Wales and South Australia explain where overnight stays are allowed, and the overnight rest area guide covers the signs and rules.
A stop at the Murray River, at Mildura or Renmark, makes a pleasant last night before Adelaide, and there are riverside camps along the way.

sections.heading: Biosecurity and borders
body: Crossing between states means crossing fruit fly and biosecurity rules, and South Australia in particular runs roadside bins and checkpoints near its borders. Eat or bin fresh fruit and vegetables before you cross, and check the interstate biosecurity guide for the rules on honey, plants and firewood.
Daylight saving also changes at the borders, so check the time before you plan a long last day.
tips: Mind daylight saving at the border

AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and each place page shows the facilities those sources publish.
Open the trip while you still have a connection, because map tiles, routing and weather need one. The iPhone app is free to download, with in-app purchases.

faq: How far is Brisbane to Adelaide by road?
About 2,050 km, which is roughly 22 to 24 hours of driving. Most people take three to four days, with nights at Dubbo or Parkes, Mildura or Broken Hill and Adelaide.
Which route is best from Brisbane to Adelaide?

The Newell Highway through Goondiwindi, Moree and Dubbo is the usual route, joining the Mid-Western and Sturt Highways towards Mildura and Adelaide. A coastal alternative through Sydney and Melbourne is much longer.
Is there a fruit fly checkpoint on the way?

Yes. Moving between Queensland, New South Wales, Victoria and South Australia crosses areas with biosecurity rules, and South Australia runs roadside bins and checkpoints near the border. Eat or bin fresh fruit and vegetables before you cross.
Can I drive Brisbane to Adelaide in two days?
It is possible but long, at more than ten hours a day. Three or four days is far more comfortable and gives time to stop at Dubbo, Mildura or the Murray River.

brisbane-to-airlie-beach-drive.title: Brisbane to Airlie Beach Drive 2026: Bruce Highway Route, Stops and Camping
brisbane-to-airlie-beach-drive.description: Brisbane to Airlie Beach is about 1,130 km and two to three days on the Bruce Highway. Stops at Bundaberg, 1770 and Rockhampton, fuel, flood closures, caravan parks and free camps.
brisbane-to-airlie-beach-drive.imageAlt: The Whitsunday coast at Airlie Beach with the lagoon in the foreground and islands in the distance
brisbane-to-airlie-beach-drive.intro: Brisbane to Airlie Beach is about 1,130 km up the Queensland coast on the Bruce Highway, and it is the classic first leg to the Whitsundays. Two long days will do it, three is better, and the stops at Hervey Bay, Bundaberg and Agnes Water are good enough that many people take longer.

sections.heading: The route and how long it takes
body: The route is the Bruce Highway (Highway 1) the whole way, through Gympie, Maryborough, Gin Gin, Gladstone, Rockhampton, Sarina and Mackay. From Proserpine you turn east on the Airlie Beach Road for the last 25 km. It is a continuous road with towns every hour or so, which makes it easy to plan overnight stops.

Allow two long days of about seven hours each, or three days with stops. The Brisbane to Cairns guide covers the rest of the Queensland coast if you are going further north, and the east coast road trip guide covers the whole Sydney to Cairns drive.
tips: Airlie Beach is 25 km off the highway

sections.heading: Fuel, traffic and flood closures
body: Fuel is easy to find along the Bruce Highway, with a town or roadhouse about every hour. The road is busy and has stretches of single carriageway with trucks and caravans, so rest every two hours and avoid driving at dusk and dawn when wildlife is active. The fatigue guide covers the breaks that matter.

In the wet season, from about November to April, floods and cyclones can close sections of the highway. Check QLDTraffic before you leave and again each morning, and the wet season guides cover what to do if a road is closed.

sections.heading: Camping and caravan parks
body: Caravan parks carry most nights: Hervey Bay, Bundaberg, Agnes Water, Gladstone, Rockhampton, Mackay and Airlie Beach all have parks, and there are free rest areas and showgrounds along the way. The camping rules guide for Queensland covers where overnight stays are allowed, and the overnight rest area guide covers signs and local rules.
Airlie Beach and Cannonvale are busy in the dry season and school holidays, so book ahead for the Whitsundays. If you cannot get a site at Airlie, Proserpine and Bowen have good alternatives.

sections.heading: Plan the Brisbane to Airlie Beach drive in AussieCamps

AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds, 5,552 rest areas and 1,393 dump points from park agencies, road authorities and public datasets, and each place page shows the facilities those sources publish.
Open the trip while you still have a connection, because map tiles, routing and weather need one. The iPhone app is free to download, with in-app purchases.

faq: How far is Brisbane to Airlie Beach?
About 1,130 km on the Bruce Highway, which is roughly 13 to 14 hours of driving. Most people split it over two or three days with stops at Bundaberg, Gladstone or Rockhampton.
Is the Bruce Highway safe to drive in a campervan?
Yes, but it is busy and has stretches of single carriageway, so take your time, rest every two hours and avoid driving at dusk when wildlife is active. Check QLDTraffic for flood and works closures.
Where should I stop between Brisbane and Airlie Beach?
Popular stops are Hervey Bay for whale watching, Bundaberg for the rum distillery and turtle rookery at Mon Repos, Agnes Water and the Town of 1770, Gladstone, Rockhampton and Mackay.
Do I need to book a campsite in the Whitsundays?
Yes, in the busy dry season. Airlie Beach, Proserpine and Cannonvale caravan parks fill quickly in winter school holidays, so book ahead.

sydney-to-byron-bay-drive.title: Sydney to Byron Bay Drive 2026: Pacific Highway Route, Stops, Tolls and Camping
sydney-to-byron-bay-drive.description: Sydney to Byron Bay is about 770 km and two days on the Pacific Highway. Stops at Newcastle, Port Macquarie and Coffs Harbour, tolls for visitors, fuel, caravan parks and free camps.
sydney-to-byron-bay-drive.imageAlt: Cape Byron lighthouse and the headland above the sea at Byron Bay
sydney-to-byron-bay-drive.intro: Sydney to Byron Bay is about 770 km up the Pacific Highway, and it is the classic north coast drive: beaches, national parks and small towns every hour or so. You can do it in one very long day, but two days is far kinder, and three gives you time for Port Macquarie and Coffs Harbour.

sections.heading: The route and how long it takes
body: The route is the Pacific Highway the whole way, leaving Sydney on the M1 through the Central Coast to Newcastle, then north through Taree, Port Macquarie, Kempsey, Coffs Harbour, Grafton and Ballina to Byron Bay. Almost all of it is dual carriageway now, with towns every hour or so for fuel and breaks.

The Brisbane to Byron Bay guide covers the northern end and the Brisbane to Sydney guide covers the whole highway, so this page is for the Sydney start. Allow two days at a steady pace, or three if you want to see Port Stephens, Port Macquarie or Coffs Harbour.

sections.heading: Tolls and driving
body: The Sydney end of the drive has tolled motorways, depending on where you start, and the toll roads guide explains the visitor options and how long you have to pay. North of Newcastle the Pacific Highway is toll free.

Fuel is easy to find along the highway. Rest every two hours, and avoid driving at dusk and dawn when kangaroos and wallabies are active. Live Traffic NSW shows closures and roadworks, and the fatigue guide covers the breaks that matter.

sections.heading: Camping on the north coast
body: Caravan parks and holiday parks carry most nights: Port Stephens, Port Macquarie, Coffs Harbour, Yamba, Ballina and Byron Bay all have parks, and there are national park campgrounds and free rest areas along the way. The camping rules guide for New South Wales covers where overnight stays are allowed, and the overnight rest area guide covers the signs.
Byron Bay has strict rules about camping and campervans, and parks fill quickly in summer and school holidays, so book ahead. Ballina, Brunswick Heads and Lennox Head are good alternatives close by.

faq: How far is Sydney to Byron Bay by road?

About 770 km on the Pacific Highway, which is roughly 8.5 to 9 hours of driving. Most people take two days, with a night at Port Macquarie or Coffs Harbour, or three days with stops on the mid north coast.
Is the Pacific Highway dual carriageway all the way?
Almost all of it now is, which makes the drive quicker and safer than it used to be. Speed limits vary along the road and there are roadworks at times, so check Live Traffic NSW before you leave.
Are there tolls between Sydney and Byron Bay?
The Sydney end has tolled motorways, including the M1 and the Sydney Harbour crossings depending on your start point, so check your route. The visitor options are explained in the toll roads guide.
Where should I stop between Sydney and Byron Bay?
Popular stops are Newcastle, Port Stephens, Port Macquarie, Coffs Harbour, Yamba and Ballina, and the Hunter Valley is a short detour inland.

sydney-to-gold-coast-drive.title: Sydney to the Gold Coast Drive 2026: Pacific Highway Route, Stops, Tolls and Camping
sydney-to-gold-coast-drive.description: Sydney to the Gold Coast is about 840 km and two days on the Pacific Highway. Stops at Newcastle, Port Macquarie and Byron Bay, tolls, the border time change, caravan parks and free camps.
sydney-to-gold-coast-drive.imageAlt: The Pacific Highway running as a divided road through green hills on the New South Wales north coast
sydney-to-gold-coast-drive.intro: Sydney to the Gold Coast is about 840 km up the Pacific Highway, mostly dual carriageway, with a time change at the Queensland border for half the year. It is a long day or an easy two, and the coastal towns and national parks along the way are worth the extra night.

sections.heading: The route and how long it takes
body: The Pacific Highway (M1) is the route all the way: out of Sydney through the Central Coast to Newcastle, north through Taree, Port Macquarie, Coffs Harbour and Grafton, then past Ballina and Byron Bay to the border at Tweed Heads and Coolangatta. The Gold Coast begins just over the border.

Allow two days with a night at Port Macquarie or Coffs Harbour, or three to spend more time on the coast. The Sydney to Byron Bay guide covers the route up to Byron in more detail, and the Brisbane to Sydney guide covers the whole highway.

About 840 km on the Pacific Highway, which is roughly 9.5 to 10 hours of driving. Most people split it over two days, with a night at Port Macquarie or Coffs Harbour.
What is the best route from Sydney to the Gold Coast?
The Pacific Highway (M1) all the way, through Newcastle, Port Macquarie, Coffs Harbour and Byron Bay to the Queensland border at Tweed Heads and Coolangatta.
Do I need to worry about tolls?

Yes, at the Sydney end and into Queensland. Sydney has tolled motorways, and the Gold Coast has the Gateway and Logan Motorways near Brisbane if you take them. The toll roads guide explains how visitors pay.
Is there a time change at the border?
From October to April, New South Wales is on daylight saving and Queensland is not, so Queensland is an hour behind for those months. Check your clock at Tweed Heads.

perth-to-esperance-drive.title: Perth to Esperance Drive 2026: Routes, Stops, Wave Rock and Camping at Cape Le Grand
perth-to-esperance-drive.description: Perth to Esperance is about 720 km and two days by Wagin, Hyden and Ravensthorpe. Route options, fuel, Wave Rock, Cape Le Grand and Lucky Bay, caravan parks and free camps.
perth-to-esperance-drive.imageAlt: White sand and turquoise water at Lucky Bay near Esperance with a kangaroo on the beach
perth-to-esperance-drive.intro: Perth to Esperance is about 720 km south-east across the wheatbelt to the south coast, and it ends at some of the whitest beaches in Australia. The road is sealed and quiet, you can do it in a long day, and a night at Hyden for Wave Rock or Ravensthorpe turns it into an easy two-day drive.

sections.heading: The route and how long it takes
body: The direct route leaves Perth on the Albany Highway and turns off through Williams and Wagin, then takes the Lake Grace and Ravensthorpe roads to the South Coast Highway and east to Esperance. A popular variant goes through Hyden for Wave Rock before joining the highway at Ravensthorpe.

The longer route via Albany and the south coast is about 900 km and takes a day more, and the Perth to Albany guide covers the first half. The other option is to head east through Kalgoorlie and Norseman, about 950 km, which is the road if you are coming from the Nullarbor.
