sections.heading: Fuel and driving
body: Towns are spaced at reasonable intervals, but the gaps on the wheatbelt roads can reach 100 to 150 km. Fill up whenever you pass half a tank, and carry water. The fuel planning guide covers range for a campervan, and the fatigue guide covers rest breaks.
Kangaroos and emus are active at dawn and dusk and the roads are unlit, so avoid driving at those times. Heavy trucks use the highway, so give them room.

sections.heading: Camping around Esperance
body: Esperance has caravan parks in town and at Cape Le Grand and Cape Arid national parks. Lucky Bay and Le Grand Beach campgrounds are the most popular and book out in school holidays, so reserve ahead through the Parks and Wildlife Service. The camping rules guide for Western Australia covers where overnight stays are allowed, and the overnight rest area guide covers the signs.
On the way, Wagin, Lake Grace, Hyden and Ravensthorpe all have caravan parks and free camps, and Wave Rock has a caravan park right beside the rock.

faq: How far is Perth to Esperance by road?
About 720 km by the Albany Highway and the South Coast Highway through Ravensthorpe, or about 950 km via Norseman. The direct route is roughly 8 hours of driving, so most people take two days.
Is there a good place to stop between Perth and Esperance?
Yes. Wagin, Lake Grace, Hyden for Wave Rock and Ravensthorpe are common stops, and Kojonup and Albany make a nice detour if you take the south coast route.
Are there fuel gaps on this drive?
There are towns at reasonable intervals, but gaps of 100 to 150 km are common, so fill up whenever you pass half a tank.
When is the best time to visit Esperance?
Summer and autumn are warm and dry, and the beaches at Cape Le Grand and Lucky Bay are at their best. Spring has wildflowers, and winter is cooler and quieter.

sydney-to-dubbo-drive.title: Sydney to Dubbo Drive 2026: Blue Mountains Route, Stops and Camping
sydney-to-dubbo-drive.description: Sydney to Dubbo is about 390 km and five hours over the Blue Mountains, through Bathurst and Orange. Route, stops, tolls, winter road conditions, caravan parks and free camps.
sydney-to-dubbo-drive.imageAlt: The Great Western Highway crossing the Blue Mountains with eucalypt forest either side
sydney-to-dubbo-drive.intro: Sydney to Dubbo is about 390 km over the Blue Mountains and across the central west, and it is the main road to the Western Plains. It is an easy day, but the Blue Mountains, Bathurst and Orange are worth a stop, and Dubbo's zoo and campground make a comfortable base.

body: The usual route leaves Sydney on the M4 and the Great Western Highway, climbs the Blue Mountains through Katoomba and Lithgow, then runs down to Bathurst, where it joins the Mitchell Highway through Orange and Wellington to Dubbo. It is mostly dual carriageway as far as Lithgow, then a mix of two-lane road and overtaking lanes.
Allow five hours with a break or two, or turn it into a weekend with a night at Katoomba, Bathurst or Orange. The Blue Mountains guide covers the mountains in detail.

faq: How far is Sydney to Dubbo by road?
About 390 km, which is roughly 4.5 to 5 hours of driving. The usual route is the Great Western Highway over the Blue Mountains to Bathurst, then the Mitchell Highway through Orange and Wellington.
Can I drive from Sydney to Dubbo in a day?
Yes, it is an easy day, and stopping at the Blue Mountains, Bathurst or Orange makes it a good one. Many people also stay a night in one of those places.
Is there snow on the Blue Mountains road?
Occasionally in winter, and fog and ice are possible. Check Live Traffic NSW before you leave and carry warm clothes.

Taronga Western Plains Zoo is the main attraction, with a campground and holiday park nearby, and the town is a hub for the Western Plains and the Warrumbungles.

campervan-hire-cost-australia-2026.title: Campervan Hire Cost in Australia 2026: Fees, Excess and Bond
campervan-hire-cost-australia-2026.description: Hire companies show daily rates only after you enter dates. Published costs: cover from $30 to $95 a day, one-way fees of $200 to $300, bonds of $500 to $8,000.
campervan-hire-cost-australia-2026.imageAlt: A four-wheel-drive camper with a pop-top roof parked at a bush campsite in the northern Flinders Ranges, South Australia
campervan-hire-cost-australia-2026.intro: No Australian campervan company in this check publishes a standard daily rate: Maui, Britz, Apollo, Mighty, Cheapa Campa, Travellers Autobarn and Jucy publish no daily rate on their own pages, and Wicked Campers says about $40 a day in low season. What they do publish is the cost on top of the rate: cover that lowers your liability from $30 to $95 a day, one-way fees of $200 or $300, and bonds from $500 to $8,000. The figures below were read on each company's own pages on 21 October 2026.

sections.heading: What each company publishes
body: Cover and bond figures below are for travel from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 where the company dates them. Liability is the most you pay if the van is damaged, which many hire companies call the excess, and a bond or deposit is held on your card against it.

Apollo, Maui, Britz, Mighty and Cheapa Campa belong to the same group and share one Australian FAQ, so their one-way fees, driver age and unsealed-road rules match, though cover and deposits differ by brand. Jucy publishes its rental terms as PDF documents, and the figures in them were not readable from its web pages, so it has no row here.
tips: Rates appear only in each booking engine
Liability and bond are the numbers to compare

sections.heading: Daily rates and seasons
body: The only published figure is Wicked Campers' line that you can get a van for about $40 a day in low season, with no vehicle breakdown and no season dates. Travellers Autobarn says May, June, August and September can generally be seen as low season, and treats the other months as peak. Apollo and Britz publish price years, travel from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 and the year after, not low, shoulder and peak dates.

So a daily rate by van size and season cannot be quoted from the companies' own pages, and an average from a comparison site would not be a rate you can book. Enter the same pick-up and drop-off dates, the same number of sleeping berths and the same cover level at each company, then compare the total, not the daily figure.
tips: Price years run April to March
Longer hires sometimes carry a discount

sections.heading: One-way fees and location fees
body: The Apollo and Maui group FAQ lists a one-way fee of $200 among Cairns, Brisbane, Sydney, Melbourne, Hobart and Adelaide, and $300 for any trip that involves Darwin, Broome, Alice Springs or Perth. From 1 April 2027 these rise to $205 and $310. Other listed charges are $125 for a Hobart pick-up, $900 for a Broome location fee and $125 for a pick-up or drop-off on a public holiday.

Branch dates matter on northern one-way trips. The same FAQ says Broome and Darwin pick-ups are closed from 1 December 2026 to 21 March 2027, with drop-offs closed from 1 December 2026 to 7 March 2027, and Alice Springs is closed from 1 December to 31 March. Promotions sometimes remove the fee on a route: on 21 October 2026 the group listed a deal with no one-way fee on Northern Territory and Cairns departures. Travellers Autobarn and Wicked Campers offer one-way hires but do not publish their fee.
tips: Look at the route, not just the price
Northern branches close in the wet
Deals that waive fees change often

sections.heading: Liability, excess reduction and the bond
body: Without extra cover you pay up to the liability amount if the van is damaged. Apollo and Maui set it at $7,500 per incident, Britz at $7,500 for 2WD and $8,000 for 4WD, and Mighty at $3,500 to $8,000 depending on the van. Travellers Autobarn calls its figure a security bond of $3,500.

Cover removes most or all of that. Apollo and Maui's High Road is from $67 a day, their Value Pack from $77 and Platinum Pack $93. Britz lists $57 to $67 a day for High Road on 2WD vans and $67 on a 4WD, with 4WD cover leaving $750 liability. Mighty's High Road is $42 to $62 a day. Travellers Autobarn's Protection Plus is $30 a day for station wagons and $35 for campervans, and covers two tyres and one front windscreen with the bond at $0.

Read what cover leaves out. Mighty says any breach of the exclusions in the rental agreement voids all cover, and Britz adds a card surcharge to the deposit: 2% on Visa and Mastercard debit, 3.1% on credit and 2.9% on Amex.
tips: Compare liability, not the cover's name

sections.heading: How the bond is held and returned
body: Apollo and Maui debit the deposit to your credit or debit card on the day you collect the van. It is refundable if the van comes back on time, undamaged, clean and with a full tank, a full AdBlue and gas, and the card refund can take up to 14 business days. Travellers Autobarn holds its bond as a pre-authorisation on a Visa or Mastercard for about 14 days and does not take cash cards.

Wicked Campers says it can withhold a bond for a breach such as driving on a prohibited beach, going over the kilometre allowance or returning the van dirty, and refunds can take up to 30 days after drop-off for longer hires. Because the bond sits on your card for weeks after the trip, it also lowers the credit you have for fuel and campsites in the final fortnight.
tips: Return the van clean and full
A held bond lowers your card limit

sections.heading: Extras and fees that add up
body: Apollo's extras page lists camping chairs at $24 each, a table at $33, a fan or heater at $21, an esky at $29, an RV Essentials Kit at $155 or $205, a Linen Exchange Kit at $42 and a child or booster seat at $46. An extra driver is $4 a day, capped at $60, and free with the Value Pack. Cleaning penalties are $299 for each toilet or waste tank returned not empty and $325 for pet cleaning, both including GST.

A 14-day Apollo or Maui hire with High Road cover at $67 a day costs $938 for the cover, then a $200 one-way fee, a $56 extra driver and a $155 kit take that to $1,349 before the daily rate, fuel and campsites. These are the published add-on figures on that route and cover level, not a total price.
tips: GST is included in the group's daily rate

sections.heading: Licence, age and road rules that change the price
body: Apollo and Maui hire standard campers to drivers aged 21 or over with a full licence and need the physical licence, not a photocopy. If it is not in English they need an accredited English translation or an International Driving Permit, or they cannot release the van. Travellers Autobarn accepts a valid international driving licence or a full licence from your country of residence and says a translation may be required.

The roads you may drive on affect your cover. The group FAQ says 2WD campers cannot be driven on unsealed roads, apart from well-maintained access roads under 12 km to a recognised campground or major attraction, and beaches are not permitted. Wicked Campers says 2WD campers can only drive 10 km on unsealed roads and that beaches and off-road tracks are not permitted. Travellers Autobarn says the hirer is liable for damage caused by driving on unsealed roads or on a beach.
tips: Check the unsealed-road limit before a detour

sections.heading: Plan the trip around the hire in AussieCamps
body: AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds and 745 national parks from the state park agencies, plus 5,552 rest areas from road authorities, with each place's facilities, fees and rules as the agency publishes them. You can build a trip with ordered stops, dates, notes and route distance, which helps you check a one-way route against a company's kilometre limit before you book.

Holiday parks and motels listed by BookEasy can be booked in the app, so a trip can mix a hire van's powered nights with national park campgrounds. Place details work offline; map tiles, routing, weather and photos need signal. AussieCamps does not show hire prices, so get those from the rental company.
tips: Get hire quotes from the company

faq: How much does it cost to hire a campervan in Australia?

None of the big hire companies publishes a standard daily rate: Maui, Britz, Apollo, Mighty, Cheapa Campa and Travellers Autobarn quote through their booking engines or by phone. Wicked Campers says you can get a van for about $40 a day in low season. On top of the rate, Apollo and Maui list cover that cuts your liability to $0 from $67 a day and one-way fees of $200 or $300.
Is there a one-way fee for campervan hire in Australia?

Often, yes. The Apollo and Maui group FAQ lists $200 between Cairns, Brisbane, Sydney, Melbourne, Hobart and Adelaide, and $300 for any trip that starts or ends in Darwin, Broome, Alice Springs or Perth. Travellers Autobarn and Wicked Campers do not publish an amount, and promotions sometimes waive the fee, so ask for it in the quote.
How much bond do I need for a campervan in Australia?

It depends on the company and the cover you buy. Travellers Autobarn's standard bond is $3,500, Wicked Campers says its bonds vary from $500 to $2,000, and Apollo's deposit if you buy no cover is $7,500. Bonds are held on a credit or debit card, so check that the card's available balance can cover the bond and your fuel.
Can I hire a campervan in Australia with an overseas licence?

Yes, if you hold a full licence, and it is in English or comes with a translation. Apollo and Maui need the physical licence and an accredited English translation or an International Driving Permit if it is not in English, and Wicked Campers asks for an official translation or an IDP. The overseas licence guide sets out the state rules for visitors.

buying-a-campervan-australia-working-hol.title: Buying a Campervan in Australia on a Working Holiday: Rules 2026
buying-a-campervan-australia-working-hol.description: A visitor can buy and register a van, but the states differ. Queensland wants a Queensland garage address and a seller's safety certificate. 14 days to transfer.
buying-a-campervan-australia-working-hol.imageAlt: A sealed stretch of the Eyre Highway west of Nullarbor Roadhouse, South Australia, with a warning sign for camels, wombats and kangaroos
buying-a-campervan-australia-working-hol.intro: Yes, a working holiday visitor can buy a campervan in Australia, but registration is run by each state, and your address is what decides how easy it is. In New South Wales, Queensland and Western Australia the buyer has 14 days to transfer registration, and in Queensland the seller must hand over a safety certificate. The pages below were read on 21 October 2026, and fees change each 1 July, so confirm each figure with the road authority before you pay.

sections.heading: Rules by state at a glance
body: Registration, inspections and transfers all sit with the state or territory road authority, and the rules differ. The table sets out what each authority says about a buyer's deadline, the inspection or certificate, and the address or identity you need as a visitor.
Where a state leaves a gap, such as roadworthy rules for South Australia, treat it as something to ask the authority, not as a sign that no rule applies.

sections.heading: The address problem for visitors
body: Registration is built around a home address, and a hostel or a friend's couch is not always enough. Queensland's page says that a new customer, or anyone whose vehicle will not be kept at their address, must bring a driver licence, a property rates notice or a gas, phone or electricity bill as evidence of the Queensland address where the vehicle is garaged. Victoria wants an overseas residential or business address and a Victorian garage address, which a letter from a Victorian licence holder over 18 can confirm.

Buying from a licensed dealer is the easier path in some states, because the dealer handles the paperwork. Northern Territory's rules say a dealer can register a vehicle for an interstate or overseas resident. Ask a seller which state the van is registered in before you view it, because a van registered in another state brings that state's inspection and transfer rules.
tips: Ask which state the van is in
A dealer can handle the paperwork

sections.heading: Transfer fees, duty and registration costs
body: The buyer pays the transfer fee and stamp duty. New South Wales charges duty on the purchase price or the market value, whichever is higher. Queensland does the same, using the sale price including GST, and charges light vehicles up to 4.5 tonnes $3 per $100 for 1 to 4 cylinders, $3.50 for 5 to 6 and $4 for 7 or more. A $10,000 four-cylinder van therefore carries $300 in duty. Queensland charges no duty on trailers and caravans, and Western Australia exempts certain caravans from duty but not from the transfer fee.

Running costs follow. Queensland's published cost as at 1 October 2026 for a four-cylinder light vehicle for private use was $385.45 registration, $67.25 traffic improvement fee and $411.80 to $427.80 compulsory third party insurance, a total of $864.50 to $880.50 for 12 months. A campervan's class and engine can change that, so use the Queensland cost calculator for the exact van. In New South Wales a current green slip transfers to the new owner, unless it has expired or the seller cancelled it and claimed a refund.
tips: Duty is on price or market value
Budget for a year of registration
Caravans can be exempt from duty

sections.heading: Check the van before you pay
body: Run a PPSR search on the vehicle identification number. It costs $2 online or $7 by phone, is not refundable, and shows whether a finance company has a security interest in the van. It may also show stolen or written-off records from the state agencies, but that data is not always available or up to date. The PPSR suggests searching twice: when you find the van and again on the day you buy.

In New South Wales a free registration check shows the registration expiry, status, the compulsory third party insurer and its expiry, and the last three odometer readings. Ask for the service history, check any gas fittings against Queensland's gas certificate rule, and have a mechanic inspect the van, because a certificate in the sale is a snapshot, not a guarantee of the van's condition.

sections.heading: Dealer, private sale or buy-back
body: The ACCC says consumer guarantees under the Australian Consumer Law apply to cars sold by licensed dealers, and that most dealers must also provide a state statutory warranty. A private seller has no statutory warranty or cooling-off period, but the ACCC says they must still guarantee clear title and that there is no undisclosed security on the van.

Travellers Autobarn publishes a guaranteed buy-back: its table gives a negotiable price under 3 months, 40% of the purchase price up to 6 months and 30% up to 12 months, with the percentage agreed in writing before you leave, and it asks for a service every 5,000 km. Its page example is a 2010 Falcon bought at $6,000 that returns $3,000 after 12 weeks, $2,400 after 6 months and $1,800 up to 12 months. Another page quotes 40% and says 50% if you sell to another traveller, so get the percentage in writing. No published buy-back terms were found on the Jucy or Hippie Camper pages.

sections.heading: What vans cost
body: Travellers Autobarn's buy or rent page says a converted van averages $8,500 and a HiAce campervan $16,500. The page does not give a date for those averages. Listings on Caravan Camping Sales, seen on 21 October 2026, show how wide the range is at the top. These are asking prices from the seller, not what the vans sold for.
A van with 280,000 km or more is cheap to buy but is more likely to need work, so keep a repair reserve. The working holiday budget guide sets one aside.
tips: Asking prices are not sale prices

sections.heading: When you leave Australia
body: You will need to sell the van or cancel its registration before you go, and the rules differ by state. Queensland refunds the unused registration and compulsory third party premium on cancellation, minus a $22.00 administration fee, and the plates must be surrendered. Western Australia says to return the plates before selling to be considered for a refund of the remaining licence period.
The guide to selling a van before you leave covers notices of sale, plates and timing.

body: AussieCamps cannot check a van's registration or condition, and it does not list vehicles for sale. Once you have the van, it lists 1,838 campgrounds and 745 national parks from the state park agencies, plus 5,552 rest areas from road authorities, with each place's facilities, fees and rules as the agency publishes them.

You can save places as Liked, Starred, Visited or Want to Visit, group them into collections with notes, and build a trip with ordered stops, dates, notes and route distance. Place details work offline; map tiles, routing, weather and photos need signal.
tips: Save places as Want to Visit
Build a trip with route distance

faq: Can a backpacker buy and register a campervan in Australia?

Yes, but each state runs its own registration, so the rules depend on where you buy. Queensland asks new customers for proof of a Queensland address where the vehicle is garaged, Victoria asks overseas residents for an overseas address plus a Victorian garage address, and Northern Territory dealers can register a vehicle for an overseas resident with a copy of the passport.
Do I need a roadworthy certificate to buy a campervan in Australia?

It depends on the state. In Queensland the seller must give you a current safety certificate, and caravans and motorhomes are not exempt from the gas certificate. In Victoria the seller supplies a roadworthy certificate on a private sale, and Western Australia inspects interstate vehicles before licensing them. In New South Wales most light vehicles over 5 years old need an inspection report at renewal.
How long do I have to transfer registration after buying a van?

In New South Wales, Queensland and Western Australia the buyer has 14 days to transfer registration. Late fees can apply, and in Queensland the seller can stay liable for tolls and fines until the transfer is finalised, so do it straight away.
How much does a campervan cost in Australia?

Travellers Autobarn says a converted van averages $8,500 and a HiAce campervan $16,500, but its page does not give a date. Asking prices on Caravan Camping Sales on 21 October 2026 ran from $10,500 for a 1994 HiAce with more than 280,000 km to $159,990 for a 2025 model. Asking prices are not what vans sell for.

selling-a-campervan-australia-before-you.description: Tell the road authority about the sale at once: NSW says immediately, WA within 7 days. Queensland sellers must also supply a safety certificate. Steps by state.
selling-a-campervan-australia-before-you.imageAlt: The entrance to Howqua Valley caravan park at Howqua, Victoria, under tall gum trees
selling-a-campervan-australia-before-you.intro: To sell a campervan before you leave Australia, give the buyer the paperwork your state requires and tell the road authority about the sale straight away. New South Wales says to submit a notice of disposal immediately after the sale, Western Australia requires the seller to notify within 7 days, and a Queensland seller must supply a safety certificate. The pages below were read on 21 October 2026, and each state's authority has the final word.

Whichever state you are in, keep the receipt and a copy of the notice, because they are your proof of the date the van left your name.

sections.heading: Safety certificates in Queensland and Victoria
body: Queensland's seller must give the buyer a current safety certificate or certificate of inspection, and the buyer lodges it with the transfer. The certificate is valid for 2 months or 2,000 km on a private sale and 3 months or 1,000 km on a dealer sale, and it is not needed when you sell to a dealer. A vehicle with gas fittings needs a gas certificate under 3 months old, and caravans and motorhomes are not exempt.

In Victoria a private seller supplies a roadworthy certificate issued no more than 30 days before the sale, and a vehicle that is not registered can be sold without one. Because a certificate can find faults that cost money, book the inspection early enough to fix them before you advertise.
tips: Selling to a dealer needs no Queensland certificate
Gas fittings need their own certificate

sections.heading: Cancel the registration or sell with it
body: If you sell the van with its registration, the buyer pays the transfer fee and duty, and you tell the authority the date the van left your name. Queensland's page says the seller can stay accountable for the buyer's offences until the transfer is finalised, so a late notice keeps you exposed.

If you cancel instead, Queensland refunds the unused registration and the compulsory third party premium, deducts a $22.00 fee and requires the plates to be surrendered. New South Wales cancellation needs the form and plates at a Service NSW centre, and it deducts a cancellation fee. Western Australia says no refund is possible once the vehicle is relicensed in another state.
tips: A refund needs the plates back
Cancelling and selling are separate routes
Check refund fees in your state

sections.heading: Clear the finance and prove the sale
body: A buyer should run a PPSR search, which costs $2 online and shows whether a finance company has a security interest in the van. The ACCC says a private seller must guarantee clear title and that nothing undisclosed is owing, so clear any loan before the sale.

Keep a signed receipt with the buyer's name, the price, the date and the vehicle identification number. In New South Wales also delete the registration from your toll account and update your comprehensive insurance, because the green slip normally moves to the buyer.

sections.heading: Where backpackers sell and how long it takes
body: Travellers Autobarn's selling advice says fellow backpackers are the best buyers and that Gumtree works but needs frequent relisting. It adds that a sale at 60% to 80% of what you paid is pretty good, that keeping at least 3 months of registration on the van helps, and that Sydney, Perth and Melbourne are quietest from April to July, with Darwin and Cairns slow from December to June.

Those are a van dealer's views, not official rules, and no price or timing is guaranteed. If you bought from Travellers Autobarn with its guaranteed buy-back, its page sets the return at 40% of the purchase price up to 6 months and 30% up to 12 months, with the figure agreed in writing, so work out whether the buy-back beats a private sale before you list.
tips: Weigh a buy-back against a private sale

sections.heading: Plan the last trip in AussieCamps
body: AussieCamps cannot list or sell your van. It can help you finish the trip near the city where you plan to sell, because a trip holds ordered stops, dates, notes and route distance, and marks visited progress as you go.

It lists 1,838 campgrounds and 745 national parks from the state park agencies, plus 5,552 rest areas from road authorities, with each place's facilities, fees and rules as the agency publishes them. Place details work offline; map tiles, routing, weather and photos need signal.
tips: Finish near the city where you sell
Route distance for the last leg

faq: Do I need a roadworthy certificate to sell a campervan in Australia?

In Queensland, yes: the seller must give the buyer a current safety certificate unless the sale is to a dealer or the vehicle is exempt. VicRoads says a Victorian private seller supplies a roadworthy certificate issued no more than 30 days before the sale, unless exempt. Check your own state's authority before you list the van.
How long do I have to tell the road authority I sold my van?

New South Wales says to submit a notice of disposal immediately after the sale. Western Australia requires the seller to notify within 7 days, and Victoria, South Australia and the Northern Territory give 14 days. Do it on the day of the sale, because until the transfer is finished the seller can be liable for tolls and fines.
Can I sell my campervan to a buyer in another state?

Yes, but the paperwork changes. Western Australia says to return the plates and sell the vehicle as unlicensed to an interstate buyer, and South Australia needs a paper notice of disposal when the buyer is not from the state. Ask the authority in the state where the van is registered.
When is the best time to sell a van before leaving Australia?

Travellers Autobarn, which buys and sells backpacker vans, says the quietest months in Sydney, Perth and Melbourne are April to July, and that Darwin and Cairns are slow from December to June. It advises leaving enough time to sell and keeping at least 3 months of registration on the van.

working-holiday-road-trip-budget-austral.title: Working Holiday Road Trip Budget in Australia 2026: Cost Per Week
working-holiday-road-trip-budget-austral.description: Two people in a campervan spend about $475 to $775 a week on fuel, food and camping, with fuel $289 at 1,000 km. Costs by camping style, October 2026.
working-holiday-road-trip-budget-austral.imageAlt: The roadhouse and fuel pumps at Nullarbor, South Australia, with a tanker truck and parked vehicles
working-holiday-road-trip-budget-austral.intro: Two people sharing a petrol campervan and driving 1,000 km a week spend about $475 to $775 a week on fuel, groceries and campsites, depending on how they camp, using published prices from October 2026. Fuel is $289 of that at 12 L/100 km and $2.41 a litre, and the vehicle, insurance, eating out and activities come on top. This guide sets the weekly figure out by camping style so you can swap in your own kilometres and nights.

Camping prices come from published tariffs in the camping fees guide and one showground tariff, not from an average of holiday parks, because the big chains show a price only after you enter dates.
Each total is arithmetic on those inputs for one week, so treat it as a starting point and replace the numbers with your own.
tips: Camping is the line you control

sections.heading: Fuel: the line that moves most
body: The government's Fuel Plan page showed average retail prices in the five largest cities on 14 October 2026 of about $2.41 a litre for petrol and $2.80 for diesel. NRMA's weekly report for Sydney on 19 October showed regular unleaded at 239.8 cents and diesel at 280.1 cents. The fuel cost guide's examples use the Australian Institute of Petroleum averages for the week ending 1 November 2026, so use the dated figures here when you compare.
Distance matters more than price. Halving the kilometres halves the bill, and remote roadhouses charge more than the city averages.

sections.heading: Campsites: what the published tariffs say
body: Queensland charges $7.75 per person a night or $31 for a family, Victoria's campgrounds are half price from $16 a site until July 2027, and Western Australia and the Northern Territory charge $10 to $20 per adult, as the camping fees guide sets out. Parks Victoria says the half-price fees were reintroduced on 1 July 2025 for two years.

For holiday parks, Exhibition Park in Canberra publishes a tariff of $40 powered and $35 unpowered a night until 1 November 2026, rising to $45 and $40 from that date. The big chains show a price only after you enter dates, so get a quote for your own route and season.
tips: Parks Victoria half price to July 2027
Powered adds about $5 at one showground
Get chain quotes for your dates

sections.heading: Food
body: The grocery prices guide puts a solo week of core staples at about $85 on Numbeo's community-reported prices for October 2026, which is $170 for two. Eating out adds quickly: the eating out guide shows an inexpensive restaurant meal at $20 to $45 a person in Sydney.
A small campervan fridge limits what you can carry, so budget for restocking every two or three days instead of one big shop.
tips: Eating out is the line that drifts

sections.heading: What the weekly number leaves out
body: The vehicle comes first. A 14-day Apollo or Maui hire with High Road cover, a one-way fee, an extra driver and a kit adds $1,349 before the daily rate, as the hire cost guide works out. If you buy, Queensland's published 12-month registration and compulsory third party cost on 1 October 2026 was $864.50 to $880.50 for a four-cylinder light vehicle, and the buying guide covers transfer duty.

Then add travel insurance, a phone plan, activities and a repair reserve. The campervan budget guide recommends holding money for a tyre, a windscreen or a changed ferry, and a working holiday visa has its own application charge and funds requirement on the Home Affairs website.
tips: Vehicle costs sit outside the week
Check visa costs with Home Affairs

sections.heading: Budget around work stops
body: Home Affairs says that on a working holiday visa you can only work for the same employer for a maximum of 6 months, with exemptions that include plant and animal cultivation work anywhere in Australia and some industries in northern Australia. Plan a break in your budget each time a job ends, because travel between jobs earns nothing.
The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes the national minimum wage and casual loading, and it changes each 1 July, so check its page for the current rate before you plan your weekly income.

sections.heading: Ways to lower the weekly number
body: Drive fewer kilometres, because fuel scales with distance. Use free camps only where the land manager allows camping by sign or standing rule, and read the state rules in the free camping guide. Pair two or three low-cost nights with one serviced night for showers, laundry, water and charging, which the campervan budget guide recommends.
Check each park agency's fee page before you book, because the half-price Victorian fees end in July 2027 and fees can change each 1 July.

sections.heading: Price the nights in AussieCamps
body: AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds and 745 national parks from the state park agencies, plus 5,552 rest areas from road authorities, with each place's facilities, fees and rules as the agency publishes them. You can filter by cost, including free sites, and read reported camping prices on a place page.

Holiday parks and motels listed by BookEasy can be booked in the app with their address, hours and a Book now button. Build a trip with ordered stops, dates, notes and route distance, then use the distance in the fuel formula above. Place details work offline; map tiles, routing, weather and photos need signal.
tips: Use trip route distance for fuel

faq: How much does a working holiday road trip in Australia cost per week?

For two people sharing a petrol campervan and driving 1,000 km a week, about $475 to $775 a week on fuel, groceries and campsites, using published prices from October 2026. That is roughly $240 to $390 each. The vehicle, insurance, eating out, activities and repairs come on top.
How much should I budget for fuel on a campervan road trip?

Multiply the kilometres by the litres per 100 km, divide by 100 and multiply by the price per litre. At 12 L/100 km, 1,000 km is 120 litres, which is $289 at the $2.41 petrol average and $336 at the $2.80 diesel average the government's Fuel Plan page showed for 14 October 2026. Remote roadhouses charge more.
Is free camping the cheapest way to do a working holiday road trip?

It cuts the camping line to $0, but fuel and food stay, and a free camp is only legal where the land manager allows it by sign or standing rule. Many travellers still pay for a night with showers and laundry every few days, so budget for at least one paid night a week.
Do I need to budget for gaps in work on a working holiday visa?

Yes. Home Affairs says you can only work for the same employer for a maximum of 6 months on a working holiday visa, though it lists exemptions such as plant and animal cultivation work. A move between jobs can mean a week or two of unpaid travel, so hold a buffer worth at least a couple of weekly budgets.

campervan-vs-caravan-australia.title: Campervan vs Caravan in Australia 2026: Licence, Towing, Rules
campervan-vs-caravan-australia.description: A car licence covers a campervan up to 4.5 tonnes, while towing a caravan adds brake and mass rules. Compare licence, registration, size and where each suits.
campervan-vs-caravan-australia.imageAlt: A four-wheel drive towing a caravan along the Eyre Highway at Eucla Pass, Western Australia
campervan-vs-caravan-australia.intro: A campervan is one vehicle you drive on a car licence, up to 4.5 tonnes gross vehicle mass, while a caravan needs a tow vehicle and brings brake, mass and mirror rules of its own. For a working holiday that makes a campervan simpler to buy, register and sell, and a caravan better when you stay put and want to drive a car. The rules below were read on 21 October 2026, mostly from New South Wales and Queensland, and other states differ.

Rules marked New South Wales or Queensland are from those states' pages, and other states can differ.

sections.heading: Licence and towing rules
body: New South Wales says a car licence covers vehicles up to 4.5 tonnes gross vehicle mass seating up to 12 people including the driver, so most campervans need no special licence. Towing a caravan on a car licence depends on the combined mass limits of the licence and the tow vehicle. New South Wales learners cannot tow, and P1 car licence holders can tow up to 250 kg unloaded.

Brakes depend on the trailer's gross mass. New South Wales requires none up to 750 kg, brakes on at least one axle from 751 to 2,000 kg and brakes on all wheels from 2,001 to 4,500 kg. Over 2,000 kg a breakaway system is needed, and New South Wales requires one safety chain under 2,500 kg and two crossed chains over 2,500 kg. Western Australia caps unbraked towing at 750 kg or the manufacturer's limit, whichever is lower. Queensland and New South Wales both say extra mirrors may be needed when towing a large trailer.
tips: Check the tow vehicle's rated limit

sections.heading: Registration, inspections and gas
body: A caravan is registered as well as the car that tows it, and a campervan is registered once. New South Wales requires a yearly inspection report for most light vehicles over 5 years old, and this covers trailers and caravans up to 4.5 tonnes ATM, with caravans of a tare under 411 kg exempt. A New South Wales green slip is required to register a vehicle, and trailers and caravans are excluded.

Queensland charges no vehicle registration duty on trailers and caravans, but it does charge light vehicles by cylinder count when ownership transfers. Queensland also requires a gas certificate under 3 months old at transfer for a vehicle with gas fittings, and caravans and motorhomes are not exempt. The buying guide sets out the transfer rules by state.

sections.heading: Size, roads and where you can go
body: Length and width limits apply to both. New South Wales says a vehicle, trailer and load together must not be longer than 19 m, and the load must not make the width exceed 2.5 m. A caravan and car is a long combination for narrow bush roads and town car parks, and a campervan is shorter and easier to turn.

Check a place before you commit. Park agencies publish access notes for each campground, such as 2WD or high-clearance 4WD, so read the page for the site. The Spirit of Tasmania guide sets out the ferry rules for both, and the road trains guide covers sharing the road on long outback legs.

sections.heading: What the usual comparisons say
body: Comparison guides from hire companies and caravan sellers commonly say that a campervan suits couples and people who move often, because packing up means closing the door. They say a caravan suits long stays and families, because it can stay set up while you drive the car, and that a camper trailer suits rougher tracks. These are opinions, not rules, and they come from businesses that sell one or the other.
Fuel use depends on the vehicle, so run the fuel formula for each setup: kilometres times litres per 100 km, divided by 100, times the price per litre.
tips: Run the fuel formula for each

sections.heading: Which suits a working holiday
body: A working holiday usually means buying a vehicle, using it for months and selling it before you fly home. A campervan is one vehicle to check, register and sell. A caravan means a car and a caravan to buy, inspect and sell, plus towing rules that rise with the trailer's mass.

A caravan suits a long fruit-picking or farm placement in one place, where you leave it set up and drive the car to work. A campervan suits a trip with a new camp every few nights. If you will move often, price both setups for the whole trip and include the sale at the end.
tips: Price the whole trip, then the sale

sections.heading: Check each place's vehicle details in AussieCamps
body: AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds and 745 national parks from the state park agencies, plus 5,552 rest areas from road authorities. A place page shows facilities and a Vehicles and RVs section, such as a car park or caravan sites, as the agency publishes it, so you can see what a place says about your setup before you drive there.

You can save places and build a trip with ordered stops, dates, notes and route distance. Place details work offline; map tiles, routing, weather and photos need signal. The app does not tell you a caravan's size limits for a given road, so read the agency's page.
tips: Read the Vehicles and RVs section
Check size limits on the agency page

faq: Is a campervan or a caravan better for a working holiday in Australia?

A campervan is usually simpler: one vehicle to buy, register, insure and sell. A caravan needs a tow vehicle as well, so you buy, check and sell two vehicles, and the towing rules apply. A caravan can stay set up while you drive the car, which suits a long stay in one place.
Can I tow a caravan on a car licence in Australia?

Generally yes, within the limits of your licence and your vehicle. In New South Wales learner drivers cannot tow, and a P1 car licence holder can tow up to 250 kg unloaded. Check the towing limit in the vehicle's handbook and the licence rules of the state where you will drive.
Does a caravan need brakes in Australia?

It depends on its weight. New South Wales requires no brakes up to 750 kg gross trailer mass, brakes on at least one axle from 751 to 2,000 kg, and brakes on all wheels from 2,001 to 4,500 kg, with a breakaway system over 2,000 kg. Western Australia caps unbraked towing at 750 kg or the manufacturer's limit, whichever is lower.
Do I need a special licence to drive a campervan in Australia?

Not for most campervans. A car licence covers a vehicle up to 4.5 tonnes gross vehicle mass seating up to 12 people including the driver, which includes most campervans. A heavier motorhome needs a higher licence class, so check the van's plate.

powered-vs-unpowered-sites-australia.title: Powered vs Unpowered Sites in Australia: Cost and Which to Book
powered-vs-unpowered-sites-australia.description: A powered site adds mains power, such as 15 amp at Discovery Jindabyne, and unpowered sites suit tents and campervans. One tariff shows a $5 gap. Which to book.
powered-vs-unpowered-sites-australia.imageAlt: Caravans and motorhomes parked on red ground at the Eighty Mile Beach caravan park on the north-west coast of Western Australia
powered-vs-unpowered-sites-australia.intro: A powered site has a mains power outlet and an unpowered site does not, and the price gap can be small: Exhibition Park in Canberra charges $5 a night more for power. Book powered when you need the power for a fridge, charging or heat, and unpowered when a battery or solar covers you or the site is in a national park. The pages below were read on 21 October 2026, and each park sets its own site types.

sections.heading: Powered and unpowered at a glance
body: A powered site is a pad with a mains outlet, and some also have water and a sullage point. An unpowered site is a pad or patch of ground with no outlet. Parks describe both in their own words, so read the site page rather than the label.
Examples from Discovery Parks and one showground show how the two compare.

sections.heading: What a powered site gives you
body: Power is the main addition. Discovery Parks' Jindabyne powered site lists 15 amp power, a water supply and a sullage point, and says the site suits a van up to 25 ft total length including the drawbar. Not every powered site lists water or sullage, and the pages for other parks gave no amp rating, so check the site page.

To use the power you need a lead that fits the park's outlet and a van with a mains inlet. Britz says powered sites suit suitably wired motorhomes and campervans, so ask the hire company or the seller whether your van has an inlet and a lead.
tips: Pack the lead and adaptor the park asks for
Not all powered sites have water

sections.heading: What an unpowered site gives you
body: Discovery's Cradle Mountain unpowered sites are gravel pads of about 16 feet, suitable for tents, campervans and small motorhomes, and every site has access to the amenities blocks, dump point and coin-operated laundries. BIG4 says unpowered sites suit caravans, motorhomes, rooftop tents and camper trailers.
Size varies, and one Discovery unpowered gravel site is described as too small to set up a tent or an awning, so check the size before you book.

sections.heading: What the price gap looks like
body: Exhibition Park in Canberra publishes $40 powered and $35 unpowered a night until 1 November 2026, then $45 and $40 from that date. That is a $5 gap, or $35 more for a week of powered nights. It is one showground, not an average of parks, and the big chains show prices only after you enter dates, so compare quotes for the same park and dates.
The camping fees guide covers the per-person and per-site fees for national park campgrounds, which are separate from holiday park site fees.
tips: Compare quotes for the same dates

sections.heading: When powered is worth paying for
body: Power helps most when the fridge is under strain in the heat, when you need to charge devices or run a laptop for work, and when you want a fan or heater without draining the battery. The grocery guide explains why a small campervan fridge loses efficiency in Australian heat.
On a long stay, such as a farm placement near a holiday park, a powered site is usually worth the small gap. On a night when you arrive late and leave early, unpowered is enough.
tips: Charging and remote work need power

sections.heading: Camping unpowered: batteries, solar and generators
body: On an unpowered site you rely on the van's battery, solar or a portable power station. Work out the power you use by listing each device and its hours of use, then size the battery and solar to match, with a margin for cloudy days.

A generator is not the easy fix. Queensland says generators are not permitted in most parks and forests, and New South Wales generally does not permit them unless a sign or the park manager allows it, so the generator guide sets out the rules by state.
tips: List each device and its hours

sections.heading: Check the site type in AussieCamps
body: AussieCamps lists 1,838 campgrounds and 745 national parks from the state park agencies, plus 5,552 rest areas from road authorities, with each place's facilities, fees and rules as the agency publishes them, and you can filter by cost, including free sites. Holiday parks and motels listed by BookEasy show their address, hours and a Book now button.

AussieCamps does not show powered or unpowered site availability, so confirm the site type, amp rating and price with the park before you book. Place details work offline; map tiles, routing, weather and photos need signal.
tips: Confirm site type with the park
Save the park to your trip

faq: What is the difference between a powered and an unpowered site in Australia?

A powered site has a mains power outlet and an unpowered site does not. Discovery Parks lists power on its powered sites, with water and sullage on some, and describes its unpowered sites as suitable for tents, campervans and small motorhomes with access to the park's amenities blocks, dump point and laundry.
How much more does a powered site cost than an unpowered one?

It varies by park. Exhibition Park in Canberra publishes $40 powered and $35 unpowered a night until 1 November 2026, then $45 and $40, a $5 gap. The big holiday park chains show prices only after you enter dates, so compare quotes for the same park and dates.
How many amps is a powered caravan site in Australia?

It depends on the park. Discovery Parks Jindabyne lists 15 amp power on one of its powered sites, and the pages checked for other parks did not state an amp rating. Check the site's own page or ask the park, and use the lead and adaptor it asks for.
Can I use a generator on an unpowered site?

Often not. Queensland says generators are not permitted in most parks and forests, and New South Wales generally does not permit them unless a sign or the park manager allows it. Rules are set campground by campground, so read the sign or the park's page before you pack one.

holiday-park-prices-australia-2026.title: Holiday Park Prices in Australia 2026: Powered, Unpowered and Cabin Costs
holiday-park-prices-australia-2026.description: Published 2026 tariffs show powered sites from $30 to $60 a night, unpowered from $20 to $40 and cabins from $85, with peak seasons higher. Prices and how to save.
holiday-park-prices-australia-2026.imageAlt: Grassed camping area under eucalypts at the Flaxmill Caravan Park in Boyup Brook, Western Australia
holiday-park-prices-australia-2026.intro: In published 2026 council tariffs, a powered site costs $30 to $60 a night for two people, an unpowered site $20 to $40 and a cabin from $85, and the peak season adds roughly $4 to $20 a night to a site. The big chains do not publish a price until you enter your dates, so the council tariffs are the clearest price list there is. The pages below were read on 28 October 2026, and each park sets its own price.

sections.heading: What published tariffs show
body: Four parks that publish a 2026 tariff give a spread of prices across states. The prices are per night for one to two people unless noted, and each park has a peak tier for school holidays and summer.
tips: Peak adds $4 to $20 for a site
Chains show prices after you search

sections.heading: Powered, unpowered and cabin prices
body: A powered site costs $5 to $20 a night more than an unpowered one in these tariffs, and the biggest gap is at Victoria Park Lake in peak season, where powered is $55 against $40 unpowered. Boondooma Dam prices an unpowered site per adult, so two adults pay $36 off-peak, close to the powered rate.

A budget cabin at Ross in Tasmania is $85 off-peak and $99 in peak, and the bigger cabins run $120 to $145. At Boondooma Dam a self-contained lakeside cabin is $135 or $145 for two, with $18 or $22 for each extra adult.

sections.heading: Peak and off-peak
body: Peak is when the park fills: school holidays, long weekends and summer. Ross runs peak from 1 September to 30 April and off-peak from 1 May to 31 August, so the cheap months are the Tasmanian winter. Victoria Park Lake and Boondooma Dam publish a peak and an off-peak tier too.
The chains charge by date instead of by a published tier, so the same site can differ by the week. Search the dates you want, then try the same park a week either side.

sections.heading: The big chains
body: BIG4 lists 312 parks and G'day Parks lists more than 350 across Australia, and Discovery Parks is part of the G'day network. None of the chain home pages read shows a nightly price. They show it after you enter dates, which is why this page leans on council tariffs.
NRMA Parks and Resorts runs a rewards scheme with booking discounts across its parks, from Queensland to Tasmania, and its home page does not list a nightly price either.

sections.heading: How to pay less
body: Choose an unpowered site when a battery or solar covers you, travel in the off-peak tier, and ask about weekly rates, which Ross lists as negotiable. Compare the same dates across a council park and a chain park in the same town.

BIG4 Holiday Perks+ and G'day Rewards each list 10% off a stay, capped at $50 a booking. For a trip with several nights at the same chain, that can pay for the membership, and for one weekend it usually will not.

sections.heading: Plan the budget in AussieCamps
body: AussieCamps carries 1,838 campgrounds from park agencies, and you can filter by cost to see the free and cheaper ones before a holiday park night. Holiday parks, cabins and farm stays listed by BookEasy can be booked in the app, with the price shown when you check dates.

A trip adds up the nights and the driving distance between stops, and every place's details are saved on the phone for use without signal. The map, routing and weather need a connection, and it runs on iPhone only.

faq: How much is a powered site at a holiday park in Australia?

Published council tariffs for 2026 show $40 to $60 a night for two people: Greater Shepparton's Victoria Park Lake is $40 off-peak and $55 in peak, Boondooma Dam in Queensland $50 and $60, and Ross in Tasmania $30 and $40. Big holiday parks are usually dearer, and the chains show prices only after you enter dates.
How much is a cabin at a holiday park?

Council-run cabins in the tariffs read run from $85 a night for a budget cabin at Ross in Tasmania to $135 off-peak and $145 in peak for a lakeside cabin at Boondooma Dam, for up to two people. Chain parks price cabins by the date you search.
Is it cheaper to camp in the off-season?

Yes. Each tariff read charges less off-peak, and the peak tier is $4 to $20 a night higher for a powered site. Peak periods cover school holidays, long weekends and summer, so a midwinter or term-time night costs least.
Do holiday park memberships save money?

On the chains read, a membership takes 10% off, capped at $50 a booking: BIG4 Holiday Perks+ and G'day Rewards both list it. It pays back after a few stays, so compare the fee against the nights you expect to book.

first-two-weeks-working-holiday-australi.title: Your First Two Weeks on a Working Holiday in Australia: Tax File Number, Bank, Phone and First Trip
first-two-weeks-working-holiday-australi.description: Apply for your tax file number, open a bank account, get a phone number and a transport card in week one, then plan a first road trip. A working holiday checklist for 2026.
first-two-weeks-working-holiday-australi.imageAlt: The Sydney Opera House at dusk, seen from the Manly to Circular Quay ferry
first-two-weeks-working-holiday-australi.intro: Do four things in your first week: apply online for a tax file number, open an Australian bank account, get an Australian mobile number and sort out transport. In week two, check your work rights, start looking for a job and plan a first short road trip. The pages below were read on 28 October 2026, and the rules for your visa and country can differ.

sections.heading: The two-week checklist
body: Order matters a little: the phone number and bank account unlock the tax and government accounts, and the tax file number unlocks pay at the right rate.
tips: Keep your passport details to hand

sections.heading: Tax file number
body: You apply for a tax file number online with the ATO once you are in Australia on a visa that lets you work, using your passport number, country of issue, name and date of birth as printed on it. The ATO says the application is free.

Give the number to each employer. If you start work without one, the ATO's tax table says the employer must withhold 45%. Working holiday makers are taxed at 15% on income up to $45,000 in 2026-27, but only when the employer is registered with the ATO as an employer of working holiday makers, and an unregistered employer withholds 30% up to $135,000.

sections.heading: Bank account and phone
body: An Australian account gives you a BSB and account number, which employers need to pay wages and super. Bring your passport and visa details when you open one, and ask the bank which fees apply to your account.
A prepaid SIM or an eSIM gives you the Australian number the ATO app and myGov need, so buy one before you try to link them. Set up myGov early, because it handles sign-in and government mail.
tips: BSB and account number for pay
Set up myGov in week one

sections.heading: Getting around the city
body: Australia has no national transport card. Sydney uses Opal, Melbourne myki, south-east Queensland the go card, Perth SmartRider and Adelaide metroCARD, and contactless bank cards work on many of these networks. The guide to public transport costs compares the fares.
A weekly cap or daily cap limits what you pay in most cities, so tap on and off every trip and let the cap do the work.
tips: Each city has its own card

sections.heading: Work rights and your first job
body: Check your work rights in the Home Affairs VEVO service or the myVEVO app, and note the conditions on your visa. Home Affairs says you can usually work for the same employer for 6 months only, with exemptions that include some farm work and some industries in northern Australia.

Keep a record of your hours and payslips. The Fair Work Ombudsman's Record My Hours app stores them, and visa holders have the same workplace rights as every other employee. Super is paid on top of wages, and you can claim it after you leave Australia.
tips: Super can be claimed on departure

sections.heading: Your first road trip
body: A first trip works best short, with sealed roads and booked nights: a long weekend from your base city teaches you how fuel, camping fees and distances really feel. The guide to buying a campervan covers the choice between buying and hiring, and the working holiday budget guide shows what a longer trip costs.

Learn the rules before you sleep in the van. The guides on sleeping in a car and on rest areas explain where an overnight stop is legal, and a holiday park is the safe default for the first few nights.
tips: Holiday parks for the first nights

sections.heading: Plan the first trip in AussieCamps
body: AussieCamps keeps places of every kind in one app: campgrounds, rest areas, dump points, water points and bookable stays. Build a trip from them with arrival dates, see the driving distance and time for each leg and read the forecast for each stop.
Saved places and trip details open without signal, so a stop's details are still there on a dirt road, and the map, routing, weather and photos need a connection. It runs on iPhone only.

faq: How do I get a tax file number on a working holiday visa?
Apply online with the ATO once you are in Australia, using your passport details. The ATO describes it as free, and visas that carry a no-work condition cannot use the online route.
What happens if I start work before I have a tax file number?
Your employer must withhold tax at 45%, according to the ATO's tax table for working holiday makers. Give your employer the number as soon as you have it.
How much tax do working holiday makers pay in Australia?
15% on income up to $45,000 in 2026-27, but only if the employer is registered with the ATO as an employer of working holiday makers. An unregistered employer withholds 30% up to $135,000.
How long can I work for one employer on a working holiday visa?
Home Affairs says you can usually work for the same employer for 6 months only, with exemptions that include some farm and northern Australia work. Plan a gap between jobs in your budget.

bushfire-safety-camping-australia.title: Bushfire Safety for Campers in Australia 2026-27: Ratings, Warnings and Apps
bushfire-safety-camping-australia.description: What each fire danger rating means for a campsite, the three warning levels, the warning app for every state and when to leave. Checked November 2026.
bushfire-safety-camping-australia.imageAlt: A roadside fire danger rating sign in New South Wales reading Your fire risk today is, with Moderate, High, Extreme and Catastrophic segments
bushfire-safety-camping-australia.intro: Check two things each morning in fire season: the fire danger rating for your district and any warnings near your campsite. On an Extreme day, reconsider staying in bush or grass country; on a Catastrophic day, leave it the night before or early in the morning, because parks may close and help may not reach you. Warnings come from your state's app or website, not from a national one, so install the right app before you drive into the bush. We read each fire service's page on 3 November 2026.

sections.heading: Fire danger ratings: what each level means at a campsite
body: The Australian Fire Danger Rating System uses the same four levels in every state, so the sign outside a country town and the forecast in an app mean the same thing. The rating is a forecast of how a fire would behave if one started that day, not a sign that a fire is burning.

On a Moderate or High day most campsites stay open, but know how you would get out. From Extreme, the official message is to take action now, and the Northern Territory adds that travellers should reconsider travel through bush fire risk areas. Catastrophic means leave.
tips: Same four levels in every state
A rating is a forecast, not a fire

sections.heading: The 2026-27 outlook
body: AFAC's Seasonal Bushfire Outlook for spring 2026, last updated on 19 August 2026, shows increased fire potential in northern and southeastern New South Wales, south-east Queensland, northeastern Tasmania, large parts of the Northern Territory and parts of Victoria, South Australia and Western Australia. Dry soil, below-average rain and heavy fuel loads lie behind it.

AFAC publishes a summer outlook each year, usually in late November. Read it before you lock in a January trip to forest country, and expect total fire bans and park closures to be likelier in the areas it marks.
tips: Spring 2026: higher risk in parts of every state
A summer outlook follows in late November
Check it before booking forest sites

sections.heading: Warning levels: Advice, Watch and Act, Emergency Warning
body: When a fire is burning, the fire service issues a warning at one of three levels, each with an action such as "Leave now" or "Shelter now". The levels can be skipped: a fast fire can start at Watch and Act or Emergency Warning with no Advice first.

Tasmania Fire Service, like every state, uses the Australian Warning System. Read the action in the warning and follow it straight away: when it says it is too late to leave, do not try to drive out through smoke.
tips: Follow the action in the warning
Too late to leave means shelter

sections.heading: Warning apps and websites by state
body: There is no single national bushfire app. Install the app for each state you will camp in and set a watch zone on the campsite, because the app warns you about the places you choose, not only about your location.

Phones also get government alerts. AusAlert, the national system that sends warnings to phones by cell broadcast, says this includes visitors to an area and people roaming on their phone, if the device is compatible. Treat it as a backup: in a valley with no signal, nothing arrives, so check the app before you lose coverage and carry an AM or FM radio for ABC emergency broadcasts.

sections.heading: When parks close
body: Victoria closes parks and forests on Catastrophic days. Parks Victoria says that on a forecast Catastrophic fire danger rating, it and DEECA close parks and forests, including state forests and national parks, for public safety. If you are already there, leave the night before or early in the morning, and do not wait for a sign or a personal warning, which may not come. On 9 January 2026, camping bookings for the closure were cancelled and refunded.

Other states close parks area by area as conditions demand, and a closure can cover campgrounds, picnic areas and walking tracks. Each park agency lists closures and fire bans on the park's alerts page, so check it on the morning you plan to arrive, not only when you book.
tips: Victoria closes parks on Catastrophic days
Check park alerts the same morning

sections.heading: If a fire starts near your campsite
body: Leave early, before the fire is close. Roads near a fire close quickly, smoke cuts visibility to a few metres, and a campground in forest is one of the worst places to be when the front arrives. Drive towards a town or cleared ground, never towards the smoke, and call Triple Zero (000) if you see a fire with no one attending to it.

If you cannot leave, go to a place of last resort. In New South Wales these are Neighbourhood Safer Places, which the NSW Rural Fire Service describes as a place of last resort that does not guarantee your safety; other states keep similar lists. Find the nearest one when you arrive, not when the warning comes.
tips: Leave before the fire is close
Know the nearest place of last resort

sections.heading: Plan around fire season in AussieCamps
body: AussieCamps puts campgrounds, rest areas and holiday parks on one map, so when a forest campground closes for a fire day, you can find a stay in the nearest town or on the coast and save it to your trip. Place details are saved on the phone, so you can still read a campsite's facilities without signal.
The map, routing and weather need a connection, so check them and your state's warning app before you drive out of coverage. AussieCamps runs on iPhone.
tips: Find a town or coast stay fast
Check warnings before you lose coverage

faq: What should campers do on a Catastrophic fire danger day?

Leave bush fire risk areas the day before or early that morning. The national message for Catastrophic is "For your survival, leave bush fire risk areas", and in Victoria, Parks Victoria and DEECA close parks and state forests on days forecast as Catastrophic, cancelling and refunding the camping bookings.
Which app shows bushfire warnings in Australia?

Each state runs its own: Hazards Near Me NSW, VicEmergency, Emergency WA, Alert SA and TasALERT. Queensland posts warnings on the Queensland Fire Department's current incidents map, the ACT on the ESA site and the Northern Territory on SecureNT. Set a watch zone for where you are camping, not only for home.
What is the difference between a fire danger rating and a warning?

A fire danger rating is a forecast of how dangerous a fire would be if one started, from Moderate to Catastrophic. A warning is about a fire that is burning: Advice, Watch and Act or Emergency Warning. A Catastrophic day can have no fire at all, and an Advice warning can come on a Moderate day.
Will an overseas phone get emergency alerts in Australia?

The AusAlert site says alerts reach visitors in the area and people roaming on their phone, as long as the device is compatible. Do not rely on it alone: install the state warning app and check it each morning while you are in fire country.

school-holidays-australia-2027.title: School Holidays 2027 in Australia by State: Dates and Camping Peaks
school-holidays-australia-2027.description: 2027 school holiday dates for every state, the long weekends, and when campgrounds book out: Easter in late March, autumn, winter, spring and summer.
school-holidays-australia-2027.imageAlt: Tents and cars at the Tidal River campground in Wilsons Promontory National Park, Victoria, under Mount Oberon
school-holidays-australia-2027.intro: In 2027, Victoria and Queensland break for autumn from 26 March to 11 April, which takes in Easter on 26 to 29 March, while New South Wales, South Australia, Western Australia and Tasmania break from 10 April to late April. Winter holidays run from 26 June in Victoria and Queensland and from 3 July elsewhere, and spring from 18 or 25 September. Campgrounds near the cities fill first in those weeks, so book as soon as your park agency opens the dates. We read each education department's 2027 calendar on 3 November 2026.

sections.heading: 2027 term dates by state
body: The table gives the last day of each term and the first day of the next for government schools; the holiday is the gap between them. Independent and Catholic schools set their own dates, and pupil-free days can add a day at either end.

Two groups emerge. Victoria and Queensland break a week earlier for autumn, winter and spring. New South Wales, South Australia, Western Australia and Tasmania break together for winter and spring. Queensland ends the year first, on 10 December.
tips: Queensland ends the year on 10 December

table.caption: 2027 government school terms: last day of term, then first day back. From each education department, read 3 November 2026.

Autumn break

sections.heading: The end of the summer break
body: The 2026-27 summer holidays end at different times. Victoria, Queensland and South Australia go back on Wednesday 27 January 2027, Western Australia on Monday 1 February, New South Wales (Eastern division) on Wednesday 3 February and Tasmania on Thursday 4 February. Western division schools in far-west New South Wales return on 10 February.

The last week of January is busy everywhere because of the Australia Day public holiday on Tuesday 26 January. After that, the campgrounds near Melbourne, Brisbane and Adelaide empty first, while the New South Wales and Tasmanian coasts stay busy into February.
tips: NSW and Tasmania stay busy into February

sections.heading: Easter and the autumn break
body: Easter 2027 runs from Good Friday 26 March to Easter Monday 29 March. In Victoria and Queensland it falls at the start of the school holidays, so expect Easter campgrounds to fill and stay busy for two weeks. In the other states Easter falls in term time, and their holidays start on Saturday 10 April.

Anzac Day is Sunday 25 April, and New South Wales, Queensland and Western Australia add a public holiday on Monday 26 April. For New South Wales, South Australia, Western Australia and Tasmania that weekend closes the autumn break, so it is one of the busiest weekends of the year.
tips: Anzac Monday: 26 April in NSW, Qld and WA
Late March to late April is one long peak

sections.heading: Long weekends in 2027
body: Long weekends fill campgrounds within a few hours' drive of the cities, even outside school holidays. March brings Labour Day in Western Australia on Monday 1 March, then a long weekend on Monday 8 March in Victoria (Labour Day), South Australia (Adelaide Cup Day), Tasmania (Eight Hours Day) and the ACT (Canberra Day).

The King's Birthday is Monday 14 June in most states, but Western Australia keeps it on Monday 27 September and Queensland on Monday 4 October. Labour Day in New South Wales, South Australia and the ACT is also Monday 4 October, during the Queensland and Victorian spring holidays. Queensland's Labour Day is Monday 3 May.
tips: 8 March: four long weekends at once
King's Birthday: 14 June in most states
4 October: NSW, SA, ACT and Queensland

sections.heading: Winter: the northern peak
body: Winter school holidays are the busy season in the north, because they fall in the dry season, when the Kimberley, the Top End and outback Queensland are open and warm. Southern families head north in the four weeks from 26 June to 20 July, so book the best-known northern campgrounds as soon as their dates open.

In Western Australia, the park agency limits a stay to 14 nights in any park if a night falls in WA school holidays, against 28 nights at other times, and you must wait 14 days before booking that park again. WA park campsites can be booked up to 180 days before arrival.
tips: WA parks: 14 nights in school holidays

sections.heading: When to book
body: Parks Victoria releases campsites in four batches a year, about six to nine months ahead. Stays from 1 March to 30 June 2027, which take in Labour Day, Easter, Anzac Day and the King's Birthday, were released on 28 September 2026 for Tidal River and 30 September for every other campground, so many holiday dates are already taken. Watch for the next release.

Other park agencies open bookings on a rolling basis. For a holiday week, book on the first day you can, and have a second campground in mind. Weeks outside the school holidays, and towns farther from the capitals, are the easiest to find a site in.
tips: Parks Victoria: four releases a year
Keep a second campground in mind

sections.heading: Plan holiday trips in AussieCamps
body: AussieCamps shows campgrounds, rest areas and holiday parks on one map, so when your first choice is full for the holidays, you can look at the next valley or the next town and save the alternatives to your trip. Holiday parks listed by BookEasy can be booked in the app.
Place details are saved on the phone for use without signal. The map, routing and weather need a connection, and AussieCamps runs on iPhone.
tips: Book holiday parks in the app

faq: When are the Easter school holidays in 2027?

It depends on the state. Victoria and Queensland break from Friday 26 March to Sunday 11 April, so Easter (26 to 29 March) falls at the start of their holidays. New South Wales, South Australia, Western Australia and Tasmania finish term 1 on Friday 9 April, after Easter, and go back between 26 and 29 April.
When do the 2027 winter school holidays start?

Victoria and Queensland finish term 2 on Friday 25 June and return on Monday 12 July. New South Wales, South Australia, Western Australia and Tasmania finish on Friday 2 July and return on 19 or 20 July, so the winter peak runs for about four weeks across the country.
Which 2027 holiday is busiest for camping?

Summer is the longest, but the autumn break is the most crowded on the east coast: Easter falls on 26 to 29 March, inside the Victorian and Queensland holidays, and the other states break from 10 April through the Anzac Day long weekend. For northern Australia, the winter holidays are the peak, because they fall in the dry season.
How far ahead can I book a campsite for the 2027 school holidays?

Parks Victoria releases campsites four times a year, about six to nine months ahead; stays from 1 March to 30 June 2027 were released on 28 and 30 September 2026. WA parks take bookings up to 180 days before arrival. Check the park agency for your state when you know your dates.
